News.title: How brazen scammers are taking over UK homes to make brothels & drug farms…while owners face ‘no help’ from police
News.content:
FOUR years ago, landlord Craig Shepheard welcomed a new tenant claiming to be a courier into a two bedroom flat he owned in Hertfordshire.

The first few months passed by without issue until, suddenly the rent payments stopped.



Then came complaints from neighbours about cannabis use, and reports of men visiting the flat at night.

“The vast majority of my tenants are absolutely lovely,” Craig told BBC Panorama as part of their investigation into criminals taking over homes, set to air tonight.



“I was using a professional lettings agency, and they got this chap in. He had passed all of his tenancy checks.”

When the tenant told Craig the washing machine was broken, he used the opportunity to investigate what had happened to his flat.

Finding sexual paraphernalia inside, he reported to the police that his flat seemed to be being used as a brothel, but was told they needed more evidence to get a search warrant.

Craig turned detective himself and started filming.

“I opened the door, and there was a double bed there with a blonde naked lady, covered in tattoos, fast asleep on the bed,” he said.

“Through into the second bedroom, there was another double bed, and a man and lady asleep on the bed. And she screamed because there was a strange bloke standing at the doorway, and then the first lady came out with her dressing gown and that’s when we started having a conversation.”



Both women, it turned out, had been paying hundreds each week to rent out the room from someone else.

Hertfordshire Police told Craig that they had been part of an organised prostitution ring, run by a network in Brazil, and that they operated pop-up brothels across England.

The lettings agency that had met the tenant and seen proof of identity had been fooled by a high-quality forgery.



Though Craig was able to track down the tenant and get him to give up the flat, he was down four and a half months’ unpaid rent and faced a £4,500 repair bill to make it suitable to rent again.

In the end, the sex workers vanished, and Hertfordshire Police closed the case due to “lack of evidence”.

Similar stories are playing out across the UK, with criminals able to rack up thousands of pounds worth of profit from these illegal operations while facing little to no threat of retribution.

In South London, Monica was faced with a nightmare after renting out her flat to someone who – on paper – seemed perfect.

The so-called accountant passed reference checks with flying colours and had a British passport.



Six months later, the downstairs neighbours rang her up as water was pouring into their from the flat Monica was letting out above them.

“I found out there was a cannabis farm on my property,” Monica said.

“I was absolutely petrified. I had no idea what had happened to the place.”

Police raided the flat and found more than 60 plants with a street value of an estimated £75,000.



The flood had been caused by an issue with the farm’s complex irrigation system.

Inside, the flat was “horrendous”, Monica added.

“They had blackened out all the windows. The actual cannabis smell was unbelievable.

“There’s mold everywhere, due to the humidity. The floors were completely gone.”



A Vietnamese man was arrested but later released without charge, with police suspecting he was a victim of modern slavery.

Monica told BBC Panorama that she received little support from the Metropolitan Police, who told the program they were still investigating.

Worst of all for Monica is that, six months on from the farm being found in her flat, she still did not have it back as the tenancy agreement was still valid.

Housing law requires landlords to go through a lengthy process of serving a notice and applying for a court date in order to secure an eviction.

However, backlogs and delays mean in many cases the entire process can last between six months to a year.



Monica herself applied for a court date in April and has only just had one confirmed for August.

Again, as with Craig’s flat, the tenant had used a fake passport to pass reference and identify checks.

“The use of false identities is growing almost exponentially,” said Simon Miller, who works for fraud prevention database Cifas.



“Fraud in the UK has become endemic. It’s 45 per cent of all crime, and ID fraud is a really significant part of that.”

In order to find out just how easy it is to obtain fake identity documents these days, BBC Panorama journalist Hazel Martin went onto the internet and found it awash with options.

For just £75, she was able to obtain a completely realistic-looking driver’s licence with her photo, but someone else’s details.

Crucially for the fraud to work, the details on it are based on a real person – someone whose name, address, and data have been stolen and are for sale online.

False ID documents based on legitimate details are much more valuable to criminals, as when those details are passed through verification checks, they will show up as real.



Hazel managed to get in touch with the person whose details were being sold online to create false documentation and warn them.

However, when Hazel tried to report the fraud to the City of London Police, who oversee reporting cybercrime, she was told he could not report it as a crime as she was not the victim.

In addition to brothels and cannabis farms, others have their properties illegally rented out on platforms such as AirBnB.



Neha told BBC Panorama how she had begun renting her flat to a tenant claiming to be a data scientist.

However, neighbours soon alerted her that the tenants had been illegally renting their flat out on AirBnB.

She secured an eviction notice, but just days before they got the flat back, the criminal tenants emptied the flat of all its furniture into the back of a van.

When they were finally able to go back round, they found their flat ransacked and the balcony window smashed.

Looking at the other properties the gang had on AirBnB, Neha saw her stolen furniture being used in the listings.



Despite filing four complaints to the Metropolitan Police over identity fraud, criminal damage, and theft, no one has been arrested in the two and a half months since the ordeal.

“We have done all the hard work of gathering all the evidence. But there have been zero repercussions just yet,” said Neha.

“This makes me believe that this is the perfect crime.”



The Metropolitan Police said that they are still investigating the case.

BBC Panorama tracked down the person whose name had been used on the ID documents to rent Neha’s flat – a woman called Poonan Grover, who lived in north London

She looked nothing like the woman on the ID documents, which, it turned out, was an image of a model available online.

It turned out that her details had been used multiple times, and she had even been threatened by debt collectors over unpaid rent that had nothing to do with her.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In reality, Poonan was one of many around the country who are victims of identity fraud.



To date, none of the fraudsters or criminals in the BBC Panorama documentary had been arrested or tried.

News.title: Josh Kerry, 28, charged after Ann Widdecombe found dead with head wound following ‘targeted attack’ at her home
News.content:
Joshua Kerry, 28, has been charged after Ann Widdecombe was found dead in her bungalow with a head wound following a “targeted attack”.

He was arrested in Rotherham, South Yorkshire – nearly 300 miles from the Devon home where the ex-Tory minister, 78, was found.



Kerry was arrested on suspicion of her murder and later re-arrested for the commission, preparation and commission of a terrorist act.

He was charged with one count of murder.



Frank Ferguson, Chief Crown Prosecutor of the CPS Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division said: “We have decided to prosecute Joshua Kerry for murder following a police investigation into the death of Ann Widdecombe in Haytor, Dartmoor.

“Police enquiries into the defendant’s motives are ongoing, including a potential political or terrorist connection.

“Our prosecutors have worked closely with the police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring this case to court, and we will continue working with them as their investigation progresses.”

Forensic searches of his devices led terror cops to take over the probe, as they investigate whether the killing was politically motivated.



But the 28-year-old suspect “was not known” to the Prevent programme, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said.

Kerry has now been charged in connection with the veteran politician’s death, cops confirmed today.



It’s understood Ms Widdecombe’s domestic assistant found the Strictly star at her bungalow in Haytor, Dartmoor, on July 9.

The Reform UK spokeswoman is believed to have been bludgeoned to death in her isolated home at around 12.30pm the day before.

Ms Widdecombe’s final interview was recorded just minutes before she is believed to have been murdered.

CCTV footage obtained by The Sun showed Kerry leaving his home in Rotherham, South Yorks, just before 8am that day.



She had joined a Christian radio station between 11.54am and 12.10pm and defended Nigel Farage over a £5million gift which he says was for security.



Footage shows she recorded the interview in her library, wearing the same outfit as she wore in an appearance on TalkTV at 8am that morning.

Ms Widdecombe was then due to appear on Channel 5’s Matt Allwight show at 1pm – but failed to respond to show producers.

She did not reply to a Zoom link sent half an hour later at 12.48pm, before a producer messaged at 12.55pm asking: “Hi Ann is everything ok?”

During the show, Mr Allwright confirmed Ms Widdecombe had been due to appear but had stopped responding to messages.

Fears were raised for Ms Widdecombe, who was a regular on the panel show, and would typically respond to interview requests quickly.



However, the ex-MP failed to appear having not picked up the phone or joined a virtual link.

Studio staff reportedly made multiple further attempts to contact Ms Widdecombe over the following hours – but to no avail.

Channel 5 said it passed all of the relevant information to police after news of Ms Widdecombe’s death broke.

Presenter Dan Walker later confirmed her agent was contacted and asked to go check on her.

Her body was not found until 11.40am the next day, meaning there was a 24 hour gap in which the 78-year-old could not be contacted.



Cops were thought to be working on the theory she was murdered in a burglary gone wrong.

But counter terror cops later said they believe the murder was a “targeted attack”.

Ms Widdecombe’s home was shown on national television just five days before she was killed.



TV channel Quest aired an episode of Celebrity Yorkshire Auction House featuring the late 78-year-old politician on July 2, TV listings show.

In the episode, the inside of her £600,000 bungalow was shown in extensive detail as she gave host Angus Ashworth a guided tour.

There is no suggestion that visuals of the home on TV inspired or led to the killing.

Cops had initially arrested another man on Friday on suspicion of murder at an address in Newton Abbot, 11 miles away from her house.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But he was quickly released with no further action.



It is believed that her killer was caught on her home CCTV cameras.

News.title: Disturbing twist in ‘16 feral kids’ case as SECOND horror home discovered ‘covered in waste with secret attic’
News.content:
TROUBLING details have emerged about the four adults arrested on child endangerment charges, as it’s revealed the family left a second home in horrific conditions.

The deplorable conditions uncovered at the Siders family‘s home in Hamden, Ohio, may have been the tip of the iceberg, as it has emerged that their previous home about 10 miles away was filled with human feces.



Gary Siders Sr., 73, Christina Siders, 66, Gary Siders II, 36, and Elizabeth Siders, 33, were arrested on June 30 after authorities said they found 16 children, described as almost like “feral animals,” living in a 12-feet-by-12-feet room under their care.

Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson was aghast when explaining the conditions of the home, describing it as “pure evil.”



Vinton County Sheriff Ryan Cain said the children were unable to speak, adding that “our livestock was kept in better conditions.”

Investigators said the Siders family “bounced around” often before settling in Hamden in Vinton County, roughly 80 miles southeast of Columbus.

Records now show the family previously lived at a home in Gallia County, about 10 miles south of Hamden, between 2020 and 2024, according to ABC affiliate WSYX.

Melissa Edmonds lived next to the Siders but couldn’t remember much about the reclusive family or the children.

“We did not know they had even left for quite a while,” Edmonds told the outlet.

“It was kind of just an empty house, I guess, left a message and not really in that great of condition.”



Like most of their neighbors who have spoken out, Edmonds also said she never saw any of Siders II or Elizabeth’s children.

However, Edmonds recalled that her nephew played with some of the children one summer.

“My sister-in-law told me that their kids had talked to them, but they didn’t know them either,” she added.

“They didn’t hang out with him or anything. Possibly in 2021 or summer 2022, somewhere in that area.”

It’s unclear when the Siders departed the home in Gallia County, but property records showed a new owner purchased the property in May.



Bruce Gullick was spotted making renovations at the home and described the vile conditions he found.

“A lot of kids’ clothes in the attic stuffed away like someone was living up there,” Gullick told WSYX.

“The whole entire house was just urine, human and pet feces, so it was pretty tough.”



The children came under the radar of authorities five years before the shocking rescue.

Court records revealed officials launched a truancy case in October 2021 after six of the children failed to attend a single day of school.

The children were enrolled at Addaville Elementary School in Gallia County during the 2021-2022 academic year.



Siders II and Elizabeth were summoned to juvenile court but the case was dismissed in January 2022 after the parents could not be located.

Court records listed the Siders at a mailing address in Cheshire, Ohio, although one month after the truancy case was dismissed, Elizabeth reportedly gave birth at a Gallia County hospital using an address in Chippewa County, Wisconsin.

Property records identified that Wisconsin location as agricultural land with no residential building, while county officials reportedly found no record of calls or visits there.

Elizabeth later used the Cheshire address again when giving birth in November 2022 and once more after delivering twins in January 2024.

In August 2023, deputies responded to a report of a smashed vehicle window at the Cheshire property, but the caller reportedly lived there and was not connected to the Siders family, suggesting they may already have moved away.



Siders Sr., Christina, Siders II, and Elizabeth have all pleaded not guilty to 16 felony counts of child endangerment.

The elder Siders was released from jail after he suffered a medical issue while behind bars.

Prosecutors recommended he be released on recognizance bond due to his serious medical condition.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Christina, Elizabeth, and Siders II are being held on $300,000 bond.

The younger Siders is due in court on Thursday for a hearing on unrelated indecency charges stemming from several incidents in late May.

News.title: Burnham promises to show Trump the ‘best of Manchester’ in G20 visit after Don called new PM’s home city just a ‘town’
News.content:
HALF A WORLD AWAY Burnham promises to show Trump the ‘best of Manchester’ in G20 visit after Don called new PM’s home city just a ‘town’

ANDY Burnham has promised to show Donald Trump “what Manchester had to offer” in a future visit.

The new PM invited the President to come and visit for next year’s G20 summit in one of his first phone calls since taking office.



The G20 summit of world leaders will be held in Manchester next year – a decision made by Keir Starmer while he was still in office.

Trump had previously described Burnham as “a mayor of a town” and had slammed the PM as “extremely liberal”.



The t-shirt-wearing PM said the comment may have ruffled some feathers in Manchester, saying “that won’t have gone down fantastically well”.

Burnham himself has also fired shots at the president, saying in 2017 that he would refuse to meet him as a “matter of principle” after accusing Trump of sharing “hateful extremist material” online.



But the PM has since had to wheel back his remarks, saying that his plan to deal with Trump will be about “being yourself” while also “respecting the office, the UK-US relationship.”

In a call with the US President today, Burnham talked about football, Manchester and the Iran war.

He congratulated Trump on a successful World Cup and the pair agreed that England had an “excellent tournament”.

A Downing Street spokesperson said they had also discussed defence and security, saying that the security of the UK and its allies was “at the top of his agenda”.



Donald Trump then offered an “update on the situation in the Middle East” while the PM highlighted his desire to open up the Strait of Hormuz, according to Downing Street.

Though the leaders started on rocky footing, Trump recently hailed Burnham’s decision to open up two new gas and oil fields in Scotland.

The PM has been tipped to reverse a Labour manifesto pledge and allow new North Sea licences in Rosebank and Jackdaw.



Trump has celebrated the u-turn – after previously clashing with Starmer over the issue.

In a Truth Social post the US president said: “The People of Aberdeen, in Scotland, are dancing in the streets because the new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, has stated that he will be opening up, all the way, the invaluable North Sea Oil!”

The commander-in-chief also said the drilling would be an economic boost for Brits and transform the country from a “poverty stricen disaster” into one of the richest countries in the world.

He added: “Britain pays Norway Billions of Dollars a year to buy its Oil, which they get from a less valuable part of the North Sea.

“How ridiculous is that!”



In a whirlwind of phonecalls since taking office, Andy Burnham has also chatted with Volodymyr Zelensky and European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen.

The Ukrainian president wrote on X: “I was happy to speak with Andy Burnham and congratulate him on taking office as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I truly appreciate that the support for Ukraine and our people will remain steadfast.”

And Ursula von der Leyen hailed a “very good first discussion” and hinted that a UK-EU summit could be on the cards.

News.title: Horror moment tourist plummets 40ft from zipline after safety latch snaps leaving him with broken limbs and nerve damage
News.content:
THIS is the moment a tourist sustained serious injuries after he fell nearly 40ft from a zipline when the ride’s safety lock snapped.

Kuber Surpur, 24, survived the fall but was left with broken arms and legs, as well as severe nerve damage.



The horrific incident unfolded at the Sterling River Resort in the town of Dandeli in southern India on July 3.

The footage shows Surpur gliding along the zipline before his safety lock suddenly snaps and he crashes to the ground within seconds.



His brother, Prashant, captured the terrifying fall on his phone.

Surpur was taken to Dandeli Government Hospital, but his injuries required specialist treatment so he was later moved to a hospital in Miraj for surgery.

Doctors told his family he will need further operations on his arms and legs as part of his recovery.

His family have accused the resort of failing to carry out the required safety checks before allowing the ride to operate.

Surpur’s family claimed the resort “initially provided concrete assurances that they would bear 100 per cent of Kuber’s medical expenses”, but have stopped answering their calls and are no longer addressing concerns over his mounting medical bills.

Insisting the tragedy “could easily have been avoided”, the family has demanded accountability from the resort, including the permanent suspension of its adventure sports licence and legal action against those responsible.



The video has since gone viral, prompting concerns over safety standards at adventure tourism attractions as many demanding stricter inspections of zipline operators.

One social media user wrote: “This is a horrible zipline design. The harness should keep him attached even if he lets go of the rope. How was something like this ever approved?”

Another added: “Let me guess. A small fine, a few weeks’ closure, and the resort will be back in business. No justice.”



Police have launched a criminal case against the operators of Sterling River Resort, alleging negligence that endangered visitors’ lives and safety.

The manager of Sterling River Resort confirmed the incident had taken place but denied any negligence.

Describing the incident as an unfortunate accident, the manager said he planned to travel to Vijayapura to meet Kuber’s family.

Earlier this month several families were left stranded in the sky after multiple gondolas crashed in a horrifying mid-air pile-up.

Stomach-churning footage showed the cabins swinging above the ground as the entire tower shook under their weight.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sixteen people, including four children, said they faced “the greatest fear of their lives” while stranded in the sky.

The gondolas had been travelling across the Volga river in Russia when the cableway system unexpectedly broke down.

News.title: Urgent warning for summer holidaying Brits to brace for 43C heatwave in tourist hotspot Greece – before STORMS strike
News.content:
AN URGENT warning has been issued for holidaying Brits jetting off to Greece this summer as highs of 43C are set to hit the tourist hotspot.

The Mediterranean nation will face its hottest days of the years so far – and visitors from the UK have been urged to travel with caution.



The unprecedented heatwave kicked off on Sunday and is expected to last until Wednesday.

The mercury will soar past 40C in several regions – and experts say locals and tourists may feel this more acutely because of intense sunlight.



In Thessaly, Aitoloakarnania, Phthiotis, Boeotia and the Peloponnese, residents will see temperatures of up to 42C, while in Larissa, highs of 43C are expected.

Holiday hotspots Crete and Rhodes will also record sweltering highs of 41C, authorities predict.

In Athens, it could reach 40C, with most areas around the capital set to see temperatures between 37C and 38C.

In Thessaloniki – where huge wildfires engulfed swathes of land earlier this month – temperatures will reach about 37C.

Doctors have urged people to drink plenty of water, avoid direct sunlight, and wear loose clothing while also avoiding booze if possible.

As a precautionary measure, several Greek cities have opened air-conditioned halls and public spaces for locals and holidaymakers to cool off.



The UK Foreign Office’s website says there is still a “high risk of wildfires” from April to October.

“Ensure that your mobile phone is registered to receive emergency alerts to be warned of wildfires near your location,” it says.

“Wildfires are highly dangerous and unpredictable. The situation can change quickly.”



From Thursday onwards, the weather is expected to become less extreme.

The heat is set to drop dramatically and thunderstorms may follow in the aftermath.

Temperatures will fall by up to 10 degrees in some regions and strong gusts are also expected to follow.



It comes after sprawling wildfires tore through Europe amid a record-breaking heatwave.

More than 19,000 hectares of land were destroyed across Europe amid the sweltering temperatures.

The European Commission helped 14 countries in the worst-affected areas of Cyprus, Greece, Italy, France, Spain and Portugal to fight further blazes.

In Greece, emergency services faced nearly 100 infernos over 48 hours as firestorms wreaked havoc across the country.

The most dangerous blaze was in Mandra, northwest of Athens, where 210 firefighters, 76 vehicles and 29 water-dropping aircraft were deployed.



The area was put under a level-four extreme fire risk warning.

Flames sparked by a forest fire also tore through factories in Thessaloniki in the north of the country over the weekend.

The infernos led to mass evacuations as authorities warned households to keep their windows closed due to “toxic smoke”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A facility housing 157 people with disabilities was also forced to evacuate amid the chaos.

A 76-year-old man was also arrested on suspicion of having started the blaze through negligence by generating sparks with his vehicle.

News.title: Final words of Brit girl, 15, killed by boat propeller on field trip to Maldives as parents sue ‘negligent’ school
News.content:
TRAGIC PLEA Final words of Brit girl, 15, killed by boat propeller on field trip to Maldives as parents sue ‘negligent’ school

A BRITISH schoolgirl pleaded for help shortly before she died after being hit by a boat’s propeller on a school excursion, her grief-stricken family have revealed.

The tragic final words of Jenna Chan, 15, were included in a lawsuit her parents filed on Monday, accusing the school of negligence.



Jenna had been assisting a UK conservation charity to protect whale sharks in the Maldives when she died on November 8 2024.

She had only just entered the water when she was struck by the propeller on the underside of a boat.



The schoolgirl was hauled from under the vessel with the help of her classmates.

In what would be her tragic final words, Jenna briefly regained consciousness to whisper “help me”, CNA reports.

She was pronounced dead less than an hour later at the Dhigurah Health Centre.

Her grief-stricken parents, Jennifer Liauw and Alan Chan, filed a negligence claim against her school, St Joseph’s Institution International Ltd, in the High Court of Singapore.



They have also named the group the school was working with, the Maldives Whale Shark Research Programme (MWSRP), in the claim.

The lawsuit was filed on the day Jenna would have turned 17.

Ms Liauw said: “We did not want to be here.

“For over a year and a half we asked the school to work with us to find out what happened so this can never happen to another child.

“Every door was closed. This claim is about accountability, and about making sure Jenna is the last.”



The claim alleges there had been serious failures in the school’s duty of care and raised broader concerns about safety on overseas school trips.

The boat engine had been engaged when Jenna and other students were in the water, the statement of claim said.

Her parents allege the guides failed to provide proper supervision because they were not nearby when Jenna was struck by the propeller.

The court claim also alleged the boat crew failed to alert appropriate emergency medical services or administer life-saving assistance to Jenna while she was being transferred.

Her parents’ requests for updates on the school’s investigation findings have gone unanswered, the claim alleges.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ms Liauw and Mr Chan have previously accused the school of stonewalling their attempts to find out why their daughter died.

The school’s solicitors, Rajah & Tann Singapore, said in a letter dated November 21 2025, that it did not owe Jenna a “positive non-delegable duty of care” from the risk of harm, the statement of claim said.

News.title: Tragic mum asked pal ‘will you look after my bairns?’ as driver tore through road at 100mph before killing her in crash
News.content:
LAST MOMENTS Tragic mum asked pal ‘will you look after my bairns?’ as driver tore through road at 100mph before killing her in crash

A TERRIFIED mum asked a friend to look after her children as a driver tore through roads at 100mph before killing her in a crash.

Jade Duncan, 41, sent a string of heartbreaking messages as she was driven in a Peugeot 407 Coupe by Sean Hogan.



Hogan, who was banned from the roads, had already clipped a car in Haddington, East Lothian, during the terrifying journey.

Newcastle Crown Court heard Jade then messaged her friend saying he was drunk and was “going to kill her”.



Prosecutor Omar Ahmad said: “Jade Duncan then made a further call to her friend and said ‘he’s f***ing hit a car, we are in a field, he’s doing 100mph, he’s going to kill us. Will you look after my bairns?

“During this time her friend overheard the defendant in the background shouting and repeatedly telling Jade Duncan to ‘shut the f**k up’, to which she responded he had just hit a car.

“Miss Duncan informed her friend they were in Haddington in a field because they had just crashed the car and the defendant was going to kill her.

“At around 8pm the friend received a video call from Miss Duncan, who could see them driving towards another car. She can be heard screaming and the defendant manages to stop just in time.”



The court the video call was the last contact the friend had with Jade before the Peugeot smashed into a roundabout in January.

Jade and Hogan were catapulted 48m through the air in Berwick-upon-Tweed, Northumberland, before the car hit an embankment.

The mum, from Dundee, suffered catastrophic torso injuries and died at the scene.

Hogan, aka Mark Goulding, 46, pleaded guilty to causing death by dangerous driving, causing death by driving while disqualified and causing death by driving while uninsured.

He was today jailed for 13 years and four months with a four year extended licence period.



The court was told he had been given a 16 month jail term, suspended for 12 months with a 15 month road ban, just five days before the fatal crash.

Hogan had also been banned from driving twice before and the Peugeot had failed its last MOT with “dangerous” faults.

Judge Penny Moreland told him: “You showed an utter disregard for the risk of danger to others.

“You have a long history of blatant disregard for the rules of the road.

“Your repeated periods of disqualification lead me to think there will be a risk when you are released from custody.”



The court heard Hogan suffered a life changing brain injury in the crash and remembers nothing about what happened.

He was more than twice the drink-drive limit and spent two months in hospital in a coma.

In a victim impact statement, Jade’s daughter Raychel said: “I want to begin by saying this collision was entirely preventable.

“My family now have to live with the devastating consequences of the aftermath because you Sean Hogan should not have been driving.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I will never forget the moment the police told me what had happened. My world and my family’s world came crashing down.”



Her son Robbie added: “My mam was everything to us. She was the heart of our family, the person who kept us together and the one everyone turned to for help and advice.”

News.title: Andy Burnham Cabinet picks – live: Healey named as Chancellor and Miliband Foreign Secretary
News.content:
David Lammy's resignation letter in full

David Lammy shared his resignation letter on social media following Burnham becoming PM.

In a post shared to X/Twitter, he said: "It has been the greatest privilege of my life, coming from humble beginnings in Tottenham, to serve in government as @Keir_Starmer’s Foreign Secretary, Justice Secretary and Britain’s first Black Deputy Prime Minister.

"I am immensely proud of what we achieved, in Opposition and in Government. As Foreign Secretary and Deputy Prime Minister, I helped rebuild Britain’s relationships with our European allies after the catastrophic Brexit years, stood steadfastly with Ukraine in its darkest hours, championed a new partnership of equals with the Global South and was proud to play a leading role in Britain’s recognition of the State of Palestine.

"I worked to secure the Special Relationship with the United States in a new era and deepened our partnerships with the Gulf and India to deliver trade, growth and security for the British people. As Justice Secretary and Lord Chancellor, I put record investment in our courts to begin stabilising the backlog for victims left waiting too long for justice, put in changes to take our prisons back from the brink to prevent a collapse in prison capacity ever again, put massive investment in the probation service and victims and helped deliver the Hillsborough Law.

"I also put in place a new approach to improving the diversity of our judiciary and made the Ministry of Justice a Whitehall leader in harnessing the potential of artificial intelligence. I would have been proud to continue serving in Cabinet. But a new Prime Minister is entitled to build his own team, and I wish @AndyBurnham and the new Cabinet every success.

"I will continue to serve the great people of Tottenham, support this Labour government from the backbenches and do everything I can to help defeat Reform again at the next general election."

News.title: Ofcom drops legal action against suicide forum linked to death of over 160 Brits
News.content:
Ofcom drops legal action against suicide forum linked to death of over 160 Brits

Ofcom investigators found illegal suicide content on the forum including instructional guides and threads detailing different methods of suicide

View 2 Images The Molly Rose Foundation which works to prevent suicide said online forum had been linked to 164 UK deaths (file photo) (Image: Getty Images)

No further action will be taken against an online suicide forum linked the deaths of more than 160 people in the UK, Ofcom has said.

‌



The watchdog said the forum provider, based in the US, had blocked access from the UK to the harmful content. This was the “the fullest extent of what can be achieved under the Online Safety Act,” Ofcom said.

‌



Speaking today the government body admitted that any further changes to the site “would impact global users, which is beyond UK jurisdiction,” and therefore “all possible legal routes under the Act have now been exhausted”.

‌



As the provider had voluntarily blocked access to UK users, there were no legal grounds to ask a court to “require internet service providers to block UK access to the site,” Ofcom explained.

The Molly Rose Foundation, which advocates for safer online environments and works to prevent suicide said the “nihilistic pro-suicide forum” had been linked to 164 UK deaths.

View 2 Images (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The group said families and survivors had been “left devastated by this incomprehensible decision that means more vulnerable people will continue to be groomed on the site and which will ultimately result in more lost lives”.

The suicide forum, which had been cited in multiple coroners’ in reports into the deaths of UK citizens, was the first target to be investigated by Ofcom under the new UK online safety laws last year.

Ofcom said its investigators found illegal suicide content on the forum including instructional guides and threads detailing different methods of suicides with some of them left up on the site for years.

‌



The forum’s operator was fined £950,000 in May for failing to comply with duties under the Online Safety Act. Ofcom told those behind the forum they had until June 12 to pay up - but the watchdog has still not received payment.

Ofcom confirms investigation into Married At First Sight UK READ MORE :

Sky News slapped with Ofcom complaints over Ann Widdecombe 'spinster' comments READ MORE :

The US-based operator of the site has previously disputed that it falls under UK jurisdiction, raising questions over whether the fine can be enforced. Ofcom previously said it would not identify the forum or its provider because of the nature of the content involved.

A spokesperson for Ofcom said: “The suicide forum’s provider is based in the US, and we have initiated work regarding the pursuit of this debt, as we have done with all companies that have not paid their fines by their deadlines.”

‌



Ofcom said it would review its powers relating to “business disruption measures” – through which the watchdog can apply for a court order requiring internet service providers to block access to a site in the UK.

Ofcom said since being fined, the forum made a further change to its geoblock which addressed an issue whereby registered UK users could still log in without a VPN.

The watchdog said this meant “the vast majority of UK users who do not use a VPN to mask their country location are now no longer able to access the site”.

‌



Ofcom said it recognised that geoblocks “do not fully eliminate all risk of harm, especially for individuals who choose to access sites through VPNs and use them to mask their country location”.

It added it was aware of a “very small number of existing registered users of the forum who, for technical reasons that do not appear linked to the provider’s implementation of the geoblock, are still able to access the site from the UK without using a VPN”.

The watchdog said it would closely monitor the forum to check the “geoblock remains in place”. Ofcom said it did not have the legal powers to apply for a business disruption order for failure to pay a fine alone.

‌



It added that it considered applying for a “conditional order” – essentially a pre-emptive court order that would become effective automatically in the event a site removes its geoblock – but the Act does not provide a mechanism to do so.

A spokesperson for Ofcom said: “While, in a narrow set of circumstances, failure to comply with obligations in the Act can give rise to criminal liability, this is not one of them and we cannot pursue criminal proceedings in this case.

“This means all possible legal routes under the Act have now been exhausted.”

‌



Ofcom said major search engines removed links to the forum following its investigation.

Suzanne Cater, director of enforcement at Ofcom, said: “This nihilistic suicide forum, and the predators who use it to prey on some of the most vulnerable people in our society, have devastated lives and inflicted immeasurable heartbreak.

“We’ve used the powers we’ve been granted to the fullest extent possible, which has resulted in blocking this site for the vast majority of users in the UK.

‌



“We recognise this may not bring closure for bereaved families but it will help protect people in the UK in the future.”

Andy Burrows, chief executive of Molly Rose Foundation, said: “It has taken Ofcom 468 days since launching its investigation to decide not to seek to block a nihilistic, pro-suicide forum responsible for at least 164 deaths, after having to be pushed every step to continue investigating by bereaved families.

“Families and survivors have been left devastated by this incomprehensible decision that means more vulnerable people will continue to be groomed on the site and which will ultimately result in more lost lives.

‌



“Deciding to bury this bad news on the day a new prime minister is announced demonstrates an utter lack of moral courage and shows why bereaved families are right to think Melanie Dawes has no place continuing to lead the internet safety regulator.”

Sarah Ruane, director of policy, practice and influencing at Samaritans, said: “We are extremely disappointed by today’s announcement from Ofcom.

“After months of investigating this suicide forum, and over three years since the Online Safety Act was passed, we are yet to see meaningful action against some of the most harmful sites online.

‌



“Online platforms must know that any breach of the act will be heavily punished and this is a missed opportunity to hammer that message home.

“All today’s announcement does is raise serious questions about whether the Online Safety Act is fit for purpose.

“Under the new PM’s leadership, we need to see a strong commitment to ensuring Ofcom has the powers it needs to take decisive action.”

Article continues below

David Parfett, of Families and Survivors to Prevent Online Suicide Harms, said: “We continue to see suicides where victims have found information on methods online, and often have been encouraged to self-harm.

“This continues what we’ve seen for years; vulnerable people being able to easily find information and communities online which would be illegal in the real-world.

“The Online Safety Act in Ofcom’s hands is not working and that’s starkly measured in continued avoidable loss of life.”

News.title: Ann Widdecombe suspect Joshua Kerry charged with murdering ex-Tory MP
News.content:
Ann Widdecombe suspect Joshua Kerry charged with murdering ex-Tory MP

Joshua Kerry, 28, was originally detained on suspicion of Ann Widdecombe's murder, before being re-arrested two days later on suspicion of commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism

View 9 Images Joshua Kerry has been charged with murder

A man has tonight been charged with the murder of former Tory minister Ann Widdecombe.

Joshua Kerry, 28, from Rotherham, South Yorkshire, is set to appear in Westminster Magistrates Court on Tuesday accused of attacking the Conservative turned Reform UK spokeswoman in her Devon home.

Frank Ferguson, Chief Crown Prosecutor of the CPS Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division said: “We have decided to prosecute Joshua Kerry for murder following a police investigation into the death of Ann Widdecombe in Haytor, Dartmoor.

“Police enquiries into the defendant's motives are ongoing, including a potential political or terrorist connection.

“Our prosecutors have worked closely with the police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring this case to court, and we will continue working with them as their investigation progresses."

Kerry was originally arrested on suspicion of murder on Saturday, July 11, before being re-arrested two days later on suspicion of commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism.

View 9 Images Ann Widdecombe was killed last week (Image: Steve Taylor/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

Ms Widdecombe was killed in her house on Wednesday July 8, 30 minutes before she was set to appear via video call from home, on Channel 5's Matt Allwright show. The 78-year-old had last messaged a producer at 12.19pm but failed to respond to a text at 12.48pm.

Devon and Cornwall Police believed she died at 12.30pm in the bungalow where she lived alone with her cat on the edge of Dartmoor National Park. Her body remained undiscovered for almost 24 hours before being found in the kitchen of the house at 11.40am the next day.

An inquest will be opened into the death of Ms Widdecombe's on Tuesday morning.

View 9 Images Ann Widdecombe was found dead inside her home (Image: Getty Images)

Kerry is understood to have been unemployed since working as an office administrator up until two years ago.

Ms Widdecombe was first elected a Conservative MP in Kent in 1987, then served as an MEP for the Brexit Party and spokeswoman for Reform UK. She also starred in Strictly Come Dancing and Celebrity Big Brother. Prime Minister Keir Starmer said he had spoken to his successor Andy Burnham, Tory leader Kemi Badenoch and Reform UK's Mr Farage to "urge everybody to come together at a moment like this".

View 9 Images Police were at the suspect's home from Sunday (Image: Iconic Media Group / SWNS)

View 9 Images A mid-terrace home was under police cordon following an arrest at about 9pm on Saturday, July 11 (Image: Tom Maddick / SWNS)

Paying tribute to Ms Widdecombe, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said on Tuesday: "Ann Widdecombe dedicated her life to politics and public service. For nearly 40 years, she was a fixture of our political life. She brought conviction to our politics, grounded in her profound Catholic faith. She was forthright in her opinions and argued courageously for the things she believed in. But, perhaps most of all, she brought an inimitable style to politics. She was forthright and fearless."

The Home Secretary added: "She was one of those rare politicians who was bigger than politics."

9 View 9 Images The scene at a Rotherham address on Sunday (Image: Iconic Media Group / SWNS) 9 View 9 Images Officers were spotted searching bins and leaving the house with boltcutters (Image: Iconic Media Group / SWNS)

House of Commons Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle also paid tribute to Ms Widdecombe in the chamber and urged MPs not to say anything that might prejudice a future trial. He said: "Ann was a formidable politician, a prominent figure in public life. She was a member of Parliament for Maidstone for 23 years, holding a number of ministerial posts in the 1990s.

"Ann was fierce and enjoyed robust political debate. Whether you agreed with her or not, she was principled, spoke her mind and was true to her beliefs, informed by a Christian faith. On a personal level, Casa Pizza in Lambeth is where I spent a lot of time in the evening sharing a pizza with the one and only Ann Widdecombe. She was a friend in many ways. Politically we may not agree, but she was without doubt a courageous, principled politician and all our thoughts are with her family and her friends."

View 9 Images Ann was formerly a Conservative minister, and later a Reform spokesperson (Image: Christopher Jones/Shutterstock)

‌



Sir Lindsay has previously spoken about his fears for MPs following the killings of Labour MP Jo Cox in 2016 and Conservative David Amess in 2021. He added: "Ann was a close friend to David Amess and both were animal lovers."

View 9 Images Ann Widdecombe was allegedly killed in a "targeted attack", police said (Image: Christopher Jones/Shutterstock)

Counter Terrorism Policing took over the investigation into Ms Widdecombe's death after Devon and Cornwall Police initially said there was "nothing to suggest" the murder had been politically motivated.

Article continues below

Terrorism laws allow a suspect to be held for up to seven days in the first instance, with investigators permitted to apply for time extensions up to 14 days in total.

News.title: DARREN LEWIS: 'Burnham must get Black voters back on track'
News.content:
So just what is Andy Burnham going to do about Labour’s Black MP problem? Miatta Fahnbulleh is a start. She’s a key adviser to Burnham and has a wealth of experience developing and delivering policy to empower communities. We also know that she has worked hard to come up with new ideas to reshaping our economy inside government and out. But who else?

Glance at any of the selfies the UK’s new PM takes and the numbers of Black MPs in particular behind him are embarrassing. David Lammy has long since lost the confidence of his Tottenham constituency, near where I live in North London.

Dylan Law, the Green Party’s deputy mayor in Hackney Downs where I grew up, is the kind of fresh energy people want to get behind. Burnham talks a terrific game in his bid to fend off the rise of the Greens. But Zack Polanski’s disruptors champion Black political talent.

View 3 Images David Lammy at the the House of Commons (Image: House of Commons/UK Parliament/PA Wire)

‌



Where will it be in this next Labour cabinet? Who is the next male cab off the rank to speak to the issues affecting millions of Black and Brown men and boys in this country?

Who will be their advocate around the table to address their over-representation in the criminal justice system, their high exclusion rates from school increasing their vulnerability to exploitation, their mental health disparities and stop and search?

Who is the female MP to fight for the Black women affected by the racism and discrimination endemic in NHS maternity care, leading to Black mothers being nearly three times as likely to die during childbirth compared to white women?

Who is the Black female Cabinet candidate to end the perception that Labour’s “regard” for Black voters is largely performative, per the treatment of Diane Abbott and Kate Osamor, under the regime of Sir Keir Starmer?

‌



Just a couple of months ago, Eunice O’Dame and Enid Mollyneux – two long-serving Black women councillors – were blocked by Labour from standing in one of its safest wards in Croydon, Bensham Manor. The seat was instead contested by Starmer’s niece, Ellie Sandover.

View 3 Images Dylan Law, the Green Party’s deputy mayor in Hackney Downs, is the kind of fresh energy people want to get behind (Image: Getty Images)

Nobody doubts Ellie’s ability to do the job and this is most certainly not about her as an individual. It is about Labour and their inability to read the room regarding Black candidates.

This is far from the first time this column has raised this issue. Labour simply cannot take our votes for granted. The UK is at its most febrile in terms of race relations since the vile Seventies and Eighties, with poisonous racism spouted unashamedly.

‌



The Windrush scandal continues to see the state waiting for claimants to die rather that meet its responsibilities. More fool us for believing things would change in that regard with the Tories out of power.

Then there’s the ongoing hostile environment, the empowerment and appeasement of those rejecting anti-racism and so much more. Burnham has a golden opportunity, to do better than Starmer whose government pretty much abandoned Black Britain.

Young, clued-up people want visionaries who looks like them, speak truth to power and understand their lives. A Dylan Law would probably never have made it on to a Labour shortlist, based on the patterns of many years.

And if Burnham wants to change his Cabinet, he needs to do better than Shabana Mahmood, who defended Starmer’s Island Of Strangers remarks.

‌



A woman who threw people of colour under the bus with her immigration policies and rhetoric. A woman whose left-wing principles disintegrated once she gained a whiff of high office. Us Black voters are waiting. Can Burnham rise to the challenge?

News.title: Organised crime cops help catch 1,393 'paedophiles and sex abusers'
News.content:
Organised crime cops help catch 1,393 'paedophiles and sex abusers'

Regional organised crime units who normally investigate gangland kingpins have been deployed on paedophiles and domestic abusers arresting 1,393 and safeguarding 1,351 children

View 3 Images Rhys Meikle, 31, was jailed for four years for a sex offence (Image: North West Regional Organised Crime Unit)

Specialist police fighting organised crime have helped catch more than one thousand suspected sexual predators, it has been revealed today.

‌



Tactics normally used to nail gangland kingpins have been deployed on paedophiles and domestic abusers leading to 1,393 arrests, safeguarding 1,351 children and securing 1,487 years of jail time.

‌



Regional organised crime units (ROCUs) continue to tackle drug dealers, serious violence, money laundering and firearms offending, but have become increasingly focused on protecting the most vulnerable people in society.

‌



Among those jailed were Declan Sains, 28, after talking online to an undercover police officer who he thought was a 14-year-old boy online.

Sains pleaded guilty to engaging in sexual communication with a child, making indecent images of children and inciting a boy to engage in sexual activity. He was sentenced to eight years and three months in prison at Teesside Crown Court.

Man planned to abuse young girl with her dad before police arrived at his home READ MORE :

View 3 Images Declan Sains, 28, was jailed for child sex offences (Image: NEROCU)

‌



Rhys Meikle, 31, was jailed last month for four years at Manchester Crown Court after he pleaded guilty to arranging or facilitating the commission of child sexual offences and making; and distributing indecent images of children.

Chief Constable Trevor Rodenhurst, the National Police Chiefs’ Council lead for ROCUs, said: "Organised crime continues to evolve rapidly, with offenders increasingly exploiting digital platforms and targeting vulnerable individuals in new ways. ROCUs are adapting alongside those threats, developing specialist skills, technology and intelligence capabilities to ensure communities remain protected.

"The ROCU network has evolved significantly since its creation and now plays a crucial role in tackling some of the most harmful threats facing our communities.

‌



"From disrupting organised crime groups involved in drugs and firearms, to protecting children from online predators, supporting victims of abuse and identifying hidden exploitation, our officers and staff are making a tangible difference every day.

"Organised crime is becoming increasingly complex, and ROCUs are needed more than ever."

View 3 Images Heroin seized by ROCU officers (Image: ROCU/West Midlands Police)

‌



'It is vital we recognise exploitation'

Deputy Chief constable Wendy Gunney, the NPCC lead for national SOC, added: "Today, vulnerability is a theme we recognise and see running throughout so many of our investigations because organised criminals are experts in exploitation and coercion. It’s vital that our officers recognise this and not only pursue dangerous offenders but identify and safeguard victims.

“The ROCU network has demonstrated that the tactics and capabilities they use to tackle SOC are highly effective and are confident they will greatly assist in the fight against violence against women and girls and online exploitation.”

Since their inception in 2013, ROCUs have grown into a national network of around 4,000 officers and staff.

Article continues below

Working alongside the National Crime Agency (NCA), officers are using advanced investigative methods to support local forces .

Over the past year, ROCUs have arrested 4,363 suspects, secured 7,242 years of prison sentences, protected 2,259 children and 823 adults and made 1,492 drug and firearms arrests.

The units have seized 95 firearms and 652 rounds of ammunition along with more than 1.5 tonnes of cocaine, 158 kg of heroin and 8.4 tonnes of cannabis.

News.title: Burnham's wife Marie-France van Heel was 'coolest girl in college' - but Downing Street walk was wildly out of her comfort zone
News.content:
Outside Downing Street, as the new Prime Minister made his way through the crowds, shaking hands and hugging supporters, one of the most important political figures in Andy Burnham’s life was missing – and one woman hung on longest, almost refusing to let him go.

Burnham’s dad Roy, an engineer who taught him as a child about how Margaret Thatcher had decimated Liverpool, was not there at the most important moment of his son’s life because he has dementia. Speaking movingly about Roy, Burnham has said that because of his illness, his dad won’t know that his son has become Prime Minister. But he added: “It’s a family achievement … although he doesn’t know it, it still makes me feel that we’ve kind of done something together.”

Outside that famous black front door, Eileen Burnham’s arms were wrapped firmly around her son, hugging him as if the rest of the world wasn’t there. For Andy Burnham’s wife Marie-France Van Heel, however, the whole event will have been wildly out of her comfort zone – however immensely proud she is of the husband she met back when she was known as “the coolest girl in Fitzwilliam College”.

Marie-France – who Burnham calls Frankie – is not going to be a classic political wife. A highly intelligent, warm, stylish, funny woman who speaks three languages, she has always kept herself separate from his job as Mayor of Greater Manchester. She didn’t join him on stage after his victory speech as new Labour leader, and stood back in Makerfield, hidden behind oversized sunglasses. And – unless she undergoes a personality and morality transplant – she will not be ordering £2,260 of ‘gold wallpaper’ from Lulu Lytle or any and £500 table cloths any time soon – not least because she may not actually live very much in the goldfish bowl of Downing Street at all.

‌



View 3 Images Prime Minister Andy Burnham with wife Marie-France van Heel arrive at 10 Downing Street today (Image: Simon Dawson / No 10 Downing Street)

Marie-France has the kind of perspective on life that only deep family tragedy and facing a potential cancer diagnosis can bring. Her sister Claire died of breast cancer at the age of just 39. In 2010, Marie-France underwent a double mastectomy – after a genetic test showed she could be at risk of the same disease.

The Burnhams’ experience of the NHS during Claire’s illness and Marie-France’s mastectomy – which came as Andy fought a leadership election – shaped how the Prime Minister sees the NHS. While his gran’s – and now his dad’s – experience of social care, has shaped his ambition for a ‘National Care Service’. His cleaner grandma, Kitty Murray, died in 2002 after having spent her £35,000 life savings on care – and ending up in a home where her wedding ring was stolen. Mum Eileen told him then: “If you get elected, bloody well do something!”

Born in January 1970, Marie-France van Heel grew up in the Netherlands and Belgium before moving to the UK and going to Cambridge University, and works in marketing and strategy. She is the chief marketing officer at Iduna Infrastructure, a firm which owns large parts of Manchester’s electric vehicle charging network – meaning her husband had to exempt himself from EV network decisions while Mayor.

‌



Since her sister’s death, Marie-France has taken part in Cancer Research UK’s Race for Life many times, and has many other charitable interests. As well as having been involved with charities from Marie Curie, Great Ormond Street, and The Alzheimer’s Society, she is on the board of trustees for Plan International UK.

When the couple were first dating, in 1992 – having agreed it with her future husband – Van Heel appeared on an episode of Blind Date where she chose ‘Will from Surrey’ to be her date on a holiday to Gibraltar. It’s fair to say they did not hit it off – perhaps unsurprisingly given Will from Surrey went on to work for the Conservative Party. Burnham has said he watched the programme from behind the sofa.

View 3 Images Britain's new Prime Minister Andy Burnham delivers his first speech outside 10 Downing Street today (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

When Andy Burnham was running for Labour leader in 2015, the Cambridge English graduate spoke at a literary event about one of his favourite short stories – the Election for Beadle by Charles Dickens, which pokes fun at corrupt parish elections. One member of the audience seemed determined to heckle him. After shouting out “don’t embarrass me”, when Burnham was asked if he himself wrote poetry (he admitted he did), the same woman raised her hand during the Q&A afterwards.

‌



“You’re not allowed to ask a question,” Burnham joked. Marie-France replied: “I was just going to ask when you’re next home?”

Her home now is at least theoretically Downing Street. One issue with taking up residence, may be her beloved rescue dog Axel, who something of a handful, and may not cohabit well with Larry the Cat. However they choose to run their lives as Prime Minister and ‘First Lady’, one thing the Burnhams do exceptionally well, is ‘human’ – which in an era when politics could not have grown more distant from the people, is more important than it sounds.

It’s easy to imagine that moments after that important speech outside, as her husband awaited the parade of shadow cabinet hopefuls, Marie-France was back at her laptop on a zoom call, while Eileen put some bacon for one of her favourite butties. In 2015, Eileen, a former GP receptionist, whose dad drove a lorry for Tate & Lyle, and used to cry watching Boys from the Blackstuff, told the Daily Mirror why her son would make a good Prime Minister.

“He will change things, because he really cares,” Evertonian Eileen said. “When I hear people talking rubbish about him I get upset. They just don’t know our Andy.”

News.title: Andrew and Tristan Tate's lawyer vows to fight extradition to UK on rape charges
News.content:
Andrew and Tristan Tate's lawyer vows to fight extradition to UK on rape charges

Joe McBride, the lawyer for Andrew and Tristan Tate has said he will fight their extradition to the UK adding that Britain was 'a fallen state that prosecutes its citizens for free speech'

View 4 Images Andrew Tate (L) and his brother Tristan Tate (file photo) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Andrew and Tristan Tate’s lawyer has said they will fight their extradition to the UK to face rape and sex trafficking charges, saying the brothers are victims of a “political witch hunt”.

Lawyer Joe McBride said Britain was “a fallen state that prosecutes its citizens for free speech” in a statement to the press outside a Miami courthouse.

He added that his clients were being “attacked for what they say, not what they’ve done”.

He appeared to reference the case of a woman being arrested for praying outside an abortion clinic, while also claiming political activist Tommy Robinson had been targeted “simply for exercising his free speech rights”.

Mr McBride seemed to call for US President Donald Trump to intervene in the extradition, saying: “he was elected to fight against this kind of nonsense”.

Andrew Tate and brother Tristan arrested with 38 new sexual offence charges READ MORE :

Andrew Tate challenges court's decision to withhold names of rape accusers READ MORE :

View 4 Images Joseph McBride, lead counsel for Andrew and Tristan Tate, speaks to reporters in Miami, Florida (Image: Getty Images)

The brothers, who are dual US and UK citizens, were arrested by US marshals at the weekend and are set to appear in court on Monday.

The pair were taken into custody after more charges were brought against them by the British authorities.

Andrew Tate, 39, was charged with seven further counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and 19 additional charges for offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

Tristan Tate, 38, was charged with one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation.

View 4 Images Andrew Tate (R) and his brother Tristan (L) were arrested by US Marshals in Florida (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said the 38 additional charges, in addition to 21 existing charges, relate to alleged offences between July 2010 and August 2017. The brothers have previously denied any wrongdoing.

Mr McBride said: “We of course are going to fight extradition.”

Describing the further charges as “salacious and defamatory”, he said: “Some of them are despicable, meritless, heinous and atrocious. They’re designed to poison the jury pool, to re-poison public consciousness.”

Mr McBride added: “We’ve never seen a scintilla of evidence that indicates that these guys are guilty of anything. They’re being punished and attacked for what they say, not what they’ve done.

View 4 Images Lawyer Joseph McBride labelled the arrest a 'political witch hunt' (Image: Getty Images)

“You can love them, you can hate them, but nobody should go to jail for free speech, and that is exactly what this is about. Make no mistake about it, the United Kingdom was once the greatest empire the world has ever known. It is a fallen nation. It is a fallen state that prosecutes its citizens for free speech.”

He went on: “That is not what democracies and free societies do. That is what communist China and despotic regimes do. And we’re going to fight them at every turn, at every corner, because they are American citizens.”

Mr McBride argued US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and others in the administration “are not fans of communism”. He said: “They’re not fans of prosecuting people for free speech. This is one of the reasons why they’ve been elected.

“So I would just think, as a matter of principle, based on the reasons why they were elected, that they would not want to see two free citizens go to a country where they’re going to be thrown in jail for political reasons.”

He added: “I can’t comment directly on what my president is going to do. All I can say is he was elected to fight against this kind of nonsense, and I can’t see him looking at this with an objective lens and agreeing to a political witch hunt and a political kidnapping.”

Article continues below

Mr McBride expected the legal proceedings process to take around 60 days. He said: “Could be a little longer. It could be a little shorter, depending on how it shakes out for us. But I think for the foreseeable future, we’re in this for the next two months.”

News.title: Mum's 'immense surprise' as she gives birth to 'unheard of' identical quadruplets
News.content:
Mum's 'immense surprise' as she gives birth to 'unheard of' identical quadruplets

Jenitar and Jortham Na-amoana have welcomed identical quadruplets - Emily, Harriet, Alexa and Catherine - who have been born at the Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital

View 4 Images A woman has given birth to identical quadruplets (Image: Go Fund Me)

A mum has given birth to "unheard of" identical quadruplets in Australia.

‌



Jenitar and dad Jortham Na-amoana welcomed four baby girls, Emily, Harriet, Alexa and Catherine, at the Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital.

‌



They were naturally conceived and monozygotic quadruplets - where a single fertilised egg splits into four embryos.

‌



The four girls were delivered via caesarean section at 28 weeks and four days on 14 July with the chances of naturally conceiving quadruplets estimated to be around one in 15 million.

The couple have now doubled their number of offspring, as they already had four children aged between 10 and one.

View 4 Images Jenitar now has eight children in total (Image: Go Fund Me)

‌



UK airline issues ‘urgent’ plea as key flights cancelled READ MORE :

UK weather maps turn volcanic red for next 31C heatwave with 19 counties above 30C READ MORE :

Dr Alexa Bendall, after whom one of the babies was named, helped care for Mrs Na-amoana during her pregnancy.

"Jenitar has taken everything in her stride from day one – we have never seen a spontaneously conceived pregnancy of this type with quads, and she has somehow dodged every complication and risk for both herself and her babies to be here today, with four gorgeous newborn girls," she said.

“Monozygotic quadruplets are estimated at one in every 15 million pregnancies, but to share the same placenta, this is unheard of.”

‌



View 4 Images Identical quadruplets are extremely rare (Image: Go Fund Me)

The hospital said that Jenitar and Jortham were taken by "immense surprise" when told to expect quadruplets, reported news.com.au.

And Dr Bendall, who is a maternal foetal medicine specialist and obstetrician, had warned that having monozygotic quadruplets is very high risk with the hospital admitting Na'amoana as a patient at 25 weeks so she could be monitored.

‌



“We always said that if we could get her to 28 weeks, we would be doing well, so we are happy she could make it to this gestation,” Dr Bendall reportedly said “The rare quadruplets will now spend time in our specialist neonatal intensive care unit where they will grow to full term and are currently doing well.”

The plan now is for the babies to stay in the hospital's neonatal intensive care unit until they grow to full term.

View 4 Images The family are now trying to raise money to help pay for the childcare costs (Image: Go Fund Me)

‌



The couple have now set up a GoFundMe page to help them with the costs of bringing up four extra kids. A message on the page read: "Hi, my name is Jenitar Na’amoana, and I’m a mum of eight beautiful children, including our naturally conceived identical quadruplet girls—one of the rarest births in the world.

"Our four precious miracles have arrived safely, and while our hearts are overflowing with gratitude, the reality of caring for four newborns at once has brought challenges we never could have imagined. We urgently need a larger van with at least 10 or 12 seats, essential baby equipment, and help with ongoing medical, travel, and everyday living expenses.

"If you’re able to support our family, no gift is too small—every donation will make a real difference. If you can’t donate, we would be so grateful for your prayers and for sharing our story with your family, friends, church, workplace, and community.

Article continues below

"Thank you for standing with our family during this incredible journey. Your kindness, generosity, and prayers mean more to us than words can ever express."

News.title: Faisal Islam: The new PM has big ideas - but what will they cost?
News.content:
Up until this point, the new Prime Minister Andy Burnham has described his policy changes with a broad brush. From today, he faces the constraints, trade offs, and realities of high national office.

For example, Burnham has said Tuesday's announcements on cost of living support would be paid for. In other words, it would mean a tax rise or spending cut, so we will see rather quickly what the new PM prioritises when push comes to shove.

Meanwhile, the markets seem to have already reacted to the suggestion he would be using some "flexibility" in his borrowing rules to help with new announcements.

The UK government's 10-year borrowing rose above 5% on Monday after falling in recent days. It has not gone up in this way in other European economies.

The move was not huge, but it shows the sensitivities at a moment when Burnham is overhauling his cabinet.

The "flexibility" he was talking about is, I understand, about the treatment of financial institutions. This has occurred in some green energy policies and essentially helps exempt certain types of borrowing from the measures of debt. There is scope for this model to extend to housing and other infrastructure.

It was not a general suggestion of, for example, using up the increased headroom against the government's borrowing rules.

All this shows how every tricky decision and trade off is being watched by the country and the markets at the same time.

News.title: Burnham promises help with your money. How could it affect you?
News.content:
In his first speech as prime minister, Andy Burnham has promised to give people more "breathing space" to help with the cost of living.

Policies will be announced on Tuesday - his first full day in the job. Although a few hours after taking office, the new prime minister confirmed he will be "looking at" the tax-free personal allowance ahead of his first Budget in the autumn.

Cost of living is a key issue for Burnham. Many people, he has previously said, can't go out for a pint on a Friday, can't take the kids out and can't go on holiday owing to the pressure on their finances.

The cost of living has dominated people's lives in recent years, and - to some extent - our politics too. Easing that pressure hasn't been easy.

So, if Burnham chooses to support people on issues such as energy bills and the cost of transport, allows people to earn more before being taxed, and makes care and somewhere to live more affordable - he'll face tough choices on funding those moves and managing the trade-offs that come with them.

And his chancellor will often be the one who has to deliver any changes, and outline how to pay for them.

News.title: Burnham's policy choices reveal what kind of PM he wants to be
News.content:
Later this week, he is expected to change the government's stance on oil and gas exploitation, with a new energy secretary in place.

Those Labour MPs worried about the Green Party taking their seats will be concerned about this - but a lot more will be worried about whether this could be seen to be diluting the government's commitment to net zero.

There was also a promise to do something about the cost of living, with more detail tomorrow on the "breathing space" he is offering hard-pressed families.

Extending Manchester's Â£2 bus fare cap would be a tangible step and also different from the Â£3 cap under Keir Starmer and Rachel Reeves.

With energy prices rising again, there may be action there.

The former minister, Miatta Fahnbulleh, has spent the past few weeks working on policy options. She is the former head of the New Economic Foundation think tank and it wants bolder cost of living measures â from rent controls to making bus journeys entirely free for under 25s.

The question though is whether Burnham will go beyond announcing specific policies and outline a broader vision.

He indicated in his speech that he would set out how the cost of living measures will be paid for. So will he make the greater argument - which he believes - that taxes on income are too high, taxes on wealth are too low?

Will he expand on his Times interview and pledge to raise tax thresholds at least for basic rate taxpayers, while pushing up capital gains tax?

Burnham has said he will be "looking at" the tax-free personal allowance ahead of his first Budget in the autumn but stressed that changing it would be "difficult" in the current economic circumstances, and it could have "significant consequences".

But if he wants to address people's priorities more than his predecessor he may have to find a way to fund this as he also said he had "heard issues related to the personal allowance more than anything on the doorsteps in Makerfield" (the seat he represents).

He has pledged to stick to Rachel Reeves's "fiscal rules," which limit debt and borrowing - so it is likely to be "re-prioritisation" of existing spending rather than new money.

But that can still tell its own story about he intends to govern.

Burnham also promised a new kind of politics â re-using his recent catchphrase of "problem solving not point scoring".

This could be making a virtue out of necessity. If he wants to achieve the ambition he set out today - not to leave office without reforming social care â then he will need cross party co-operation.

More widely, Andy Burnham has not exactly managed expectations.

He has promised nothing less than a new economic model, leaving behind an era of centralisation, privatisation and de-industrialisation.

Just as rough sleeping is meant to signal to party members where he stands, he will soon need to set out symbolic policies which reveal - to voters and the markets alike - what the economic reality will be behind the radical rhetoric.

News.title: Watch: Starmer resigns, Burnham becomes PM... the day so far
News.content:
Andy Burnham has become the UK's prime minister today, replacing Keir Starmer.

The day began outside a busy 10 Downing Street where Starmer made his final address as PM, before he and Burnham visited King Charles in Buckingham Palace.

The new prime minister then gave his own speech in Downing Street saying he wants a "circuit-breaker for Britain" and bring some of the biggest changes that country has seen in 40 years.

News.title: Key takeaways as Andy Burnham becomes PM
News.content:
In his first speech in Downing Street, Burnham announced he would "end rough sleeping in our country".

This was swiftly followed by a No 10 press release promising an extra Â£340m for the task over the next five years.

He also promised a new 10-year plan for Britain - to be unveiled later this year - and to build a new economy, putting "life's essentials back under public control".

But arguing that people also needed "breathing space now", he said announcements on tackling the cost of living would start on Tuesday.

Other changes he promised included changing the education system to help young people into work, building more council homes, and honouring commitments to fund defence while sticking to the UK's spending and debt rules.

News.title: Kevin Keegan, Liverpool footballer who managed England and Newcastle United, dies aged 75
News.content:
Former England captain and manager Kevin Keegan has died at the age of 75, seven weeks after he revealed he had been diagnosed with stage four cancer, his family have confirmed.

One of English football's most decorated players, Keegan enjoyed spells at Scunthorpe United, Liverpool, Hamburg, Southampton and Newcastle during an illustrious playing career.

He later went on to manage Newcastle, Fulham, England and Manchester City.

Keegan revealed he had stage four cancer in June, which is the most advanced stage of cancer and means the disease has spread to other parts of the body.

His family initially disclosed he was battling the disease in January, after he had "further evaluation of ongoing abdominal symptoms" in hospital.

A statement on behalf of the Keegan family said he was "surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments".

"Kevin, a double Ballon d'Or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather," it continued.

"The family would like to thank Kevin's incredible medical team for all their support. This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy."

Newcastle United paid tribute, describing Keegan as "one of the most iconic, influential and deeply loved figures in our club's history".

The club statement added: "Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters.

"Kevin's impact will not be measured by appearances or results. It will live on in the memories he created with club and country, the dreams he inspired wherever he went, and the generations of supporters around the world who fell in love with football because of him."

Liverpool, for whom Keegan played for between 1971 and 1977, said Keegan's "indomitable spirit and remarkable contribution will be forever etched in our history and his legacy will live on".

Hamburg said football had lost one of its "defining figures" and they would always "cherish" his memory, while Fulham said Keegan "forged a strong connection" with the fans, who would "forever hold wonderful memories" of his short time at the club.

England and Manchester City both offered their condolences to the Keegan family, with the latter describing him as "one of the most iconic and fondly remembered figures in English football".

The Three Lions will celebrate Keegan's life when they host Spain in a Uefa Nations League match at Wembley on 26 September.

News.title: Ofcom launches investigation into Married at First Sight UK
News.content:
Married at First Sight UK is facing renewed pressure after the broadcast regulator launched an official investigation into the hit Channel 4 reality TV show.

In a statement on Monday, Ofcom said it was investigating "a fairness and privacy complaint" about the prime-time show.

In May, a BBC Panorama investigation revealed rape allegations from two female cast members on the show - allegations the men involved deny.

An Ofcom fairness or privacy complaint can be lodged by individuals who participated in TV or radio programmes. Complaints like these usually relate to claims of being treated unfairly or having unwarranted infringements of privacy on programmes.

It is understood the watchdog is considering a complaint of unjust or unfair treatment from a cast member of Married at First Sight UK.
