Artan has been offered the UEFA Super Cup between Aston Villa and Paris Saint-Germain after he was barred from entering the USA.

Ceferin is also strongly against any further expansion of the World Cup.

The 2026 edition was the biggest ever, with 48 teams competing, and there are plans for it to be turned into a 64-team event.

Ceferin was also a very vocal critique of the extortionate ticket prices at this World Cup, with UEFA choosing not to adopt some of the rule changes that were introduced for the World Cup.

The most notable one UEFA won't adopt is red cards for players who cover their mouths during confrontations.

5 Balogun thought his World Cup was over before politics got involved Credit: Getty

The straw that broke the camel's back

Balogun had shone for the USA as they made it to the round of 16. However, he was sent off during the 2-0 win over Bosnia in the last-32.

It was thought to be a harsh red card, but FIFA hadn't included any appeal system for the World Cup, meaning he would be banned for the match against Belgium.

However, it was then revealed that Trump phoned Infantino to ask FIFA to review the suspension.

This was confirmed by White House official Emily Goodin who said: “The President and Infantino did speak, and the President wanted to better understand the reason why a red card was given and why there was a suspension.

“The appeal process is run by an independent board.

“The U.S. government provided additional evidence that was used in the appeal process.”

5 Trump took centre stage at points during the World Cup Credit: Getty

FIFA insisted that the final decision rested with the independent board, and they opted to suspend the ban for a year.

This decision was slammed by UEFA who had one of their nations having to prepare for a player who shouldn't have been available due to their being no appeal process.

And they issued a very strong statement that read: "Yesterday's decision to suspend for a probationary period of a year the implementation of the one-match automatic suspension following the red card issued to the player Folarin Balogun crossed a red line.

"Football, like any other sports, relies on rules, which are the basis for fair, honest and transparent competition.

"Sometimes rules are open to interpretation. In this case not.

"A minimum automatic suspension of one match following a red card is not a discretionary option and does not require the decision of a competent body to be enacted. It is a principle embedded in regulations, which cannot be made subject to exceptions, let alone in the middle of a tournament where several other players have been in the same situation and regularly served their suspension.

5 Balogun getting his reprieve proved to be in vain as the Americans crashed out with a comprehensive 4-1 defeat against Belgium Credit: Getty

"When the certainty of rules is no longer guaranteed by its guardians, the integrity of the game is at stake and the credibility of a competition is undermined.

"Equally, such decision creates a precedent in the ongoing tournament, where similar situations will now require an equal treatment, to the detriment of the competition.

"Football is the most loved sport in the world because it is a beautiful game and is trusted because it is played everywhere with the same laws.

"A tournament is never a pure standalone and, if the tournament in question is the World Cup, it has the power to drive positive or negative consequences on the game as a whole.

"We express our disbelief at such an unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable decision."

Fallout continues

Despite the World Cup being over, Infantino continues to be hammered from all angles.

5 Ceferin is one of those placing huge pressure on Infantino Credit: youtube

The latest to have a go is US Soccer's Vice-President, Nathan Goldberg Crenier.

In a piece for The Guardian, he slammed FIFA for 'cosying up' to Trump and suspending Balogun's red card.

Specifically on that, he said: "When it comes to Trump’s meddling in the Balogun case, the biggest casualty was soccer’s integrity.

"Sure, in a narrow sense, US Soccer benefited from having a star player back from suspension.

"But in a more meaningful sense, US Soccer was also a victim: our players were swept up in a political firestorm before the most important game of their lives, and our biggest chance to showcase American soccer to the world will now for ever be tainted by accusations of favoritism at best and corruption at worst, unfairly clouding US Soccer’s credibility and reputation around the world.

"To boot, in return for debasing our sport again and again, Infantino (rewarded) Trump with the honour of handing out the World Cup trophy on Sunday.

"The fact that Infantino has faced little accountability for dragging soccer through the mud reflects a battle for the soul of the sport -- about whether its future will be autocratic and hyper-commercialized, rather than a force for good.

"I say no: soccer leaders must reject Infantino’s egotistical and transactional view of the beautiful game."

Sports.title: FIFA told to slap Leandro Paredes with mega ban as investigation into disgraceful post-match brawl to begin
Sports.content:
FIFA told to slap Leandro Paredes with mega ban as investigation into disgraceful post-match brawl to begin

Leandro Paredes should be banned from the whole of the next World Cup for throwing punches following the end of the final.

That's according to talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor, who slammed Paredes ahead of FIFA's upcoming investigation into his actions.



2 Agbonlahor has called for Paredes to be handed a huge ban for his behaviour Credit: Getty

The Argentina midfielder was involved in chaotic post-match scenes in New York, New Jersey, as things turned violent.

After the final whistle blew and Spain had beaten Lionel Messi and co. to become world champions for a second time, Paredes completely lost control, throwing punches and pushing Spanish players.

He was shown a red card after full-time for his aggression towards Gavi and Eric Garcia, who found themselves on the receiving end of a meltdown in the Argentinian camp.



Paredes' behaviour led to major backlash - and Agbonlahor thinks the 32-year-old should be banned for a long time.

Insisting that harsh punishment must now be dished out, Agbonlahor said on the talkSPORT Breakfast show: "If you watch it back, Paredes on Garcia, he grabs his neck. And the way Garcia's neck jolts, that's assault, it's as simple as that.



"You want to feel safe on the pitch, the punishment has to be that big that no one ever does that again.

"No matter what happens in football, you can be angry you lost, but be classy in defeat. If you want to fight Paredes, there are places to fight - not on the pitch against Garcia.



"And the way he was manhandling Gavi, a 21-year-old kid, and you were throwing him around on the pitch, that's someone's son, brother.

"Disgraceful. I would ban him from the whole next tournament if I had my way. Coward."

Co-host Jeff Stelling then added: "They [Argentina] were shameless, classless thugs during the game, and after the game as well."

2 Paredes lost his cool and started fighting multiple Spain stars Credit: Getty



FIFA set to investigate

Paredes and Argentina seem sure to be eventually hit with punishment for their post-final actions on Sunday.

And now FIFA are set to investigate, according to Sky Sports.

Three incidents could end up leading to suspension or fines, with Paredes not the only one potentially in trouble.

Defender Nahuel Molina pushed Spain captain Rodri as he tried to celebrate, with the incident starting the scuffle.

Also, Argentina coach Roberto Ayala appeared to throw a punch at Dani Olmo after full-time during the brawl.



Footage showed him swinging towards Olmo, with Garcia again involved, having to push Ayala away.

Sports.title: England and Liverpool icon Kevin Keegan dies aged 75 as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
England and Liverpool great Kevin Keegan has died aged 75.

The legendary former player and manager had been battling stage four cancer.

8 Keegan has sadly passed away aged 75 after battling cancer

In a statement, the Keegan family said: "It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75.

"The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

"Kevin, a double Ballon d'Or winner, was a much-loved husband, father and grandfather. The family would like to thank Kevin’s incredible medical team for all their support.

"This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy."

Keegan had revealed at the start of June the devastating news that he was fighting stage four stomach cancer.

His family had confirmed in January that he had been diagnosed, before his condition worsened last month.

He said at the time, per the Daily Mail: "They said we have a top doctor with this new way of fighting what you have got. Which is stage four cancer.

"He was a Liverpool supporter, so I went to meet him. I knew I wouldn't be walking alone, if you know what I mean."

Emotional tributes pour in

England have released a statement to pay tribute to former player and manager Keegan following the sad news.

They wrote: "We are incredibly saddened by the news that Kevin Keegan OBE has passed away.

8 Keegan is an English footballing legend and a two-time Ballon d'Or winner Credit: Getty

"Kevin earned 63 international caps and scored 21 goals between 1972 and 1982, before managing the Three Lions from 1999 to 2000.

"Our thoughts and condolences are with Kevin's family, friends and former clubs."

Keegan is a Liverpool legend and played for the club for six years from 1971 through to 1977, winning seven titles.

The Reds wrote on social media: "We are deeply saddened by the passing of the legendary Kevin Keegan and mourn his loss.

"His indomitable spirit and remarkable contribution will be forever etched in our history and his legacy will live on."

Keegan was Alan Shearer's manager with England and Newcastle, and the striker has posted an emotional message, writing on Instagram: "My Hero. My Manager. My friend. Sleep easy Boss."

8 The 75-year-old is considered an icon at St. James' Park for his services to the club Credit: PA

8 Keegan is one of Newcastle's most influential footballing figures Credit: Getty

His connection to Newcastle on and off the pitch during his career saw him go on to become a 'giant' of their history.

The club have paid tribute too, writing: "We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan, one of the most iconic, influential and deeply loved figures in our club’s history.

"Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters.

"As a player, he brought world-class talent, ambition and belief to St. James’ Park, helping to transform perceptions of what Newcastle United could be.

"As a manager, he ignited our city. Kevin gave supporters hope and pride, and led a team whose style, spirit and passion captured the imagination of football fans around the world. He was so much more than an Entertainer.

"Above all that, Kevin forged an extraordinary bond with Newcastle, built on the roots of his father, Joe. He understood our people. He embraced the North East with a passion that was genuine and unwavering, and in return, he earned his rightful place in the hearts of millions.

8 Keegan is the only Englishman ever to win two Ballons d'Or Credit: Getty

"Kevin’s impact will not be measured by appearances or results. It will live on in the memories he created with club and country, the dreams he inspired wherever he went, and the generations of supporters around the world who fell in love with football because of him.

"At this profoundly sad time, we send our love and deepest sympathy to Kevin’s wife Jean, his family, friends and all who had the privilege of knowing and working alongside him.

"Today, we mourn the loss of a true giant of our history, and at the appropriate moment, we will carefully consider how we shape a lasting tribute to Kevin’s remarkable life and legacy. Rest in peace, King Kev."

Keegan also featured 78 times for Southampton during his playing career, scoring 43 goals and providing 13 assists.

And the Saints have sent their own tribute to the legend, writing: "We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan.

"Kevin signed for the club in 1980 as the holder of the Ballon d’Or and brought great joy to fans at The Dell and across the football world. Our thoughts are with his family and friends at this difficult time."

8 Keegan played over 350 games for Liverpool during his playing days Credit: Getty

Keegan's iconic career

Keegan is widely considered one of the greats of his generation, playing almost 750 club games during his career.

Before his spells at Newcastle and Southampton, he played 363 times for Liverpool and became a club icon.

He scored 100 goals for the club, winning three First Division Championships, two UEFA Cups, one FA Cup and a European Cup.

The former forward also had success playing for Hamburg in Germany, netting 40 goals when playing in Europe.

He picked up his two Ballons d'Or while at the club, collecting the award in back-to-back campaigns in 1978 and 1979.

And the German side have also paid tribute, writing: "With Kevin Keegan, world football loses one of its most defining personalities.

8 Hamburg have released a statement following Keegan's sad passing Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

"We will always cherish an honourable memory of our former championship player and two-time Ballon d'Or winner.

"Our thoughts are with his family, his friends, and all those who accompanied him on his journey. Rest in peace, Mighty Mouse."

On the international stage, Keegan picked up 63 England caps, scoring 21 goals for his country and providing nine assists.

He played in one World Cup game and three Euros clashes, spanning across his decade-long career with the Three Lions.

8 Keegan almost led Newcastle to the Premier League title 30 years ago Credit: Getty

Following retirement from playing the game, Keegan returned to Newcastle, where he had spent two years as a player.

He went on to spend another five years as manager, taking charge of 251 matches in total, winning 138 of them and coming close to winning their first top-flight title since 1927 in 1996.

After leaving in 1997, the legend was next appointed as Fulham boss, before then being named England manager.

Keegan led the nation for almost two years, winning seven of his 18 games in charge, drawing another seven and losing four.

A four-year spell as Manchester City boss followed, and he secured promotion to the Premier League in 2002 with the club.

He announced his retirement from the game in 2005, but he returned to Newcastle in 2008 for a stint that was cut short after eight months, after falling out with owner Mike Ashley.

All at talkSPORT send our thoughts to the Keegan family and his friends. Rest in peace, Kevin.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino facing backlash as staggering World Cup air miles revealed, ‘circled the globe twice’
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino is facing backlash after travelling nearly 60,000 miles in his Gulfstream private jet during the 2026 World Cup.

Despite the World Cup being over, FIFA president Gianni Infantino is facing further backlash.

Ferran Torres scored in extra-time as Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in the Sunday's final as the reigning European champions secured their second World Cup trophy.



4 Spain needed extra-time to beat Argentina in the World Cup final Credit: Getty

Infantino has been at the center of the tournament, notably over the decision to overturn Folarin Balogun's red card ahead of USMNT's Round of 16 clash against Belgium.

The expanded tournament resulted in a record 104 games played, and for Infantino, that represented an opportunity to take in a lot of game time.

"FIFA President Gianni Infantino got some serious air time over the course of the 2026 World Cup, the tournament’s most far-flung edition ever," Rio Yamat of The Associated Press wrote.



"He crisscrossed North America for matches, meetings and other appearances during the competition, which took place in three countries, 16 cities and four time zones, and ended with Sunday’s final in New Jersey.

"The analysis shows that by the time Spain defeated Argentina for the world title, he flew far enough to circle the planet almost 2 1/2 times."



The numbers behind Infantino's jet-setting World Cup

In his Gulfstream G650 jet, Infantino travelled 59,281 miles (95,403 kilometers) - netting a staggering 5,772 in a single day (June 26).

In total he attended 44 matches, including the final, where he handed the trophy to Spain captain Rodri, alongside US President Donald Trump.



Infantino amassed 115 flight hours during the tournament, which is nearly five full days in the air.

Infantino saw at least one game at all 16 World Cup venues, with Miami Stadium being the venue he attended the most.

28 minutes was his shortest flight time, he flew from Seattle to Vancouver to attend USMNT vs Belgium - where Mauricio Pochettino's side were humbled 4-1.

4 Infantino's Gulfstream G650 is from the Qatari government fleet, operated by Qatar Airways Credit: AFP



4 Infantino could have circled the earth two-and-a-half times Credit: AFP

Infantino facing backlash for almost 60,000 mile World Cup

Ahead of the tournament, climate researchers and environmental groups argued the expanded tournament was likely to produce the most atmosphere-polluting World Cup to date.

FIFA claim to be net zero by 2040, but after Infantino's nearly 60,000 mile World Cup, fans can't help but point out the irony.

"Man is creating pollution faster than Erling Haaland runs, what happened to net zero?" one said.



"Football is global, but accountability should be too. This is sickening to see," a second added.

"So much pollution all for sports entertainment, basically watching people work out on a field, not on," a third commented.

"Football's biggest tournament that delivers nothing but a trophy and a huge carbon bill," a fourth said.

4 Infantino attended Sunday's final with close friend and ally Donald Trump Credit: Getty



While the expanded format was hailed as a triumph by FIFA executives, the staggering carbon footprint has left a sour note at the end of the tournament.

President Trump wants another USA World Cup, but by then Infantino, or his successor, may face far tougher environmental restrictions.

Stay up to date with the World Cup across all our talkSPORT platforms - subscribe to our YouTube channel for the latest news, opinion, exclusive interviews and our daily unfiltered, unscripted show 'The S* Word, from 8am ET

Sports.title: New unseen footage shows what sparked ugly brawl between Argentina and Spain players
Sports.content:
New unseen footage shows what sparked ugly brawl between Argentina and Spain players

New footage has revealed that Argentina's Nahuel Molina started the World Cup final brawl by throwing a punch at Rodri.

As soon as the full-time whistle blew at the MetLife Stadium, Spain's World Cup triumph descended into chaos as Argentina players were seen throwing punches at full-time.

4 Rodri and Molina were seen confronting each other at full-time, and the reason for this has now become clear Credit: Getty

After Ferran Torres' 106th-minute winner sealed victory for La Roja, the 2022 champions lost all composure in the immediate aftermath.

Leandro Paredes was shown a red card amid a series of bust-ups, having appeared to throw punches at Gavi and Eric Garcia.

Royal rumble

Fresh footage has now revealed exactly how the violent scenes began, with Argentina right-back Molina seemingly the culprit.

In a video capturing the scenes seconds after the final whistle, Spain's players can be seen sprinting in joy to celebrate.

But as Rodri runs onto the pitch from the sidelines, Molina is shown throwing a punch at the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner's stomach.

After realising what has happened, the Spain captain turns around and heads back to confront the Argentina full-back.

Separate footage has honed in on the confrontation which follows, where the pair can be seen shoving each other, before Eric Garcia comes across to stick up for his teammate Rodri.

Chaos ensued from then on, as Paredes then got involved, who shoved Garcia to the ground before grappling with Barcelona's Gavi.

As shown in television footage, Paredes also grabbed Garcia by the throat, and repeatedly pushed Gavi to the floor.

This triggered a mass brawl, with Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni forced to drag his players away, culminating in referee Slavko Vincic showing Paredes a red card.

4 A closer look at the full-time scenes shows Molina land a punch on Rodri's chest Credit: X: @TouchmineX

The ugly scenes aren't likely to go unpunished, with FIFA set to investigate the behaviour of Argentina after the final whistle at the World Cup final.

Paredes and Molina could both be handed retrospective bans, while Argentina could be sanctioned for failing to control their players.

The post-match brawl followed an ill-tempered clash, which saw Argentina reduced to 10 men after Enzo Fernandez was sent off.

Fernandez was shown a second yellow card in second-half stoppage time, before Spain finally made their dominance count as Torres netted the winner in the second period of extra time.

'Something needs to be done'

Argentina's conduct at full-time was widely condemned, with talkSPORT's Adrian Durham and Gabby Agbonlahor both calling for FIFA to take action.

Reacting on commentary at full-time, Durham said: "That Paredes punch after the full-time whistle, honestly. He needs to be done for that. Something needs to be done about these Argentinians.

4 Tempers boiled over at full-time in the World Cup final as Argentina's tournament ended in unsavoury scenes Credit: Getty

"Argentina are a total embarrassment to the game, an embarrassment to the World Cup.

"England in the semis were on top, handed it on a plate to Argentina, who came here to the final and totally embarrassed themselves."

After the dust had settled on Monday morning, talkSPORT Breakfast host Agbonlahor then insisted Paredes must be severely punished.

The Aston Villa icon said: "You want to feel safe on the pitch, the punishment has to be that big that no-one ever does that again.

"No matter what happens in football, you can be angry you lost, but be classy in defeat, if you want to fight Paredes, there are places to fight - not on the pitch against Garcia.

"And the way he was manhandling Gavi, a 21-year-old kid, and you were throwing him around on the pitch, that's someone's son, brother.

4 Argentina's midfielder Paredes was at the heart of the ugly scenes at the MetLife Stadium Credit: Getty

"Disgraceful. I would ban him from the whole next tournament if I had my way. Coward."

Sports.title: World Cup manager exit announced day after final as statement released
Sports.content:
Belgium have announced that manager Rudi Garcia will not be continuing as manager following the World Cup.

Garcia leaves his post after leading the nation to the quarter-finals of the tournament, where they lost 2-1 to Spain.

3 Garcia has left his job as Belgium manager a day after the World Cup final Credit: Getty

In a statement released on Monday, the day after La Roja lifted the trophy, the Belgian FA wrote: "Rudi Garcia and the RBFA will not extend the contract that runs until 31 July 2026.

"Rudi Garcia took up his role on 1 February 2025 as the successor to Domenico Tedesco. Under his technical leadership, the Belgian Red Devils secured their place in League A of the UEFA Nations League and qualified for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

"At the World Cup, the Belgian Red Devils were eliminated in the quarter-finals by Spain, who went on to become world champions."

Garcia himself said: "After discussions with the RBFA, we have decided not to extend the excellent journey we have shared over the past 18 months.

"I leave Belgium in League A of the UEFA Nations League and among the top eight teams in the world.

"I would like to thank my outstanding group of players, Sports Director Vincent Mannaert, and the fans who supported us throughout this World Cup.

"I wish Belgium every success as they continue the generational transition that I was proud to help initiate."

Meanwhile, Sports Director Mannaert added: “Rudi Garcia has unquestionably played a key role in restoring the Belgian Red Devils.

"He was appointed national coach in a challenging sporting and financial context. Thanks in particular to his commitment and experience, team cohesion was restored and a strong result was achieved at the most recent FIFA World Cup.

"On behalf of the federation, I would like to warmly thank Rudi and his assistants for the past 18 months. Together with my team, I am currently preparing for a new cycle, including the appointment of a new national coach.”

3 Garcia leaves after taking Belgium to the World Cup quarter-finals Credit: Getty

Garcia's Belgium tenure

Garcia took charge of 20 games as Belgium manager in total, including six at the World Cup this summer.

He won 12 of his 20 matches, losing just twice altogether.

The 62-year-old lost his first game in charge in March 2025 but then went on an 18-match streak undefeated.

The defeat to Spain at the World Cup was just his second loss as manager - and that is now his last outing.

At the tournament, Belgium drew with Egypt and Iran as they got off to a poor start, before going on to thrash New Zealand.

Kevin De Bruyne and co. then beat Senegal in the last 32 before they embarrassed co-hosts USA with a 4-1 win in the last 16.

3 The 62-year-old only lost two games in his tenure as Belgium manager Credit: Getty

Who next for Belgium?

According to reports in Belgium and the Netherlands, Mark van Bommel is a contender to replace Garcia as manager.

Van Bommel has not had a role since leaving Belgian side Royal Antwerp in June 2024.

In that post, he took charge of 107 matches, winning 57 of them and lifting the league title in the 2022/23 campaign.

He also won the Belgian Cup with the club that season, claiming the Belgian Super Cup the following campaign.

The former Barcelona and Bayern Munich midfielder has also managed Wolfsburg and PSV in his career.

Van Bommel also revealed on talkSPORT that he held some talks with Rangers in September 2025.

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan dead at 75: Football legend passes away following battle with cancer as devastated family pay heartbreaking tribute to England icon
Sports.content:
Newcastle and England legend Kevin Keegan has died at the age of 75 after a short battle with illness.

Keegan was diagnosed with stage four stomach cancer in January, having been admitted to hospital with abdominal problems.

In a statement, his family said: 'It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75.

'The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

'Kevin, a double Ballon d'Or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather. The family would like to thank Kevin's incredible medical team for all their support.

'This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy.'

Keegan leaves behind his wife, Jean, who he met on the waltzers at Doncaster fair in 1970 – he was 19 and she was 16. They married four years later and had two daughters, Laura, 48, and Sarah, 44.

Kevin Keegan in the England strip in 1981 (left) and playing for Newcastle United in 1983

The former England manager was diagnosed with stomach cancer in January this year

Keegan, who played for Hamburger SV in the late 1970s (pictured), was a formidable footballer and twice won the Ballon d'Or - football's most prestigious individual prize - during his career

He won 63 caps for England and scored 21 goals across his ten-year international career

As a Liverpool player, Keegan delivered European glory for the Anfield club in 1977

In the 1970s, Keegan was renowned for his 'poodle perm' hair

Keegan pictured with his wife, Jean, who was by his side when he died on Monday

At Buckingham Palace with Jean and three-year-old Laura after being awarded an OBE in 1982

In a statement, Newcastle FC said: 'Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters.

'As a player, he brought world-class talent, ambition and belief to St. James’ Park, helping to transform perceptions of what Newcastle United could be.

'As a manager, he ignited our city. Kevin gave supporters hope and pride, and led a team whose style, spirit and passion captured the imagination of football fans around the world. He was so much more than an Entertainer.

'Above all that, Kevin forged an extraordinary bond with Newcastle, built on the roots of his father, Joe. He understood our people. He embraced the North East with a passion that was genuine and unwavering, and in return, he earned his rightful place in the hearts of millions.

'Kevin’s impact will not be measured by appearances or results. It will live on in the memories he created with club and country, the dreams he inspired wherever he went, and the generations of supporters around the world who fell in love with football because of him.

'At this profoundly sad time, we send our love and deepest sympathy to Kevin’s wife Jean, his family, friends and all who had the privilege of knowing and working alongside him.

'Today, we mourn the loss of a true giant of our history, and at the appropriate moment, we will carefully consider how we shape a lasting tribute to Kevin’s remarkable life and legacy. Rest in peace, King Kev.'

Liverpool added: 'Liverpool FC is deeply saddened and mourning the passing of the legendary Kevin Keegan. Our "Mighty Mouse", his legacy at Liverpool will be forever etched in history. Rest in peace, Kevin Keegan'

In January, Keegan was admitted to hospital due to 'ongoing abdominal symptoms', a statement from his family said.

'These investigations have revealed a diagnosis of cancer, for which Kevin will undergo treatment,' it added.

However, he looked sprightly when he made his first public appearance since his diagnosis in June, at An Audience With Kevin Keegan in Newcastle. He told fans at the Tyne Theatre that he was responding well to treatment after joking that he 'was still alive'. He also said, 'We have a top doctor with this new way of fighting what you have got'.

'He [the doctor] was a Liverpool supporter, so I went to meet him. I knew I wouldn't be walking alone, if you know what I mean.'

Keegan began his playing career at Scunthorpe in 1968, before moving to Liverpool to play for Bill Shankly three years later.

Keegan negotiated a contract worth £50 a week – Shankly had originally offered him £45.

It marked the beginning of a glorious playing career where he won 63 caps for England – captaining the Three Lions on 31 occasions.

The attacker won the First Division three times, the European Cup once and the UEFA Cup twice during a six-year stint at Liverpool.

Keegan even made the Charity Shield memorable after Leeds United midfielder John Giles punched him in the face and was shown a yellow card. Keegan's reaction, however, after a series of aggressive tackles from the other team, saw him sent off when it sparked a brawl with Billy Bremner and they came to blows. Liverpool won the game on penalties.

🗣️ "I WILL LOVE IT IF WE BEAT THEM, LOVE IT!"



We have lost an English football legend today 😢💔 pic.twitter.com/YWo87RCnUV — The 44 ⚽️ (@The_Forty_Four) July 20, 2026

After retiring from football in 1985, Keegan turned to management and was at the helm of his beloved Newcastle United for five years (pictured with famous Geordies Ant and Dec in 1995)

His 'I would love it' meltdown saw Newcastle's Premier League title charge fall apart

Keegan also managed England but handed in his resignation in the Wembley tunnel

KEEGAN'S ILLUSTRIOUS CAREER Years Club Appearances Goals 1968–1971 Scunthorpe 124 18 1971–1977 Liverpool 230 68 1977–1980 Hamburg 90 32 1980–1982 Southampton 68 37 1982–1984 Newcastle United 78 48 1985 Blacktown City 2 1 Honours: Liverpool Football League First Division: 1972–73, 1975–76, 1976–77 FA Cup: 1973–74; runner-up: 1976–77 FA Charity Shield: 1974, 1976 European Cup: 1976–77 UEFA Cup: 1972–73, 1975–76 Hamburg Bundesliga: 1978–79 European Cup runner-up: 1979–80 Individual: Ballon d'Or: 1978, 1979 FWA Footballer of the Year: 1975–76 PFA Players' Player of the Year: 1981–82 Years Club Win% 1992-97 Newcastle United 55 1998-99 Fulham 62 1999-00 England 39 2001-05 Manchester City 44 2008 Newcastle 32 Honours: Newcastle United Football League First Division: 1992–93 Fulham Football League Second Division: 1998–99 Manchester City Football League First Division: 2001–02 Individual Premier League Manager of the Month: November 1993, August 1994, February 1995, August 1995, September 1995

He then moved to Germany to play for Hamburg and was named European Footballer of the Year in both 1978 and 1979. He added to the trophy cabinet in Germany, too, winning the Bundesliga and reaching the 1980 European Cup final.

Doncaster-born Keegan returned home after three years in Germany and spent time at Southampton and Newcastle - who he would later go on to manage. He rounded off his playing days with two appearances for Australian semi-professional side Blacktown City.

Keegan scored 204 goals in 592 career appearances across six clubs in a stellar career.

Alongside being iconic on the pitch, he produced his fair share of legendary moments off it too.

While Newcastle boss in 1996, Keegan launched a tirade on Manchester United during the heat of the Premier League title race.

Newcastle had let a 12-point lead slip at the top of the table with United moving six points clear after beating 10-man Leeds United 1-0 in April 1996.

Leeds played the majority of the game with defender Lucas Radebe in goal, which prompted Sir Alex Ferguson to question the Yorkshire side's integrity and whether they would show the same grit against Keegan’s Newcastle.

Newcastle responded by beating Leeds 1-0 to move three points behind Man Utd with a match in hand, and only two left to play.

But Keegan let the pressure of the title race get to him in his post-match interview, accusing United of being ‘slanderous’ and screaming ‘I will love it if we beat them, love it’.

His managerial career produced its fair share of bizarre moments.

In 1999 Keegan succeeded Glenn Hoddle as England boss but resigned in 2000 following a disappointing European Championship campaign and a loss to Germany at the old Wembley.

Keegan famously resigned in the tunnel following the drab defeat to Germany in October 2000. Following a brutal reception from the England fans, he told his players in the dressing room that he was stepping down before confirming his resignation to FA director David Davies in a nearby stadium toilet cubicle.

He guided Newcastle to the Football League First Division title during the first of two stints at St James' Park and came close to lifting the Premier League, only to be pipped by Manchester United.

He would go on to oversee promotions to the top flight for both Fulham and City.

Sports.title: Football world mourns Kevin Keegan: Heartbroken Alan Shearer pays tribute to his 'hero', Jamie Carragher hails 'one of the greatest players this country has ever produced', while Prince William says he 'inspired generations'
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Alan Shearer has led the tributes to football legend Kevin Keegan after he passed away at the age of 75 following a short battle with illness.

Keegan was diagnosed with stage four stomach cancer in January, having been admitted to hospital with abdominal problems.

In a statement, his family said: 'It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75. The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

'Kevin, a double Ballon d'Or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather. The family would like to thank Kevin's incredible medical team for all their support. This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy.'

And following the tragic news, figures from across the footballing world were quick to pay their respects to Keegan, who represented Scunthorpe, Liverpool, Hamburg, Southampton and Newcastle and later managed the Magpies (twice), Fulham, England and Manchester City.

Newcastle legend Shearer said: 'My Hero. My manager. My friend. Sleep easy Boss.'

Alan Shearer and Jamie Carragher led the tributes to football legend Kevin Keegan (pictured after winning the European Cup with Liverpool in 1977) after he passed away

Keegan is one of the best ever English players and enjoyed a successful managerial career

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher added: 'RIP Kevin Keegan. One of the greatest players this country has ever produced, trophies & goals galore, double Ballon d'Or winner shows he was an absolute giant of the English game.

'One of the most important men in making @LFC what it is today.'

Prince William, the official patron of The FA, said: 'Incredibly saddened to hear of the passing of Kevin Keegan.

'A truly remarkable footballer and manager who inspired generations with his talent, passion and love of the game.

'Above all, he will be remembered as a kind and generous man. Our thoughts are with his family and all who knew him. W.'

Several of Keegan's former clubs also shared their own tribute, including Newcastle.

Taking to social media, they said: 'We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan, one of the most iconic, influential and deeply loved figures in our club’s history.

'Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters.'

Liverpool shared their own heartfelt post which read: 'We are deeply saddened by the passing of the legendary Kevin Keegan and mourn his loss.

'His indomitable spirit and remarkable contribution will be forever etched in our history and his legacy will live on. Rest in peace, Kevin. 1951-2026.'

Former Reds star John Aldridge said: 'I've just been passed the really sad news.

'The great Kevin Keegan has passed away! He gave me great joy in my teens as a huge LFC fan, and the saying says never meet your heroes?

'Well I did!! Roger Hunt and KK and they surpassed everything I thought they were as people. Our thoughts are with all his family. God bless Kevin YNWA.'

Keegan, a forward in his playing days, won 63 caps for England before he later managed the Three Lions.

And they also posted a tribute which said: 'We are incredibly saddened by the news that Kevin Keegan OBE has passed away.

'Kevin earned 63 international caps and scored 21 goals between 1972 and 1982, before managing the #ThreeLions from 1999 to 2000.

'Our thoughts and condolences are with Kevin's family, friends and former clubs.'

Shearer pictured with then Newcastle boss Kevin Keegan after signing for the club in 1996

Heartfelt tributes poured in for Keegan from figures and clubs across the footballing world

Former Newcastle owner Mehrdad Ghodoussi added: 'Devastated to hear about Kevin Keegan. Growing up watching football, he was one of the names that defined an era, a double Ballon d’Or winner, European Cup champion, England captain, and one of the most exciting players the game has seen.

'But what he did at Newcastle was different. He turned belief into something you could feel in the stadium.

'King Kev wasn’t just admired, he was loved, because everything he did came from the heart. Rest in peace, Kevin. Thank you for everything you gave the game.'

During his managerial career, Keegan also took Fulham from the Second Division (now League One) to the First Division (now Championship).

And the Cottagers shared some words for the footballing legend as they said: 'We're incredibly sad to hear the news that our former manager Kevin Keegan has passed away.

'A legend of the game, Keegan led Fulham to the Football League Second Division title in 1999. He left Craven Cottage at the end of that season to focus on his duties as England manager.

'Our thoughts are with his friends and family at this difficult time.'

Manchester City, another of the teams Keegan managed, added: 'Everyone at Manchester City is devastated to learn our former manager Kevin Keegan has passed away, aged 75.

'Kevin was a transformative manager who brought optimism and vibrancy to City during his four-year spell in charge.

'The promotion campaign in 2001-02 will never be forgotten, and Kevin then established us once again as a top Premier League side in the years that followed. Our thoughts are with Kevin’s family and friends at this very difficult time.'

Sports.title: The day Kevin Keegan hurtled down the autobahn at 100mph to get me to the airport on time - after our lunch of  beefburgers and steins of pilsner to mark his move to Hamburg, writes JEFF POWELL
Sports.content:
When Kevin Keegan was on the foothills of his international career in 1972, Sir Alf Ramsey called him into an enlarged England squad.

To say that he was not best pleased when this country's only World Cup-winning manager designated him to the Under 23s match on the night before the senior game is something of an understatement.

Keegan packed his bags in anger and had to be stopped from storming out of the hotel by urgent warnings that he would be jeopardising his England future.

In common with most Fleet Street football reporters, I denounced his prima donna tantrum. A year or three of strained relations with the press ensued.

Once, upon the conclusion of a football awards dinner in London, I took a few of my guests on to the members' club Morton's for late-night drinks. The all-time greatest gossip columnist Nigel Dempster among us.

We were merrily ensconced in the bar overlooking Berkeley Square as Kevin arrived with a couple of his pals. When he saw I was there, he pulled over the manager and told him: 'I'm not comfortable with that journalist being here, invading my privacy.' The reply: 'I'm sorry Mr Keegan, but Mr Powell and Mr Dempster are founder members of this club so we won't be asking them to leave.'

Kevin Keegan was all heart in the end - brimming with energy, flooded with adrenalin, full of fun and an arch competitor

An hour or so later he departed, with a cursory nod in our direction. A thaw, then? Maybe. I was told he appreciated that both Nigel and myself refrained from embarrassing him in print about that awkward incident.

Fast forward to his transfer to Hamburg and to some surprise he agreed to an interview about his new life in Germany. Our lunch of the world's largest and purest beefburgers washed down by steins of pilsner lingered until it seemed likely I would miss my flight back to London. 'Don't worry,' said Kevin. 'I'll drive you.'

He called the restaurant valet to bring his racy German car, while the Mail settled the bill. We went bouncing down cobbled streets and then hurtled onto the autobahn at well over 100mph. Speed limits back then in the Fatherland were virtually non-existent.

A mile or two from the airport, a British Airways plane loomed into view a few hundred feet above us on a flight-path which tracked the motorway. Keegan rammed his foot even harder on the accelerator and we undertook the plane. After screeching to a halt in front of departures we jumped out of the car, laughing. High-fived as he said: 'Yes, we beat it here. That must be your return flight home. Looks like you made it.'

That was Kevin Keegan. Oh so feisty if he felt wronged. All heart in the end. Brimming with energy. Flooded with adrenalin. Full of fun. Arch competitor. Raging with ambition yet eager to help others. All of that. Off as well as on the pitch. How on earth has this irrepressible 5ft 8in human dynamo died so young at 75? Curses on the cancer which has taken Mighty Mouse, as he was affectionately nicknamed.

Mine was just one of many such rollercoaster experiences. At Wembley in the infamous 1974 Charity Shield game between Liverpool and Leeds, he and Billy Bremner were sent off for punching each other, in the brawl which followed him being hacked down by Johnny Giles. After the match, Keegan joined the hysterical criticism of Leeds as a brutal side urged into mischief by their genius manager Don Revie.

A few years later, Revie made Keegan the captain of England. Not only was all forgiven, but it was not long before Kevin hailed the Don as 'my mentor and like a second father to me'.

Actually, he should have said third father.

While he was a Liverpool legend, his England achievements took him to just one World Cup quarter-final

Of all the moves during his football lifetime, the one which launched him towards the football stratosphere was gifted unto him by the immortal Bill Shankly.

The founding father of Liverpool FC as we have known and loved that bastion of the game in recent decades was told about a little kid making waves at Scunthorpe United down in the depths of the old Fourth Division.

One cold wet midweek night in 1971, Shankly's idea of how best for him and his beloved wife to celebrate their wedding anniversary would be to make that tortuous 240-mile round-trip drive over the Pennines and back to watch the boy Keegan in action.

One £33,000 transfer, 323 matches, 100 goals, three English championships, one FA Cup, one European Cup, two UEFA Cups and six years later, Shanks said: 'Best wedding anniversary me and Nessie ever had.'

There would have been many more Liverpool goals had it not taken a while for Shankly to transform Keegan from an orthodox midfield player into a second striker. A quite passable imitation of Maradona in that free-rein role.

Hamburg were next to benefit from that transition with a ratio of more than a goal every three games (40 in 113) after signing in 1977. Thus Keegan led them to their first German championship in 19 years and their first European Cup final.

His additional personal reward for those efforts was to be voted into the pantheon of only 10 players ever to be voted European Footballer of the Year twice. To go with his English Footballer of the Year honour in his penultimate season at Anfield.

Then, at both Southampton (42 in 80 games) and Newcastle (49 in 85), he averaged better than a goal every two games. But the vibrant essence of the man ran even deeper than those impressive statistics. They were the product of that impulsive instinct for the game, the fizzing speed off the mark, the instant eye for the perfect space to sprint into, the defence-splitting pass recognised before all around him were aware, the non-stop stamina. The never-say-die optimism.

He admitted the England management job wasn't for him - but he was raging with ambition yet eager to help others

In the more rarified challenge presented to England he scored precisely once every three games – 21 in 63 – and the first England captain he played under articulated his value. Bobby Moore would say: 'Loved Kev. Terrific player and best of all he drove the opposition crazy.'

Circumstances, including injury and under-achievement by the national team, limited his World Cup impact to one quarter-final. Which starved him of much of the wider recognition his brilliance deserved. Perhaps his quirkiness, too. He simply did not care when that bizarre perming of his thick growth of hair invited comedians to do their worst.

Nor did he bother to respond to scurrilous rumours which followed him being set upon while caught sleeping in his Range-Rover on the side of the M25 in Surrey. Simply leaving it to his assailants to explain in court that they saw him as a potentially wealthy target to rob, without realising it was Keegan.

When retirement from playing led to management he became embroiled in heated rows with directors. Not that his start-stop first spell in charge at Newcastle ever cooled the adoration poured onto him by the second of two of the most passionate communities on the planet. First Merseyside, then Tyneside. An idol on both shores of the northern powerhouse of English football.

If anything the Geordies massed behind him all the more loudly when first-season promotion from the Second Division was followed by the losing of a 12-point lead over Manchester United and with it the title.

If anything they loved him all the more when the paramount manager in the history of English football, Sir Alex Ferguson, beat him at the mind games which characterised that race for glory. 'I will love it if we beat them. Love it.' That was not to be. Nor was success as manager of England.

When his one year as successor to Glenn Hoddle ended in a 1-0 home defeat by Germany which set up England for failure to qualify for the 2002 World Cup, he retreated into a lavatory in the Wembley dressing room. In that sanctuary he sadly and quietly told the FA's media chief David Davies that he was resigning immediately 'because I'm not right for this job'.

Keegan was lampooned for that by some critics, who preferred not to acknowledge the honesty within the personal anguish.

Wistful nostalgia surrounds the loss of idol Keegan - he is survived by devoted wife Jean and their two daughters

After retirement he shied away from public scrutiny, other than when boosting his several charities, and into the bosom of family life with devoted wife Jean and their two proud daughters. One consequence is that he is not recognised fully by new young football fans and partly neglected by forgetful older generations.

Wistful nostalgia always surrounds the loss like this of an idol. Personally, I for one regret not responding with alacrity on one of the occasions when I pondered organising a reunion in Berkeley Square. If it is any excuse, Mr Dempster also died too young and Morton's closed some time ago.

Sports.title: JEFF POWELL MBE: Why unapologetic imposter Lionel Messi is now not even in the top five players of all time - and will forever be tainted as the leader of Argentina's brutes in ugliest World Cup final ever
Sports.content:
JEFF POWELL MBE: Why unapologetic imposter Lionel Messi is now not even in the top five players of all time - and will forever be tainted as the leader of Argentina's brutes in ugliest World Cup final ever

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

An image of the real greatest footballer of all time flickered briefly across the stadium with no proper name before the team captained by the imposter to that throne desecrated his beautiful game.

Pele, from wherever he was watching, will have been as tortured as the rest of us by the ghastly possibility of Argentina slithering to World Cup victory on penalties after kicking more Spaniards than they did footballs.

Brazil’s maestro of the most glorious football ever played, along with hundreds of millions of us who love this game, was spared that obscenity by a solitary goal scored by a Spanish substitute in extra time.

Nor will Pele have been as forgiving of Lionel Messi’s part in that looming travesty as all those who have casually mis-proclaimed their darling little Leo as the most talented player ever to walk God’s hallowed turf. With the emphasis on walk.

And neither will he have been impressed by the armbanded standard-bearer for the ugliest losers in World Cup history. Especially not as Messi sat shedding tears for his men’s brutish failure to defend their championship. Instead of crying for Argentina and himself, he should have wept for the infamy of the team under his charge.

From Messi there has not been one syllable of apology for the thuggery which ruined the principal showpiece for the game which has enriched him beyond Croesus. Not one word of regret for his disgruntled brethren instigating the brawl which disgraced their hour of defeat. No hint of recognition for reducing this nasty, tedious game to the bottom of the list of the 13 World Cup finals which have come under my scrutiny.

Messi shed tears for his men’s brutish failure to defend their championship. Instead of crying for Argentina and himself, he should have wept for the infamy of the team under his charge

No hint of recognition for reducing this nasty, tedious game to the bottom of the list of the 13 World Cup finals which have come under my scrutiny

MY UPDATED TOP 10 FOOTBALLERS OF ALL TIME 1. Pele Brazil 2. Diego Maradona Argentina 3. Garrincha Brazil 4. Johan Cruyff Netherlands 5. Alfredo Di Stefano Spain 6. Lionel Messi Argentina 7. Ferenc Puskas Hungary 8. Cristiano Ronaldo Portugal 9. John Charles Wales 10. George Best Northern Ireland

To think, furthermore, that I was once seduced by his natural-born skills into elevating Messi to third in my ranking of the best in the anthology of football. We all make mistakes.

Those revised rankings accompany this verdict on FIFA’s elongated tournament of mixed blessings. Along with little Leo clinging on to a place in my forever best world Xl. Just about. Although he was on the brink of deletion at the end of Sunday’s final to which his only contribution was to lob a hopeful cross-cum-shot onto the roof of the Spanish goal netting.

That carefully curated image was not helped, either, by Messi doing precious little in the semi-final before Thomas Tuchel sounded England’s retreat into suicidal defence of a one-goal lead.

A lot of reputations were damaged in this ever-lasting tournament. To suggest that Tuchel should escape the hardest judgement because England won a 10-goal so-called thriller against France in that spurious run-out for third place only handicaps any hope of recovery.

That was a Mickey Mouse coconut shy of a match which France threw away by not turning up for the first half, although they partially redeemed themselves by running riot through Tuchel’s wonky England defence after the interval. Also exposed was this manager’s stubbornness in not selecting England’s most exciting player, Bukayo Saka, before they were knocked out. Even though the Arsenal forward had declared himself fully fit.

With the FA further hog-tied after rushing an extension of Tuchel’s contract to the home Euros two years from now, they are condemning England to stagnation. As Brazil, Germany, France, Argentina, especially Italy and Spain as well as Argentina begin a four-year recycling programme of head coaches as well as players towards the next World Cup, so England will lag two years behind.

Trapped in their Tuchel syndrome. If it carries on like this, stand by for another 60 years of depression.

Ominously, also, the gap is closing fast between the old-guard masters of Europe and South America and the uprising of African, Asian and Caribbean football. Witness Morocco, Egypt, Cape Verde, Senegal, Ivory Coast, DR Congo and Curacao coming close to springing a mass upset here.

To think that I was once seduced by his natural-born skills into elevating Messi to third in my ranking of the best in the anthology of football. We all make mistakes

DR Congo came ever so close to causing a huge upset against England in the last 32

Pele had predicted the time was fast approaching when an African team would win the World Cup. This is coming closer and closer as more and more talents from the continent garner experience in the major European leagues. The greatest one’s forecast is not beyond realisation in 2030, even though Spain in their dedicated and organised development of a winning style of football will again be the team to beat. Especially since they will be co-hosts.

Meanwhile this country of ours which gave the greatest of all games to the world trundles along, with the blinkered moguls of the Premier League at the wheel. Even as their clubs splurge hundreds of millions of pounds on domestic players of limited promise. If England learned one thing from this tournament, it is that the likes of Morgan Rogers, Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice are not worth nine-figure fees. Not close.

If the Premier League was taught one lesson, it is that the UFC cage-wrestling with which Arsenal won the title last season will no longer be tolerated by referees. It is an ill World Cup wind which brings no such consolations.

Although 2026 in all its expansionist corporate greed, half-time grovelling to yawn-inducing musical celebrities and suspicions of favouritism has come close to bringing down the Infantino empire. As well as England.

Sports.title: Revealed: The fee Como are willing to pay for Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah - with Morgan Rogers due for Blues medical ahead of £117m move from Aston Villa: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa plough on with Jackson move

Aston Villa are continuing to discuss a proposed deal for Nicolas Jackson at Chelsea.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday that Jackson has come up in conversation during negotiations over Morgan Rogers' £117million sale.

A proposed transfer for Rogers, who started his Chelsea medical today, and Jackson was discussed a year ago and the Senegal international is well known to Villa boss Unai Emery.

For more on this story click HERE

Nicolas Jackson joined Chelsea in 2023 but spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich

Como show hand for Chalobah

Como are willing to offer £35million for Trevoh Chalobah as talks continue over the Chelsea centre back's future.

Chalobah has been on World Cup duty with England and made a fleeting appearance against France on Saturday.

Como had been rebuffed in their opening two proposals for the 27-year-old and are working to meet Chelsea's valuation with a structured offer.

Inter Milan have also discussed Chalobah as they want two centre backs but Como are hopeful they can conclude a deal for Cesc Fabregas.

Serie A side Como are interested in signing Trevoh Chalobah from Chelsea

New arrival at Liverpool

Alejandro Rosalen has been appointed Liverpool’s new first-team goalkeeping coach. The 49-year-old Spaniard joins Andoni Iraola’s backroom staff, replacing Xavi Valero.

Rosalen was at Serie A side Napoli and previously spent eight years with Fiorentina.

Gomes goes to Villa

Aston Villa have confirmed the signing of Joao Gomes from Wolves. The deal is worth £38m comprised of an initial fee of £34m plus £4m in add-ons.

United land Thompson from Spurs

Manchester United have signed teenage winger Tynan Thompson from Tottenham, subject to the registration, in a deal believed to be worth up to £8million.

It's understood that United will pay £4m plus up to another £4m in add-ons to Spurs who will have a 15 per cent cut of any future sale.

Manchester United have signed Tynan Thompson from Tottenham

Thompson, who was on the bench for Tottenham several times last season, scored 13 goals and contributed six assists across Under-18s and Under-21s games, including seven goals in as many UEFA Youth League fixtures.

Thompson was involved in three senior matchday squads for Spurs last season and was on the bench against PSG and Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.

United confirmed the deal in a statement, saying: 'Everyone at United would like to welcome Tynan to the club and wish him the very best of luck for the future.'

CHRIS WHEELER

Rogers due for Chelsea medical

Aston Villa midfielder Morgan Rogers is due for his medical at Chelsea today.

Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday that Rogers's former club Middlesbrough will pocket around £20.2million from Morgan Rogers' £117m transfer to Chelsea, which would represent a record sell-on fee in the Premier League.

Morgan Rogers is due to undergo his medical ahead of a move to Chelsea

The ex-Boro midfielder is set for a move to Stamford Bridge after Chelsea struck a verbal agreement with Aston Villa, after Arsenal had failed to back up their interest with a suitable bid.

When Boro agreed to sell him to Aston Villa, in February 2024, for £16m, they inserted a 20 per cent sell-on clause on any profit generated from a future transfer in the England international's contract.

Diop discussing Portman Road switch

Fulham defender Issa Diop is in talks over an £8.5million move to Ipswich.

The 29-year-old played for Morocco at the World Cup and is discussing a four-year contract with Gary O'Neil's side.
