Sports.title: Hamilton says Spa practice shunt compromised his race pace | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes he could have fought for the victory in the Belgian Grand Prix had he not crashed in third practice.

The Ferrari driver finished fourth at Spa-Francorchamps after an eventful grand prix. He collided with George Russell at Les Combes on the opening lap, which led to Russell’s retirement and a five second penalty being handed to Hamilton, before running into a Ferrari mechanic during a pit lane mishap.

Russell admitted after the accident that he saw the clash as a racing incident that both of them had contributed to. But Hamilton apologised for his part in the collision.

“Ultimately, I’m sorry for George because that obviously ended his race,” Hamilton told the official F1 channel. “But I do agree that it was a racing incident.

“It’s not like I went in aggressive and was misplaced or anything like that. I think it was just an unfortunate scenario, which happens in racing. Then I had damage as well, so I carried that through the race. It was a tough one. I’m hugely grateful for the points given the damage and given the crash yesterday.”

Hamilton had given his Ferrari mechanics a busy few hours on Saturday afternoon after crashing his car at the exit of the Fagnes chicane at the end of the final practice session, but his SF26 had been fixed in time for him to participate in qualifying. However, Hamilton believes that accident compromised his performance for the remainder of the weekend and his final result and he could have joined team mate Charles Leclerc in fighting for victory without the crash.

“Ultimately, it was not a good weekend from my side,” he said. “I think my race pace was strong today and I think without the damage, and probably without yesterday, I think we could have been fighting for the win today.

“Even with the damage I was challenging Charles [Leclerc]. It is what is, we move on, and hope we can have a better weekend next weekend.”

Welcome to Monday’s edition of the RaceFans round-up.

Social media and links

The Belgian Grand Prix stewards handed Ferrari a US$30,000 (£22,300) fine of which US$10,000 (£7,440) is suspended for the unsafe pit release incident which saw Lewis Hamilton hit a Ferrari mechanic during the Belgian Grand Prix.

2026 Belgian Grand Prix - Race Report (McLaren)

Oscar Piastri: ''We had good pace today, especially in the first stint, and the podium wasn't out of the question, which is a positive we can take away. However, it was certainly not a straightforward race for us. The damage we sustained after the contact with Charles Leclerc just made things much more difficult as we were losing a few tenths per lap. I struggled for the rest of that stint, and while we compensated a little for it in the second stint, the race was tougher than it needed to be.''

Into the Ardennes (Aston Martin)

Lance Stroll: ''Our pace was pretty much where we expected it to be today. We knew this track was always going to be difficult for us and it was a tough race from the start. Towards the end I started to feel something with the gearbox, so we retired the car to investigate it. Hopefully we can be a bit more competitive in Hungary and have a stronger weekend there.''

Câmara impressively seals back-to-back sweep at Spa for Invicta (F2)

'Rafael Camara was made to work for his second victory of the season, putting in a mature display to win the Spa-Francorchamps Feature Race. The Brazilian driver had to manage losing his lead at the start, a Red Flag stoppage and challenges from his rivals to seal the win – with Invicta Racing winning both races at Spa for the second consecutive year. ART Grand Prix driver Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak achieved his maiden Formula 2 podium in P2, with Campos Racing’s Nikola Tsolov in third.'

León disqualified, Beganovic penalised following Spa-Francorchamps Feature Race (F2)

'Following the conclusion of the FIA Formula 2 Feature Race at Spa-Francorchamps, Noel León has been disqualified while Dino Beganovic has been penalised. During the race, it was alleged that a non-operational person was using a headset with a microphone fitted in the pitlane during the Red Flag period, contravening Article 21.5 and Appendix 5 of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. The Team representative explained that the person concerned was a team guest who had inadvertently taken the wrong type of headset. As it was established that the guest was associated exclusively with Car 5, the Stewards determined that the disqualification should only apply to León.'

Rivera wins with charging drive at Spa (F3)

'Ernesto Rivera was unstoppable on Sunday, claiming the Feature Race victory with an impressive drive to the top step. The Campos Racing driver started from fourth on the grid, but was patient in the early stages before picking off his rivals to move into the lead past halfway, and was uncatchable from there. Hiyu Yamakoshi claimed P2 for Van Amersfoort Racing, while Freddie Slater wound up third in the Trident, as he cut the gap to Ugo Ugochukwu down to a single point in the championship.'

Turoboyski and Piatek crowned first FIA Arrive and Drive European champions on home soil (FIA)

'Two new names have been etched into the FIA Karting history books this afternoon as Polish drivers Kacper Turoboyski and Maksymilian Piatek conquered the Autodrom Słomczyn, masterfully racing to home victory to conclude the inaugural Arrive and Drive European Championship and in so doing securing their places at the 2026 Arrive and Drive World Cup in Malaysia later this year.'

Sports.title: Rise from 21st to sixth “probably my best race” – Hadjar | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar described his performance in the Belgian Grand Prix as “probably my best race” for the team.

Hadjar started all the way down in 21st position on the grid after receiving a ‘back of the grid’ penalty for multiple power unit component infringements. However, he rose up the order through the race to finish in sixth place, extending his run of top six finishes to six races.

Hadjar pitted twice under the early Safety Car to satisfy his two tyre compound requirement, then ran two long stints on hard tyres after the restart to make his way up the order. The Red Bull driver said that long runs on the hard tyre had always been the intention, heading into a weekend where he knew he would be starting down the order.

“We knew that was part of the plan, starting nearly last, and we worked on it quite a lot through the free practice sessions,” he told Sky.

“Our one-lap pace was not the target and, today, it paid off. So I’m glad we really put the work in on the long runs. I think it really helped. And moving forwards, maybe change the approach, because it worked really well.”

After rejoining the track after his final pit stop, Hadjar was around 15 seconds adrift of team mate Max Verstappen ahead, but finished the race around 12 seconds behind the multiple world champion. Hadjar says he is very satisfied with the pace he showed during the race at Spa-Francorchamps.

“I think our one-lap pace, I showed what I needed to show,” he said. “Today I think is probably my best race.

“Race pace-wise. I’m right up there with the leaders, so I’m very glad with my first ten races. To be honest, I’m really looking forward to the race, because there are a lot of things we need to tidy up as a team – in a good way. I think there’s a lot more to come.”

Sports.title: Leclerc “confident I’ve made a step forward” after back-to-back podiums | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc believes he is finding form after taking second place in the Belgian Grand Prix and fighting Andrea Kimi Antonelli for the victory.

The Ferrari driver passed Max Verstappen and George Russell on the opening lap of the race to move into second behind Antonelli, then gained the lead of the race after pitting under a Virtual Safety Car.

He would later be caught and overtaken by Antonelli, but still finished second, just under two seconds adrift of the Mercedes driver. It was Leclerc’s second consecutive podium after winning the British Grand Prix in the last round following a start to the season where he seemed unable to match the performance of team mate Lewis Hamilton.

“I’m confident in saying that I made a step forward,” Leclerc said after the race. “Whether I’m at the level where I want to perform, not yet.

“There are still things in the car that I need to drive around. I cannot drive completely naturally, and that is slowing me down in some parts of the race. So, there are still things that I’ve got to work on in order to be better. But surely it was a step forward, and for that I’m happy. I’ll continue with the one-race-at-a-time approach because, with these cars, it’s very difficult to be confident that if one race weekend goes well, the other one will, because it relies on such small details. With what you do with your driving, it’s never a given that you get the same deployment from one lap to the other, and that’s maybe the frustrating bit about these cars.”

Leclerc admitted at the start of the weekend he expected to be “very far back, maybe to the extent of four or five tenths” a lap around Spa-Francorchamps.

“In qualifying, that was true, but in the race we were a bit closer than we thought,” Leclerc said. “So, it’s been positive.

“I think on two tracks which, on paper, were quite bad for us, we won and we finished second, with a little bit of luck, but still, I think it was a good effort from the team. On two tracks that didn’t fit our car particularly well, we’ve scored good points.”

Asked if he believed he could carry this momentum into next weekend’s race at the Hungaroring and be in contention for victory once more, Leclerc says it’s to difficult to be sure how good his team will be heading into any given weekend.

“We could be, but we could also not be, and we’ll never know until we go there,” he said. “I think it’s very difficult to predict the level of performance of every team.

“I recall very well what the overall feeling was before Monaco, and we arrived in Monaco and were under-performing compared to what everybody thought we would. So, I think we need to be cautious. We just need to do our homework, just like we do at every different track. I think what we did particularly well over these last two weekends was to really make sure that we maximised our package, and that’s the mentality we should keep for Budapest, without thinking about expectations.”

Sports.title: Wolff says Russell not alone in Mercedes power woes, was “team mistake” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff claims all Mercedes-powered cars were down on power during the Belgian Grand Prix.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli won the race for Mercedes, but team mate George Russell crashed out on the opening lap after contact with Lewis Hamilton at Les Combes.

Russell later said that while he felt the contact with the Ferrari driver was a racing incident, he implied that a battery deployment problem – which he had been complaining had been affecting his straight-line performance all weekend at Spa-Francorchamps – was more responsible for causing the clash. Wolff accepted that a power unit deployment problem had been a contributing factor.

“I think there’s two situations here,” he told Sky after the race. “First, the racing accident – that happened. Unfortunately, for us, we lost a lot of constructors points and, George, a lot of drivers’ points.

“George tried on the outside, braked late, and that corner should have been his, but it was a racing incident. These things can happen, whether you’re at the front, in the middle, or at the back of the pack. George had a tough weekend. Probably half of that can be attributed to the power unit, which wasn’t as good as it should have been in his car, and the other half perhaps to the driving.

“But we’re in this together. We all make mistakes. Today it was a team mistake on another day it’ll be a driver’s mistake. We just need to minimise those mistakes and support each other.”

Wolff says that Russell was not the only Mercedes-powered driver who was experiencing lower than expected power deployment during the Belgian Grand Prix.

“We had an issue on all Mercedes engines that we lacked the power out on the straights,” he admitted. “That bit him [Russell] badly and it goes one-hundred-percent on us.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We’re trying our best as a team. We have the most powerful power unit – we have a strong car that is capable of winning. Everybody gives their maximum to minimise their mistakes and still it happens – because we are humans at work. We let Kimi down at Silverstone where George got a podium – that was maybe better than the result should have been – one driver DNF’d in Canada, the other DNF’d in Barcelona. That’s a little bit the story of our season, here. It’s a technical sport, it’s a mechanical sport.

“I’m proud to be a part of the organisation at HPP and Mercedes Grand Prix. Those groups of people give it all they have and we came out with a product this year that is so strong and I’d rather fix the reliability than try to accelerate a slow engine or a slow car. We’re giving it one-hundred-percent and we need to give it one-hundred-percent, because we have lost a lot of points through reliability. We should be much further ahead than we are.”

Russell had been slower than than Antonelli throughout the weekend. Wolff suggested that Antonelli may have learned how to maximise the performance from the new-generation power units for 2026 compared to his more experienced team mate.

“I think, first of all, it’s very different and I think this is probably an advantage that Kimi has, because it reset for everyone,” he said.

“Then the components of energy harvesting and energy deployment plays a role. Even the way you go on the throttle – whether you give it full throttle or half throttle and when you lift off – can have consequences in terms of the energy delivery. And that’s another dimension that has been handed to the driving – some drivers may not like it, others may say ‘okay, we just need to get used to it’. But it’s another component that makes it more complex.”

Wolff said he would talk to Russell to console him following his latest setback in the championship, which has seen him drop to third in the standings behind Hamilton.

“I haven’t seen him yet, but it’s completely understandable that the moment you’re out of this race it’s so frustrating and the emotions boil. That’s why I completely understand. He has our one-hundred-percent support. We are trying to solve all the issues, he’s doing everything he can to get on top of his driving. So I haven’t spoken to him, but I’m going to try and put my arms around him.”

Sports.title: Antonelli passes Leclerc to win Belgian GP, Russell out after Hamilton clash | 2026 Belgian Grand Prix report
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the world championship to 45 points after winning the Belgian Grand Prix.

The Mercedes driver had led early on after starting from pole, but a Virtual Safety Car had allowed Charles Leclerc to take the lead in the pit cycle.

Eventually, Antonelli was able to chase down the Ferrari and pass for the lead with 11 laps to go. Max Verstappen completed the podium in third.

At the start, pole winner Antonelli held the lead into La Source, but Verstappen in second managed to get ahead of the Mercedes into Eau Rouge. Verstappen’s time in the lead was shortlived, however, as Antonelli passed the Red Bull back down the Kemmel Straight, with Leclerc also following through into second place.

Behind, a three-way fight for fourth between George Russell, Lewis Hamilton and Oscar Piastri ended in tears when Russell and Hamilton collided through Les Combes, sending the Mercedes spinning into the gravel trap and out of the race. Hamilton was able to continue, but was later handed a five second time penalty for being deemed responsible for the collision.

After a Safety Car to recover Russell’s car, the race resumed on lap five with Antonelli leading from Leclerc and Verstappen. Antonelli headed the field until a brief Virtual Safety Car on lap 18 to clear debris, which turned green by the time Antonelli had pitted for Hard tyres.

Leclerc remained out a handful more laps than Antonelli, until a second debris-related VSC was triggered on lap 20. This allowed Ferrari to pit both Leclerc and Hamilton, to serve his penalty, and enabled Leclerc to rejoin the circuit still under VSC ahead of Antonelli, taking what was effectively the lead of the race.

After Lando Norris pitted, Leclerc took the overall race lead, but Antonelli began to slowly reel him in. Eventually, on lap 34, Antonelli tucked up behind the Ferrari along the Kemmel Straight and overtook Leclerc to take the lead.

While Leclerc tried his best to remain in touch with with the championship leader, Antonelli was able to keep ahead of the Ferrari until the chequered flag, heading him by just under two seconds. Verstappen was around ten seconds behind the pair in third, with Hamilton taking fourth place after passing Piastri in the later laps.

Isack Hadjar moved from 21st on the grid to finish sixth, ahead of Lando Norris, Gabriel Bortoleto and Arvid Lindblad. Franco Colapinto took the final point in tenth for Alpine, ahead of team mate Pierre Gasly.

Hamilton will be investigated after the race for an unsafe pit release after one of the Ferrari mechanics was struck by his right-front wheel as he was released from his pit stop. Ferrari confirmed to Hamilton over team radio that the mechanic involved was unhurt.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Gets IBF Eliminator Against Conor Wallace on October 3
Sports.content:
While Wallace holds the higher ranking, his record has been built almost entirely against regional-level opposition in Australia. The 30-year-old has yet to beat an established world contender despite spending eight years in the professional ranks. His biggest victories have come against fighters such as Jerome Pampellone and Dylan Colin, making it difficult to judge how he will perform against the most talented opponent of his career.

Whittaker has also been criticized for the level of his opposition as a professional, but he brings a much stronger amateur background into the eliminator. The Olympic silver medalist defeated several elite amateurs during his run to the 2020 Olympic final before losing to Cuba’s Arlen López in the gold medal bout. That experience against elite international competition gives him an advantage that Wallace does not possess.

If Bivol keeps hold of the IBF title, the winner will move into position for a championship fight under the sanctioning body’s rules.

This is a fight for Whittaker, 29, that should provide a clearer picture of his true standing among the global elite. Wallace’s ranking makes him a legitimate opponent, but his record leaves questions about how much resistance he can offer against a fighter with Whittaker’s amateur pedigree.

Sports.title: Barry Hearn Sees Different Anthony Joshua Before Prenga Fight
Sports.content:
“AJ is in an amazing place at the moment. Obviously, I’ve seen him since 2012. We’ve got very close. He’s like a member of our family. “I don’t think I’ve seen him so motivated for the long term. Some of that’s been fueled by that tragic accident, but he’s now talking about the next three years in the ring. It was a year ago that we were talking about potentially two fights and then go off to a happy retirement. “He’s very motivated; he feels good about himself, but boxing is a funny sport. It takes one punch from a big lad to knock out anyone in the world. So, you’ve got to be on your toes all the time. You can’t take this for granted. And when you get your chance, you’ve got to take it. “AJ is in the mood to cause a lot of pain on Saturday. I don’t think I’ve seen him look better than this in the 14 years I’ve known him. He is in the right place, and I think on Saturday in Jeddah will be the right time,” Barry Hearn told Sky Sports.

Prenga wasn’t chosen to be a threat. He’s there to give Joshua rounds after the accident. Gym performances don’t mean much when the opponent isn’t expected to test you. Until Joshua gets back in with a heavyweight who can crack and force him to answer questions, nobody knows if the flaws from the Dubois fight remain. Barry Hearn’s comments are what you’d expect from a promoter backing one of his biggest stars.

Joshua was stopped by Daniel Dubois in 2024. AJ rebounded from that defeat last December, knocking out the YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul in a fight that was largely viewed as a celebrity-esque spectacle. Even in that victory, Joshua looked vulnerable before knocking out Paul.

AJ has always looked like a million bucks on the scale or hitting pads in the gym, but that means very little once someone real lands a clean shot on his chin.

He can look as motivated as Barry Hearn says, but gym work can’t replicate how a fighter reacts to getting hit, especially after coming back from a car accident. If Prenga manages to land something solid on Saturday, we’ll see right away if those old vulnerabilities are still there.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn: Boots Ennis Is ‘King Of The Castle’
Sports.content:
The way Hearn sees it, Vergil Jr. has nothing that Boots wants other than the money the fight would bring in. He doesn’t hold a major belt. The WBC interim 154-lb title isn’t enough.

Hearn says his fighter is no longer in the position of making concessions to land the bout. Boots is now “king of the castle.”

“He was taking the smaller side of the piece last time. He was going to be the B-side. He agreed to everything that they wanted to get that opportunity. So you imagine how he feels now that he’s king of the castle,” said Hearn to the media about Ennis’ position in negotiations with Vergil Ortiz Jr. “Vergil doesn’t have anything Boots wants other than a big fight and a big payday. What does Boots want to do now? He wants to unify.” “I don’t rule out that Ortiz fight at all. One thing is for sure. He ain’t close at all at the moment.“

Hearn’s comments reflect how much Ennis’ position has changed over the past year. During earlier discussions, Ennis was still chasing the biggest opportunities and was willing to accept B-side status to secure a fight with Ortiz. Hearn says those circumstances no longer exist.

Ennis now holds two world titles and has shifted his attention toward becoming the undisputed champion. Hearn indicated that unification bouts remain the priority, but he left the door open for Ortiz if Golden Boy presents an offer that outweighs Ennis’ other options.

“Tell us what the money is. And I’ll go to Jaron, and I’ll say, ‘We got Kelly, Fundora, or Ortiz,'” said Hearn.

Unless Turki Alalshikh gets involved, it’s questionable if a fight with Ortiz Jr. is financially appealing enough for Ennis to take time off from pursuing his goal of becoming the undisputed champion at junior middleweight.

Sports.title: Vernon Forrest Outboxes Shane Mosley Again in 2002 Rematch
Sports.content:
Six months after defeating Mosley to capture the championship, Forrest again relied on his size, jab and disciplined boxing to earn a 12-round unanimous decision and settle the rivalry once and for all.

The rematch carried enormous significance. Forrest defended both the WBC and Ring Magazine welterweight championships after taking them from Mosley in their first meeting earlier in the year in January 2002. Many believed Mosley would make the necessary adjustments and reclaim the titles, while Forrest had the opportunity to prove the upset had not been a one-night performance.

The event attracted 15,775 fans, the largest crowd to attend a boxing card in Indiana history at the time. HBO televised the championship bout nationally, and both fighters earned career-high paydays. Forrest received $3.42 million, while Mosley collected $2.8 million. Veteran referee Laurence Cole officiated the 12-round title fight.

Mosley came out aggressively, looking to erase the disappointment of the first bout by forcing exchanges from the opening bell. Forrest refused to be drawn into a firefight. Standing three inches taller with the longer reach, he established his jab early, circled effectively and answered Mosley’s rushes with sharp counters before tying him up whenever the action moved inside.

As the rounds progressed, Forrest steadily took control. Forrest repeatedly stabbed Mosley with the jab before tying him up whenever the challenger got close, forcing Mosley to reset his offense over and over. Referee Laurence Cole was forced to separate the fighters throughout the contest as the tactical battle became increasingly physical.

The middle rounds lacked sustained action, drawing boos from portions of the crowd, but Forrest remained committed to the game plan. One report even noted that a fight in the stands during the sixth round briefly attracted as much attention as the action inside the ring.

Mosley increased the pressure during the championship rounds, finally producing several spirited exchanges in the tenth. Forrest answered with crisp counterpunching and finished strongly, landing several hard right hands late in the eleventh before boxing confidently through the final round. There were no knockdowns, but Forrest consistently landed the cleaner, more effective punches.

CompuBox statistics reflected the tactical nature of the contest. Forrest landed 120 of 446 punches, while Mosley connected on 114 of 259, with Forrest’s jab, timing and ring control outweighing Mosley’s higher connect percentage.

Judges Gary Merritt (117-111), Tony Castellano (116-112) and Jerry Roth (115-113) all favored Forrest. HBO unofficial scorer Harold Lederman and several media scorecards also had Forrest winning, confirming that his first victory had been no accident.

The rematch closed the book on one of the era’s most compelling rivalries. Forrest had defeated Mosley twice as a professional after also beating him during the 1992 U.S. Olympic Trials, establishing a rare mastery over one of boxing’s greatest fighters.

Mosley later captured world titles in higher weight classes, while Forrest continued his championship run before unifying the welterweight division. More than two decades later, the rematch remains one of the signature victories of Forrest’s Hall of Fame career, removing any doubt that his success against Mosley was built on superior technique rather than surprise.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Reveals Zuffa Promise Behind His Signing
Sports.content:
Shakur is counting on the Tank and Devin Haney fights happening for him, but they may not. If the Haney and Tank Davis matchups evaporate, the entire situation changes, and Shakur’s massive money-making leverage shrinks instantly.

Even under the best circumstances, it’s not a given that Zuffa will be able to hook a big fish like Gervonta Davis to fight Shakur. Despite Shakur’s elite skills and massive new Zuffa backing, he simply doesn’t move the needle the same way with the casual audience.

If Shakur demands anything close to parity or tries to dictate the terms, Tank will likely dig his heels in. Tank has shown before that he would rather sit out, pursue a lesser name, or even talk about walking away from the sport entirely than give up his leverage to an opponent he feels needs him more than he needs them.

“What really went into the decision was mainly life-changing money. Not only life-changing money, just life-changing opportunities,” Shakur said to Fighthype. “Dana [White] and Nick [Khan], they kept saying, ‘We want to get you in with the best fighters. We wanted you to fight the best.’ The guys that they mentioned was Devin and Tank. And when I heard that, I’m like, why would I go away from what I’ve been wanting to do my whole career? I think my whole career I’ve been saying the titles and all that, I done it. With all due respect to the titles, I appreciate y’all… but I want to fight the best. I want to get in there and prove myself and get under them bright lights and see who’s the best. I’m not scared of taking no risk.”

Haney hasn’t said whether he’s going to fight Shakur next or defend against his WBO mandatory, Keyshawn Davis. If Keyshawn actually upsets Haney to take the WBO welterweight title, Shakur’s biggest potential fight is effectively dead.

“I think that’s what really kind of kicked it off with me and Zuffa. Their vision is as big as mine. I ain’t never really hear promoters with big visions like me. It’s an amazing thing, and I’m happy to be the person to lead the new school and new generation,” Shakur said.

With Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn officially locked in for September 12, a Ryan loss changes everything for the 147-pound division. Ryan is arguably the sport’s biggest ticket seller and pay-per-view draw outside of Canelo. Shakur vs. Ryan is a massive financial fallback if Tank or Haney fall through. If Benn beats Ryan, that golden parachute disappears.

While a Benn victory makes Conor a massive star under the Zuffa banner, a Shakur vs. Benn fight doesn’t carry the same casual fan appeal or domestic PPV weight as a clash with Garcia. Benn doesn’t have the same popularity in the U.S as he does in the UK. American fans view Benn as the son of a famous retired ex-world champion, who has never beaten any elite-level fighters during his career.

Sports.title: Mike McCallum Flattens Donald Curry With Devastating Left Hook
Sports.content:
Many favored Curry’s speed and sharper boxing to carry him to another world championship. Instead, one perfectly timed punch produced one of the greatest knockouts of the decade.

The scheduled 15-round championship bout was televised by HBO from the Caesars Palace Sports Pavilion in Paradise, Nevada. Richard Steele served as referee, while Guy Jutras, Jerry Roth and Ove Ovesen handled the scoring. An official attendance figure was never widely reported, but the event drew major attention as one of the biggest championship fights of 1987.

McCallum was making the sixth defense of the WBA junior middleweight title he had won in 1984. Nicknamed “The Body Snatcher,” the Jamaican-born master tactician had knocked out every opponent during his title reign. Even with those accomplishments, sportsbooks installed him as a 2-1 underdog.

Curry entered as the WBA’s top contender after previously holding the WBA, WBC, IBF and Ring Magazine welterweight championships. Moving to 154 pounds offered a fresh opportunity to reestablish himself among boxing’s elite and position himself for even bigger fights.

The fight also carried significant financial rewards. McCallum earned a reported $475,000, while Curry received $425,000, excellent purses for championship fighters during that era.

For four rounds, the betting odds appeared justified. Curry’s jab repeatedly beat McCallum to the target. His hand speed, combinations and movement kept the champion from settling into his rhythm, and a sharp right hand in the second round buckled McCallum’s knees. By the end of the fourth, Curry had built a comfortable lead on all three scorecards. McCallum remained dangerous, but he looked a step behind as Curry controlled the action.

At 1:14 into Round 5, Curry stepped inside and drove a right hand toward McCallum’s body. McCallum anticipated the attack, gave a subtle body feint of his own, then unleashed a crushing left hook that landed flush on Curry’s jaw. The fight ended instantly.

Curry crashed flat onto his back, staring toward the lights as Steele began the count. He slowly regained awareness around seven but never gathered himself in time to continue. The referee completed the count, and McCallum had retained his championship with one of boxing’s most unforgettable single punches.

The knockout earned KO Magazine’s Knockout of the Year honors and remains one of the finest one-punch finishes ever shown on HBO. Ironically, Sugar Ray Leonard worked the broadcast that night after Curry had reportedly objected to his presence on the telecast, which brought an extra bit of drama to an already memorable evening.

McCallum later vacated the WBA title to pursue championships at middleweight and light heavyweight, eventually becoming a three-division world champion and earning induction into the International Boxing Hall of Fame. Although he never landed the marquee fights against Sugar Ray Leonard, Marvin Hagler, Thomas Hearns or Roberto Durán, his body of work cemented his reputation as one of boxing’s most accomplished champions.

The defeat for Curry proved far more damaging than anyone expected. He won a handful of fights afterward but never returned to the level that once made him one of the sport’s pound-for-pound stars, suffering later defeats to Michael Nunn and Terry Norris before retiring.

More than three decades later, McCallum’s left hook remains one of the greatest one-punch knockouts in championship boxing history and the defining moment of an unforgettable title fight.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Pressures Diego Pacheco to Fight Lester Martinez
Sports.content:
“It’s time to grab a hold of them balls, bro. You should have been handling Sheeraz. I was picking you to beat Sheeraz. Sheeraz is getting better and better while your ass is sitting back here fighting against dudes like Aleem,” said Bradley on his YouTube channel. “Why don’t you go ahead and go after Berlanga after this? Better yet, go ahead and get Lester. Lester fought this dude, and we’re comparing the two. Lester went the full distance with him. You got him up out of there. Why don’t you fight Lester? That’s a hell of a fight.”

Bradley is right that Pacheco needs a real test, but Saturday’s performance didn’t convince me he’s ready for the division’s elite. He boxed well, finished Aleem impressively and showed patience under Buddy McGirt, yet he was still getting hit too often by a fighter who isn’t known as a devastating puncher. That’s the concern.

If Aleem was able to land that frequently, what happens against Osleys Iglesias, Lester Martinez or even middleweights Carlos Adames or Yoenli Hernandez if they moved up? Those fighters carry more power, are physically stronger, and wouldn’t be as forgiving once Pacheco found himself exchanging at close range.

The Kevin Lele Sadjo fight exposed flaws in Pacheco when the action became physical. He didn’t look comfortable under sustained pressure, and those issues weren’t answered against Aleem because the matchup never forced him into the same type of fight.

Pacheco’s post-fight comments focused on Canelo Alvarez and Jaime Munguia. Eddie Hearn has also floated Munguia as a possible next opponent. If Matchroom wants to prove Pacheco belongs with the division’s elite, fights against Iglesias, Lester, Adames or Hernandez would answer far more questions than a quick jump toward a lucrative name.

Hearn has the financial backing to make those fights. If Matchroom bypasses them and heads straight toward Munguia, it will be difficult to ignore the possibility that the priority is maximizing Pacheco’s value before a dangerous contender exposes the flaws that are still visible in his game.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Faces Zuffa Pressure Despite “Storybook” Claim
Sports.content:
“The Knicks just won the NBA championship after 53 years, and then I’m headlining Madison Square Garden a month after,” said Berlanga to TMS Sports. “It’s like thank you God. This was destined to happen. Alvarado winning the chip. I’m going next month after headlining Madison Square Garden. It all lined up perfectly. Now he’s walking me out. Brooklyn is having a moment.”

The picture outside the interview tells a different story.

Saturday’s main event is a 10-round showcase against Steven Butler, a fringe contender with five defeats who has come up short in his biggest opportunities. Berlanga also enters the fight after losing two of his last three bouts, including a knockout defeat to Hamzah Sheeraz, followed by a year away from the ring.

That leaves little margin for error in his first appearance under the Zuffa banner. An impressive win would give Dana and Zuffa a platform to match Berlanga against recognizable names at 168 or 160 pounds. A poor performance, or an upset loss, would make that job far more difficult.

Ticket demand has also become part of the conversation. The BoxingTickets account on X claimed Zuffa removed roughly half of the remaining inventory for the event before increasing prices on the seats still available, describing the move as “gimmicking the ticket sales.”

Zuffa has not commented publicly on the ticket changes. With the promotion investing heavily in Berlanga as one of its first headline attractions, Saturday’s fight carries importance well beyond the result inside the ring.

Ghana News.title: Wontumi conviction based on assumptions, not proof beyond reasonable doubt – NPP
Ghana News.content:
The New Patriotic Party (NPP) says the conviction of its Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, was based on assumptions and inferences rather than evidence that met the legal threshold of proof beyond reasonable doubt.

The Accra High Court sentenced Bernard Antwi-Boasiako to 20 years' imprisonment over illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

Addressing a press conference in Accra on Monday, July 20, the General Secretary of the party, Justin Frimpong Kodua, said the NPP disagrees with the judgment of the Accra High Court and believes the conviction cannot stand on appeal.

The party argued that it was never disputed during the trial that Chairman Wontumi lawfully acquired his mineral concession, insisting that the central issue before the court was whether he had unlawfully assigned or transferred his mineral rights.

"It is our considered view that Chairman Wontumi has been convicted in circumstances where there was no evidence at all to support a conviction in respect of the offence for which he has been convicted. It was never disputed that Chairman Wontumi lawfully acquired his Mineral concession.

"That fact was established and accepted before the Court. The central question was whether that concession had been assigned or transferred in violation of the law. It is our respectful view that no evidence was adduced before the Court establishing any such assignment or transfer of mineral rights by Chairman Wontumi," he said.

He added, "the prosecution could not produce any evidence to show that Wontumi had assigned his Mineral right. Instead, the conviction rested on assumptions and inferences which, in our view, could not amount to proof beyond reasonable doubt."

This, according to the party, "is why we firmly believe that this conviction is a travesty of justice and has to be overturned on appeal."

The NPP has indicated that it will pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the court's decision, while maintaining that Chairman Wontumi deserves a fair hearing through the appellate process.

Ghana News.title: GHAMRO to pay highest digital royalties ever
Ghana News.content:
For decades, Ghana's music royalty story has sounded like a hit record that always skipped at the best part.

Musicians wrote the songs. Fans memorised every lyric. Radio stations, clubs, bars, concerts and, more recently, streaming platforms kept the music alive. Yet when royalty season arrived, many creators were left scratching their heads.

How was my royalty calculated? Where did the money come from? Why is my payment so small?

Even worse, royalty distributions often sparked another familiar chorus. Speculation. Complaints. Allegations that payments depended more on influence than actual music usage. Some artistes publicly questioned the amounts they received, while others wondered whether the system rewarded popularity, productivity or simply proximity to power.

GHAMRO now appears determined to change that narrative.

Beginning July 27, 2026, the Ghana Music Rights Organisation(GHAMRO) will commence its first royalty distribution of the year, fulfilling its pledge to pay royalties twice annually. For the first time, every beneficiary will receive a personalised royalty statement showing exactly which quarters generated theirearnings.

That may sound like a routine administrative upgrade. It is anything but.

Transparency is the currency of trust. Today's musicians no longer want to hear, "Here's your money." They want to know exactly how every pesewa found its way into their account.

Technology finally takes centre stage

This is more than another payment cycle. It is a sign that GHAMRO is embracing the tools used by leading collective management organisations around the world.

The organisation now relies on WIPO Connect for repertoire management, ACRCloud for broadcast monitoring, CIS-Net for international rights data exchange, and CISAC standards for copyright administration. Together, these systems improve data accuracy, strengthen royalty matching, and give creators greater confidence that their music is being tracked properly.

In today's digital music economy, technology is no longer a luxury. It is the backbone of fair royalty distribution.

The numbers tell a bigger story

This distribution covers:

• Background Music Royalties for the first and second quarters of 2026

• Digital Mechanical Royalties, mainly for the third and fourth quarters of 2025

• Digital Performance Royalties, mainly for the third and fourth quarters of 2025

• Live Performance Royalties, mainly for the third and fourth quarters of 2025

The total distributable amount stands at GHS1,433,571.43, comprising:

• Background Music: GHS500,000.00

• Digital Mechanical: GHS706,149.55

• Digital Performance: GHS160,641.88

• Live Performance: GHS66,780.00

One standout figure deserves special attention. The single highest royalty recipient in this distribution will receive GHS121,000, a powerful reminder that when music usage is properly tracked and collections improve, meaningful royalty payments are possible.

The organisation has also recorded its strongest digital collections and its highest international royalty collections since GHAMRO was established in 2011. In an industry where streaming increasingly drives revenue, that is a milestone worth celebrating.

Progress worth applauding

Ghana's royalty system has travelled a long and sometimes bumpy road. Before GHAMRO, the Copyright Society of Ghana (COSGA) managed music royalties. Earlier still, Ghanaian musical works were largely administered through foreign collecting societies.

GHAMRO was created to build a more efficient, technology-driven organisation capable of protecting Ghanaian creators in a rapidly changing global music business. Today's investment in digital monitoring, international data exchange and itemisedroyalty reporting shows that vision is steadily becoming reality.

The current leadership deserves credit for pushing transparency higher up the agenda and delivering on its commitment to distribute royalties twice a year despite significant operational challenges.

The elephant is still in the studio

Every success story has its unfinished chapter.

GHAMRO's biggest hurdle remains the unresolved issue surrounding its operating licence. The prolonged licensing impasse continues to limit the organisation's ability to maximiselocal collections, ultimately reducing the money available for musicians.

Every business that uses music without paying licence fees is effectively enjoying someone else's creativity for free while the people behind the songs lose income they have rightfully earned.

This is no longer just a copyright issue. It is an economic issue affecting composers, performers, producers, publishers and the wider creative industry.

The Office of the Attorney General must bring certainty to the licensing process. The longer the delay, the greater the cost to Ghana's music economy.

The work is not finished

GHAMRO has made impressive strides, but there is still room to grow. Creators need continuous education on royalty calculations, music registration and metadata. Broadcasters and commercial music users must also take licensing obligations more seriously. The organisation can further strengthen confidence through regular stakeholder engagements, enhanced digital self-service platforms and quicker resolution of royalty disputes.

Transparency should not be a twice-yearly event. It should become part of GHAMRO's DNA.

A better future is within reach

No institution becomes world-class overnight. What matters is consistent progress.

This latest royalty distribution sends an encouraging signal. Better technology, record international collections, stronger digital revenue, personalised royalty statements and a top payout of GHS121,000 all point to an organisation moving in the right direction.

Now the baton passes to government, broadcasters, businesses and every user of music. A strong licensing regime is essential if creators are to receive the full value of their work.

After all, every unforgettable chorus, every wedding favourite, every street anthem and every global hit begins with one person and one idea.

When creators are fairly rewarded, the entire music industry wins. And so does Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Explaining the Zeepay saga (Part 1)
Ghana News.content:
Understanding Zeepay: The Rise of Ghana's Homegrown Fintech Giant

Until July 2026, Zeepay was widely regarded as one of Ghana's biggest fintech success story. Founded in 2014 as a small local startup, it grew into a cross-border payment platform connecting Africa with the rest of the world. The company attracted millions in international investment, expanded into over 20 African markets, processed billions in remittances, and became one of the continent's leading indigenous fintech firms.

That rapid rise explains why the Bank of Ghana's decision to revoke its licence attracted so much attention. To understand why it matters, we first need to understand what Zeepay actually is - and what it isn't.

What is Zeepay?

Zeepay is a fintech company that provides digital payment infrastructure, not traditional banking services. Its core business is moving money safely and quickly across different payment systems. It acts as a bridge between international money transfer companies, banks, mobile money operators, and digital wallets.

In practical terms, if a Ghanaian in the UK or US wanted to send money home, Zeepay's technology helped to deliver those funds directly into the recipient's mobile money wallet. No bank visits. No queues. No paperwork. Think of Zeepay as the "digital highway" that lets money travel between different financial systems.

Zeepay is not a bank

Some may think that Zeepay operated like a commercial bank. It didn’t.

Banks accept deposits, lend money, create credit, and offer a wide range of services under banking laws. Zeepay's primary role is facilitating payments and remittances using technology. It provides infrastructure, not banking services. This distinction matters because different types of financial institutions face different regulatory requirements.

Zeepay is not a mobile money operator

Another common mix-up: Zeepay doesn't operate like MTN Mobile Money or Telecel Cash. While all operate in Ghana's digital payments space, they serve different functions.

MTN MoMo, Telecel cash and AT cash are consumer-facing platforms where customers open wallets, store electronic money, and make transfers or payments. Zeepay specializes in connecting payment systems - it works behind the scenes. In many cases, customers receive money through mobile money without realizing Zeepay's infrastructure helped make it happen.

The problem Zeepay solved

Before mobile money, receiving money from abroad meant travelling to a bank, waiting in long queues, completing paperwork, and collecting cash. For rural communities, this process was particularly difficult.

Zeepay recognized that mobile money could transform remittances. Instead of collecting cash at a bank, recipients could receive funds instantly on their phones and immediately use them to pay bills, buy goods, transfer money, or withdraw from a nearby agent. This innovation made remittances faster, more convenient, and more accessible.

Why remittances matter

Remittances are a major source of foreign exchange and household income in Ghana. Millions of Ghanaians abroad send money home to support education, healthcare, housing, family upkeep, and business investment. According to the World Bank, remittance inflows have grown significantly over the past decade. Digital platforms like Zeepay have played a key role in making these transfers more efficient.

How Zeepay grew

Zeepay was founded in 2014 by Andrew Takyi-Appiah, after gathering over 15 years of experience in banking and business development, having worked with some very reputable corporate brands across Europe, North America and Africa.

Zeepay expanded rapidly through partnerships with international remittance companies, banks, and mobile network operators. It attracted investment from development finance institutions and impact investors including Africa50, Oikocredit, Verdant Capital and Investisseurs & Partenaires (I&P). Those investments helped finance regional expansion and strengthen its payment infrastructure. By 2025, Zeepay had raised about US$42 million and established partnerships across Africa, Europe, and the Caribbean.

The company created over 220 direct jobs and supported thousands of indirect livelihoods. It became one of the few Ghanaian fintech firms to attract substantial foreign investment, demonstrating international confidence in Ghana's digital payments sector.

Why the story matters

Zeepay's significance lies in what it represented. The company became a symbol of Ghana's growing fintech ecosystem - proof that local innovation could address practical challenges while attracting global capital. For many young entrepreneurs, Zeepay showed that a company founded in Ghana could compete regionally and secure backing from international investors.

That's why recent regulatory developments have drawn widespread attention. They raise bigger questions about financial regulation, consumer protection, innovation, and investor confidence in Ghana's digital economy.

In Part 2, we'll explore what led to the licence revocation and what it means for Ghana's fintech future.

Ghana News.title: Notorious drug cartel leader Ismael Zambada sentenced to life in US prison
Ghana News.content:
One of the most notorious figures in Mexico's drug cartels, Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, will spend the rest of his life in prison, a US judge ruled has ruled, two years after Zambada was lured to the US in an elaborate sting operation.

The 76-year-old founded the violent Sinaloa Cartel, long the most powerful criminal organisation in Mexico, with Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzmán.

In 2024, El Chapo's son led Zambada to believe they were travelling to northern Mexico to inspect clandestine airstrips, when their plane instead landed in Texas and he was arrested.

Last year, Zambada reached a plea deal and admitted to drug smuggling and conspiracy charges in exchange for avoiding the death penalty.

On Monday, US District Judge Brian Cogan sentenced Zambada during a hearing in Brooklyn federal court. His guilty plea carried a mandatory term of life in prison, Reuters reported.

El Chapo's son, Joaquin Guzmán Lopez, was also arrested in July 2024 and has pleaded guilty to federal drug charges. He has yet to be sentenced.

In the plea deal, Zambada officially accepted his role in creating the vast criminal network which has sent huge amounts of cocaine and other drugs into the US since he co-founded the Sinaloa Cartel at the end of the 1980s.

Prosecutors argued in a sentencing memo that Zambada "was one of the most-if not the most-prolific and powerful narcotraffickers in the world", according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

The Sinaloa Cartel has been at war with itself since Zambada was taken into custody and has wreaked mayhem across the Mexican state of Sinaloa. Hundreds of people have been reported missing during fighting between its two rival factions.

Violence and bloodletting also shook the cartel after El Chapo was arrested and extradited to the US in 2016, as factions wrestled for control of territory while fighting off opposing drug gangs who sensed weakness. He is also serving life in prison.

One of the issues that has arisen since Zambada agreed to plead guilty has been where he will serve his sentence.

He has requested to be sent to a prison hospital, saying he will need medical care for age-related health issues.

Federal prosecutors, though, are seeking a higher-level of incarceration, contending Zambada still poses a security threat while beyond bars and could continue to direct illegal drug operations.

The federal Bureau of Prisons will make the final decision about where he resides.

On his first day back in office, US President Donald Trump announced he would increase pressure on Mexico and the cartels, including designating the criminal enterprises terrorist groups. The US also accused the governor of Sinaloa of conspiring with cartel drug traffickers.

The Mexican government, too, has taken more aggressive steps against the cartels and sent thousands of troops to Sinaloa.

Ghana News.title: Police block thousands of ‘cockroach’ protesters marching on India’s parliament
Ghana News.content:
Thousands of supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led protest movement, took to the streets of Delhi, defying a police ban to march to parliament and demand the resignation of India's education minister.

Police blocked the march with barricades, sparking scuffles as protesters tried to push through. Several demonstrators said they had been injured in baton-charges. The police did not comment.

The march followed weeks of protests over alleged exam paper leaks, which supporters say reflect a wider education system crisis.

The movement has since broadened into one of the most visible expressions of public dissent against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government in recent years.

It gathered fresh momentum over the weekend after police forcibly moved activist Sonam Wangchuk into hospital on the 21st day of a hunger strike in support of the movement. His wife says his fast continues. On Monday, Wangchuk appealed to doctors to discharge him so he could join the march but was not allowed.

The movement takes its name from a remark by India's chief justice, who drew criticism after comparing sections of unemployed young people to "cockroaches" during a court hearing.

Although police had made clear protesters would not be given permission to march to parliament, tens of thousands of students, parents, teachers and professionals gathered from early morning at Jantar Mantar, a 300-year-old observatory in central Delhi, and remained there despite heavy rain.

The contrast between the protest site and the security outside was striking. Young people draped in Indian flags queued for food, painted placards and posed for photographs, while rows of police and paramilitary personnel sealed every road to parliament around them.

Volunteers handed out food and water, patriotic songs blared from loudspeakers and organisers repeatedly urged supporters not to confront police if they were stopped.

As the march began, protesters spilled onto the streets before being halted at successive barricades. Many sat on the road waving flags and shouting slogans.

Others broke away in smaller groups, trying to reach parliament through narrow side streets.

Inside parliament, meanwhile, the opening day of the monsoon session was repeatedly adjourned as opposition MPs protested over the alleged paper leak and other issues.

As police pushed back groups trying to breach the barricades, the first reports of injuries began to emerge.

Some protesters returned to Jantar Mantar bleeding from the head or limping, while others were carried back by fellow demonstrators. Authorities also suspended mobile internet services in parts of central Delhi, leaving many without reliable access to messaging apps or social media.

"We've treated at least 10 people," volunteer doctor Gaurish Batra told the BBC while bandaging the head of a man whose shirt collar was soaked in blood. A woman with a suspected broken leg was also brought in for treatment.

Both alleged they had been injured in police baton charges. The BBC has contacted Delhi Police for comment.

By early afternoon, two CJP representatives met Health Minister JP Nadda after waiting outside his residence for about two hours.

According to CJP spokesperson Saurav Das, they submitted a letter setting out the group's demands. Das said Nadda assured them he would raise the matter within the government.

Shortly after, Nadda posted on X, urging protesters to end their demonstration and help restore "normalcy" in the capital.

Neither the meeting, nor the statement, did much to ease tensions. Thousands remained at Jantar Mantar, hoping they would eventually be allowed to continue the march.

When the rain arrived, it barely interrupted the protest. Volunteers stretched blue tarpaulins over small groups as chants continued and soaked demonstrators waited for news from the police barricades.

Among those who had travelled to Delhi was commercial pilot Samrat Khanna, who said he had swapped flying duties to attend the march.

"I felt I had to be here," he said. "I couldn't just watch from the sidelines."

Many others expressed similar feelings. For them, the alleged exam paper leaks had become less the movement's only cause than the catalyst for broader frustrations over jobs, opportunity, transparency and accountability.

Those frustrations are at the heart of the rise of the Cockroach Janta Party, or CJP, founded by Dipke.

Although the chief justice later withdrew the comment, Dipke embraced the label, turning the cockroach into the movement's symbol.

Monday's turnout reflected how quickly the movement has grown since its first protest in June, when it was little more than a fledgling online campaign. Since then, it has spread to cities across India, drawing support from students, professionals, activists and opposition politicians.

By evening, however, the mood had shifted.

Police in riot gear entered Jantar Mantar and announced over loudspeakers that protesters no longer had permission to remain. Officers then began pushing people back, prompting some demonstrators to flee while others linked arms and refused to leave.

There was also brief confusion over Dipke's whereabouts after the CJP initially said he had been detained. The group later clarified that police had attempted to take him into custody but protesters had prevented it. Delhi Police later denied the claims, calling the allegations "entirely false".

Ghana News.title: West Africa signs off $25bn mega gas-pipeline plan
Ghana News.content:
One of Africa's most ambitious energy infrastructure projects has finally been signed off at the highest level, with West African leaders formally endorsing the long-awaited Nigeria-Morocco Atlantic Gas Pipeline.

"Don't be surprised when the gas comes your way," quipped Julius Maada Bio, Sierra Leone's president and the current head of West Africa regional bloc Ecowas, following Sunday evening's ceremony in Freetown.

The vast 6,000km (3,700 miles) pipeline will run along the Atlantic coast of 14 African nations, carrying Nigerian gas to Morocco before linking into Europe's existing gas network via Spain.

Construction is expected to begin in 2028 with a total estimated cost of $25bn (£19bn).

It signals a change from current models where gas is typically extracted from African nations, refined and processed abroad then shipped back to African nations at three or four times the price, says energy expert and former Nigerian government advisor Charles Majomi.

That practice must end, because it is a "complete devaluation of the resource that is so fortunately endowed in places like Nigeria and other countries," he told BBC Focus on Africa.

By contrast, if leveraged correctly, the new pipeline has the potential not just to stimulate regional industrial growth but also boost Africa's power on the international stage.

"In terms of Africa's regional security and its ability to negotiate and have a seat at the global table, if you will, it does need this measure of usefulness to countries [in] Europe and Asia potentially," argued Majomi.

"Beyond energy security, it will open up Africa as a corridor to international markets," Prof Ganiyat Adejoke Adesina-Uthman, of the National Open University of Nigeria, said.

It is a symbol of what Africa can achieve when countries collaborate and work together, she added.

If all goes to plan a whopping 30bn cubic metres of gas per year will pass through the Nigeria-Morocco Atlantic Gas Pipeline serving 400 million consumers - making this one of the world's longest offshore gas pipelines and reshaping West Africa's energy landscape.

Sunday's agreement follows roughly a decade of negotiations involving more than a dozen countries. It establishes the legal and governance framework for the pipeline and is widely seen as the last major political hurdle before financing and construction decisions.

While construction has not yet begun, the project has entered a more advanced political and technical phase than at any point since it was first proposed in 2016.

The project is expected to be built in phases over several years rather than all at once, with analysts telling the BBC it will not begin in Nigeria because the country was initially flagged as a potential stumbling block.

"The plan is finance the project in segments starting with the Morocco-Mauritania-Senegal axis, then moving to the Ghana-Côte d'Ivoire axis... then the final connection would be to Nigeria which would then provide the gas," Majomi said.

Unlike the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline through Niger and Algeria, this Atlantic route largely avoids the Sahel's most insecure regions, although offshore construction significantly increases costs.

Feasibility studies are said to be complete, as are the front-end engineering design (FEED) studies. And the route that the pipelines will pass through have largely been agreed.

Financing may prove stickier - the projected $25bn cost could be pushed up by inflation, plus the success of a project of this scale relies on all 13 member nations (plus the disputed territory of Western Sahara) playing their part to protect the infrastructure from attacks.

"Whether or not a country will go into default on their off-take obligations for that gas as it moves [through] will be measured by their ability to muster security and integrate the host communities in helping to defend these long, long lines of gas pipelines. I think also leveraging the use drones and aerial monitoring situations will also come to bear," argues Majomi.

Nigeria's state oil firm and Morocco's national mining body are jointly leading the pipeline project. Regional institutions supporting the initiative include Ecowas, the ⁠Islamic Development Bank and ⁠the Opec Fund for International Development.

Beyond exports to Europe, it is intended to supply natural gas to countries that currently rely on expensive imported fuels, potentially supporting new power generation, fertiliser plants, petrochemical industries and manufacturing along the Atlantic coast.

For Nigeria, it offers an opportunity to monetise its vast gas reserves while strengthening economic ties across West Africa and North Africa.

Despite strong political momentum, significant obstacles remain. ⁠Financing the project and securing the pipeline route as well as ensuring political stability across participating countries will pose major challenges even before construction can advance.

Other challenges include the problem of long offshore engineering sections, plus the competition from other export routes - including liquified natural gas (LNG) projects and the Nigeria-Algeria Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline.

Beyond all of these, is the questions over future European gas demand as the continent accelerates its transition to renewable energy.

"Nigeria has the gas and there's market access from Morocco to Europe. It's not just a extracting energy, it will lead to access to clean energy for many countries with Morocco is a gateway," says an optimistic Prof Adesina-Uthman.

"It will also create industries, job opportunity and ultimately a global market. It's not just for regional integration but a global project."

Ghana News.title: NPP accuses government of using Wontumi conviction to divert attention from national challenges
Ghana News.content:
The General Secretary of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP), Justin Frimpong Kodua, has accused the government of using the conviction of the party's Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, as a distraction from what he described as Ghana's more pressing national challenges.

Addressing a press conference following Chairman Wontumi's conviction and sentencing by the Accra High Court on Monday, July 20, Mr Kodua argued that no government should use criminal prosecutions to create what he called "the appearance of success" while critical issues confronting the country remain unresolved.

His comments came after the Criminal Division of the Accra High Court sentenced Chairman Wontumi to 20 years' imprisonment over illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

The court also imposed a fine of 10,000 penalty units, equivalent to GH¢120,000, with a default custodial sentence of three years should the fine remain unpaid.

Speaking to journalists, Mr Kodua said the government ought to concentrate on addressing the country's most urgent challenges rather than, in his view, relying on selective prosecutions to project success in the fight against illegal mining.

"No Government should attempt to divert public attention from those pressing national concerns through selective prosecutions designed to create the appearance of success," he said.

According to the NPP General Secretary, Ghanaians expect leadership that is focused on solving the country's economic, environmental and security challenges rather than pursuing what he characterised as politically motivated legal actions.

Mr Kodua argued that Ghana is currently facing a range of serious challenges requiring urgent attention from the government.

He cited the continued destruction caused by illegal mining, particularly its impact on cocoa farms, farming communities and the environment, as one of the issues demanding sustained national action.

The NPP General Secretary also referred to recent flooding in parts of the country, expressing concern over what he described as an inadequate government response to affected communities.

In addition, he highlighted growing security concerns and the increasing threat of terrorism within the West African sub-region, insisting that these matters should remain at the forefront of the government's agenda.

According to him, citizens expect decisive leadership capable of safeguarding lives, protecting livelihoods and strengthening national security.

Mr Kodua reiterated the NPP's position that Chairman Wontumi's conviction was not supported by the evidence presented during the trial.

"There is no justification for the judgment since the judge obviously ignored clear evidence exonerating Wontumi," he alleged.

The High Court nevertheless found Chairman Wontumi guilty after hearing the evidence and legal arguments presented by both the prosecution and the defence. Mr Kodua's remarks represent the party's assessment of the judgement.

Seeking to reassure party supporters, Mr Kodua said Chairman Wontumi would continue to receive the full backing of the NPP despite his conviction.

"Finally, let me assure all members of the New Patriotic Party and the good people of Ghana that Chairman Wontumi is not alone," he said.

He stressed that the party remained united behind its Ashanti Regional Chairman and would continue to support him throughout the legal process.

The NPP General Secretary disclosed that the party's legal team had already begun taking steps to challenge the High Court's decision through the appellate courts.

"Our legal team has already commenced the necessary steps to challenge this judgment through the appellate process," he announced.

The appeal is expected to seek a review of both the conviction and the sentence imposed on Chairman Wontumi.

Mr Kodua stated that the NPP considers Chairman Wontumi to be a "political prisoner".

"The NPP considers Wontumi a political prisoner," he declared.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
