The protest was launched by the CJP over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak and examination irregularities. Thousands of demonstrators attempted to march towards Parliament on Monday, but security personnel stopped them near Parliament Street, leading to clashes and the use of tear gas and lathi-charge to disperse the crowd.

World.title: 4 Indians killed, 1 critically injured after cargo ship attacked off Ukraine's Odesa coast
World.content:
Smoke rises from a vessel on fire, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine in Odesa.

Attack on Indian-crewed vessel

Black Sea tensions rise

NEW DELHI: At least four Indian nationals were killed and one was critically injured after the commercial vessel MV Golden Leo came under attack while departing Ukraine's port of Odesa on the evening of July 19, the ministry of external affairs said on Monday.In a statement, the MEA said there were 17 crew members on board the vessel, including five Indian nationals, when the attack took place."As per information available, four Indian nationals have tragically lost their lives, while one is hospitalized in a critical condition. Our Mission in Ukraine is closely monitoring the situation and is making every effort to extend all possible assistance to those affected," the ministry said.The MEA expressed its condolences to the families of those killed and wished the injured Indian national a speedy recovery."We extend our deepest condolences to the families of the deceased Indian nationals and wish the injured Indian national a speedy and full recovery," it said.The ministry condemned the attack, saying commercial shipping and civilian crew members should not be targeted."India condemns such attacks and reiterates that targeting commercial shipping and endangering innocent civilian crew members, or otherwise impeding freedom of navigation and commerce, is deplorable and should be avoided," the ministry said.According to Ukrainian authorities, the MV Golden Leo, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship carrying corn, was struck by three Russian cruise missiles shortly after departing the port of Odesa on Sunday. The vessel was reportedly manned by a crew from India and Syria, according to Reuters.The strike triggered a fire on board and led to an overnight search-and-rescue operation. Ukrainian officials said several crew members were killed, while others were rescued. A Reuters witness in Odesa also reported seeing smoke billowing from the vessel off the coast.The vessel is owned by Mumbai-based Ocean Grace Shipping Ltd, according to LSEG data.The attack comes amid renewed fighting in the Black Sea, a crucial shipping route for Ukrainian grain exports. After commercial shipping resumed under arrangements aimed at easing global food supply concerns following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, both Russia and Ukraine have recently stepped up attacks on ports, cargo vessels and maritime infrastructure.Ukraine has accused Russia of intensifying strikes on its deepwater ports and commercial ships, while Russia says it has targeted fuel storage facilities and infrastructure linked to Ukraine's military operations. The renewed attacks have raised fresh concerns over the safety of commercial shipping and global grain supplies, as both countries remain among the world's leading grain exporters.

World.title: 'No prima facie case': HC rejects plea of Mamata Banerjee faction to operate TMC accounts worth Rs 440 crore
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Calcutta high court on Monday refused interim relief to the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the

(TMC), rejecting its plea to operate three party bank accounts frozen by the

(ED).

Finding no prima facie case in favour of the petitioners, Justice Krishna Rao dismissed the request for interim relief.

The court directed the ED to file its affidavit-in-opposition within three weeks, after which the petitioners will have two weeks to submit their reply, if any. The matter will be heard again on August 26.

The ED had earlier frozen the three bank accounts, which collectively held Rs 440.42 crore, as part of a money laundering probe linked to an FIR registered by the West Bengal Police over alleged dishonest financial transactions, unlawful collection of funds, and suspected routing of money through certain party accounts.

Justice Rao also observed that the ED's freezing order, issued on July 7, was not brought to the notice of a coordinate bench headed by Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya. The court noted that neither the state nor the petitioners informed the bench about the order, as the central agency was not a party to the earlier proceedings.

On July 9, Justice Bhattacharyya had appointed a special officer to facilitate the operation of the three accounts by the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the TMC for day-to-day and legal expenses.





The petitioners had approached the court challenging the ED's initiation of an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR), the equivalent of an FIR, in the matter.

According to ED officials, the agency's preliminary investigation found that around Rs 160 crore was transferred from TMC bank accounts to Carewell Aviation India Pvt. Ltd. and its related entity between April 2023 and June 2026.

The company allegedly routed Rs 82.96 crore to another newly incorporated entity during the same period, officials claimed.

Investigators found that a "significant" amount was transferred to the entity, of which Rs 112 crore was allegedly used to purchase an Embraer Legacy 600 business jet and an AgustaWestland 109SP helicopter, officials added.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Who will ask if you’re home? The economy growing around urban loneliness
World.content:
From joint family to flat

The silver economy

The business of being heard

The small economies of a lonely weekend

Who will pay for connection?

India is the second-loneliest country in the world, according to a study by JB.com. The ranking offers a stark lens through which to view a country that is also aging rapidly, urbanising quickly and watching its traditional social structures thin out.In 2011, India had about 100 million people aged 60 and above. Projections by the Technical Group on Population Projections, cited in the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementationâs report Elderly in India 2021, show that this figure will more than double to roughly 230 million by 2036, around 15 per cent of the population. By 2050, UNFPAâs India Ageing Report 2023 estimates, nearly one in five Indians will be 60 or older.But loneliness is not waiting for old age.It is already present in the rented flats of young migrants, in the quiet of a single-person home, in weekends spent scrolling through other people's lives and in the small, almost invisible moments when there is no one to ask, âAre you home?âFor Minal, from Bihar and living alone in Pune, loneliness is âfeeling I donât belong anywhere and nobody cares about me.â She calls herself âpretty socialâ, but in her current city âhas only few people I know so I have phases when I go out alone.âA typical weekend is split between âone day I go out to eat somewhere nice and one day I stay in, cook something and journal or watch a movie.âAt home, she spends â8â10 hoursâ on screens. After closing Instagram and seeing peers travelling or getting engaged, she says she feels âempty and restless and also shit about myselfâ.Swadha, who spent years living alone in Noida for college and work, remembers the strange contradiction of returning home.âThere is a sense of reliefâ¦ but then there is also a sense of silence and nobody is there to ask are you homeâ¦ nobody cares whether you entered with the shoe on or have you left the shoe outside.âShe placed a mirror at the entrance of her home. âSomebody has to look at me, right? I used to do that for myself.âLiving alone, she says, âmeans you have absolutely no one to talk to about your dayâ¦ that will hit you so hard that it will push you away from your loved ones whom you actually speak to on the calls.âFor Neha, from West Bengal and working in Delhi, loneliness is even simpler: âno person to go back to when you feel heavyâ¦ no one to ask where you areâ¦ how have you been.âShe says she has âno social lifeâ. Her weekends are spent âgrocery shoppingâ¦ cooking and cleaningâ¦â. When she returns home, her first thought is, âwhat should I eat now.â She estimates her screen time at 4â5 hours a day at home and says that after closing social apps, she feels, âIâm wasting my timeâ¦ I should do something productive.âTheir lives may seem far removed from the concerns of India's elderly. But the emotional patterns are strikingly similar.A LASI-based study on later life reports that about 13.4 per cent of older Indians experience frequent loneliness. The odds are higher among those not in a marital union, those with more than two chronic conditions and those with small social networks or limited leisure activities. UNFPAâs 2023 report identifies social isolation and loneliness as key stressors on elderly mental health, aggravated by migration, urbanisation and weakening family support.The country is aging into this crisis.India's elderly population is not evenly distributed. Kerala's elderly share is projected to rise from about 13 per cent in 2011 to nearly 23 per cent by 2036, while Uttar Pradesh moves from roughly 7 per cent to 12 per cent. Southern states, Himachal Pradesh and Punjab already have above-average elderly proportions, creating pockets where ageing, and the risk of isolation, are much more intense than the national average.The profile is also sharply gendered.Using LASI data, government summaries note a sex ratio of roughly 1,065 females per 1,000 males among Indiaâs elderly, with women making up about 58 per cent of older persons. More than half of elderly women are widows. UNFPAâs ageing reports underline that older women are more likely to be widowed, have little personal income and live alone, increasing their vulnerability to economic insecurity and social isolation.This is the demographic stage on which India's loneliness economy is emerging.For generations, the family was India's first social safety net. That safety net has not disappeared, but it has changed shape.Migration, urbanisation, nuclear families and precarious work have moved millions away from the people and communities that once filled everyday life. A home that once had several generations may now have one person, one phone and a delivery app.The coping mechanisms are increasingly mediated by markets. Food delivery replaces the shared meal. OTT platforms fill the evening. Social media offers constant contact without necessarily providing companionship.For younger Indians, these services are conveniences. For an ageing population, they are becoming part of a much larger ecosystem of care.Policy has increasingly framed this demographic transition as an economic opportunity. NITI Aayogâs report Senior Care Reforms in India and the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowermentâs schemes speak of a âsilver economyâ built around the needs of older adults.Government estimates linked to the Senior Care Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE) initiative put the value of Indiaâs silver economy at around Rs 73,000 crore in 2024, with scope for multi-fold expansion as the elderly population grows.The first pillar is financial security.Atal Pension Yojana subscriptions rose from about 1.54 crore in March 2019 to 8.27 crore by October 2025, according to Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority data quoted in government briefs. Assets under management crossed Rs 49,000 crore.The Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme reaches around 2.21 crore beneficiaries, offering Rs 200 a month to those aged 60â79 and Rs 500 to those 80 and above. The amounts are modest, but they establish an income floor that can help with food, healthcare and basic services.The second pillar is health protection.Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY offers Rs 5 lakh a year in hospitalisation cover to vulnerable households. In October 2024, the government announced free treatment benefits of up to Rs 5 lakh annually for about 6 crore senior citizens aged 70 and above from 4.5 crore families, irrespective of socio-economic status. More than 40 lakh seniors had enrolled by January 2025.The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly, meanwhile, now covers all 713 health districts, with geriatric OPDs, wards and physiotherapy services, according to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.The third pillar is care.The SAGE portal invites start-ups to develop solutions in healthcare, housing, technology and social engagement, offering equity support of up to Rs 1 crore per project, with government equity capped at 49 per cent. The Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens grants fund 696 senior citizen homes across 29 States and UTs, with 84 more selected for 2025â26.A geriatric caregiver training scheme, run through 32 empanelled institutes, trained 36,785 caregivers in 2023â24.None of these programmes is explicitly called a loneliness programme. Yet they address many of the conditions that make loneliness more likely: widowhood, frailty, financial insecurity and living alone.Technology is becoming another layer of this support system.The government's e-Sanjeevani telemedicine platform has delivered nearly 14 crore tele-consultations nationwide, including more than 1 crore consultations involving senior citizens, according to a 2023 Press Information Bureau update and a national telemedicine assessment.For an older person who cannot easily travel, a consultation through a screen can be a lifeline. But the broader shift is significant too: an increasing number of needs, including emotional ones, are now being addressed through digital interfaces.Elderline 14567 offers senior citizens a telephone channel for grievances, abuse and emotional support, connecting callers to local services and authorities.The legal framework, meanwhile, continues to place responsibility on families. The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, and its 2019 amendment bill expand the definition of âchildrenâ and âparentsâ, remove the Rs 10,000 cap on maintenance, mandate that seniors should live a âlife of dignityâ and require dedicated police units and geriatric facilities in hospitals.The amendment widens âmaintenanceâ to include healthcare, safety and housing. It is an acknowledgement that neglect, isolation and abuse are not merely private tragedies.But loneliness is not always about being physically alone.Anandeshwar, a civil services aspirant from Uttar Pradesh now living in Delhi, describes it as ânot being understood or connected to the people around me, even when I am surrounded by others.âHe has âa big enough circle of friendsâ but meets them rarely. Deeper conversations happen âpine ke baadâ (after drinking). His ideal weekend is full: âwrite some good things, spend time with friends, participate in debating eventsâ. Reality is often different. He stays home, âwatch YT, Twitter, or just lay on the bed smoking,â joking that âevery day is weakened for an unemployed.âThe problem, then, is not simply the absence of people. It is the absence of meaningful connection.Loneliness often reveals itself through small choices.Cook or order in? Call someone or scroll? Go out or stay in bed?Minal divides her weekend between eating out and cooking at home. Neha's ideal weekend is âreading, writing and cleaning the flatâ, even if reality is often errands and rest.Yukta, a psychology student from Bengaluru living in Jaipur, describes a more connected version of the same urban life. When she is not overwhelmed by work, weekends with her roommate mean âsleep, cooking and eating good food together, watching something fun on an OTT platform, orâ¦ a movie and cafe date! And shopping or just strolling through a bazaar for fun.ââNow, it feels like âI am finally homeâ,â she says. âI can do whatever Iâd like, be whatever Iâd like and just exist in a space with only comfort to offer.âLASI-based studies identify regular social contact, leisure activities, yoga or meditation and even moderate television or computer use as factors associated with better wellbeing among older adults.The difference is that in cities such as Delhi, Pune, Hyderabad and Jaipur, these activities are increasingly curated through markets: OTT subscriptions, cafes, delivery services and paid experiences.At the other end is Srabastee from West Bengal, living in Delhi for work.âItâs feeling like no one really knows whatâs going on in your head, even when youâre surrounded by peopleâ¦ when you have something exciting or heartbreaking to share and canât think of anyone to call.âShe speaks to family and âtexts a few friends once in a whileâ, mostly sharing memes and reacting to stories. Weeks can pass before they meet.After scrolling, she often feels âdrainedâ, comparing her routine weekends of laundry, shows and ordered food with peers who seem to be âgetting promoted, buying homes, getting married, travelling the world.âThe same platforms that offer entertainment and convenience also fuel comparison. The same screens that connect people can deepen the feeling of being left behind.NITI Aayog argues that senior care needs to be recognised as a distinct sector, with regulations, standards, public-private partnerships and dedicated financing. Its vision combines public programmes such as pensions, NPHCE, telehealth and senior homes with private start-ups and NGOs.That is where the silver economy begins to overlap with the loneliness economy.The forces making Minal, Neha and Srabastee feel alone, migration, nuclear families, precarious jobs and digital overload, are also creating demand for therapy platforms, senior-living communities, companion-care services and digital communities.Some of these services may offer genuine support. Others may simply monetise a need that was once met by family, neighbours and community.The question becomes sharper when viewed against India's place near the top of the global loneliness index. A country ranked number two by JB.com is also preparing for a dramatic rise in its elderly population. By 2036, roughly 230 million Indians will be 60 or older. By 2050, nearly one in five will be.The challenge is not only how to feed, house or medically care for this population. It is also how to ensure that people have someone to talk to, someone who notices when they do not come home, someone who asks how their day was.India's loneliness economy is already taking shape, from pensions and senior homes to helplines, telehealth, therapy platforms, cafes, OTT subscriptions and delivery apps.The question is whether connection will ultimately be treated as a public responsibility or sold as another subscription.Because the people who today spend their Sundays between grocery stores and glowing screens will one day grow old. And the way India responds to their loneliness will reveal whether it sees the need to be seen, heard and remembered as a basic human need, or simply another market waiting to be tapped.

World.title: Kolkata Chai announces tie-up with Bungalow Hospitality Investments
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Kolkata Chai, the New Yorkâborn chai brand that helped introduce authentic Indian chai to large US audiences, announced a strategic partnership and investment with Bungalow Hospitality Investments, the newly formed venture coâfounded by Michelinâstarred chef

and restaurateur Jimmy Rizvi.

The deal, announced Monday, includes a financial investment in Kolkata Chai and an exclusive menu integration across Bungalow Hospitality Managementâs New York City restaurant portfolio. Beginning this summer, Kolkata Chaiâs signature Masala Chai will be rolled out at the groupâs current and upcoming restaurants, including GupShup and the forthcoming Punjab Meet House. The partnership will also produce a series of limitedâtime collaborative menu items this fall.

Kolkata Chai was founded in 2019 by brothers Ayan and Ani Sanyal and has grown through a multiâunit cafÃ© model and a line of consumer packaged goods (CPG) chai blends. In 2024, actor and comedian Hasan Minhaj joined the company as an investor and business partner, helping expand the brandâs visibility through media and cultural storytelling.

Bungalow Hospitality Investments, led by Khanna and Rizvi, focuses on investing in and partnering with emerging food and hospitality brands.





Kolkata Chai is the groupâs inaugural investment; Khanna cited a personal connection to chai and longstanding admiration for the brandâs craft and authenticity as factors in the decision.

âChef Vikas Khanna is a pioneer for Indian cuisine on a global stage, and having him join the Kolkata Chai family is a genuinely exciting moment for us,â said Hasan Minhaj in a statement. He added that the partnership reflects Kolkata Chaiâs role in connecting people across generations and cultures.

The announcement comes amid growing mainstream interest in South Asian food and beverage in the United States, driven by restaurant openings and a rising number of South Asian CPG brands. Kolkata Chai and Bungalow Foods, a CPG line coâfounded by Khanna and Rizvi, have both positioned themselves as leaders within that expanding market.

World.title: 'Hopefully govt will fix accountability': Sonam Wangchuk to continue his hunger strike
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Climate activist

on Monday said that that he has decided to continue his hunger strike after seeing the brutality on peaceful protestors marching to the Parliament.

In a handwritten note, Wangchuk said that the his hunger strike will continue until Cockroach Janata Party leaders are allowed to meet MPs at the Parliament or he is allowed to meet them at Safdarjung Hospital.

"Seeing the brutality with which peacefully protesting Youth are being dealt with, I have decided to continue my fast until the youth leaders are allowed to meet the Parliamentarians at the Sansad Bhawan or I am allowed to meet them here at the Hospital," Wangchuk said.

"Hopefully government will fix accountability of Education minister before that," he added.

He also appealed to the government and Delhi Police to allow the protesting students to present their grievances before the Parliament.

"I am touched & moved by how the youth have held on to peace despite provocation and I appeal to the Govt & Police force to resolve the issue by simply allowing the students to present their grievances before the Parliament today or tomorrow," Wangchuk said.

"I'm sure the young protesters will show the same patience and tolerance tomorrow as they did today," he added.

This comes hours after a delegation of CJP met Union minister JP Nadda and submitted its petition demanding accountability from the government over the NEET-UG paper leak case.





According to CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka, the meeting with Nadda was under way, with the Union minister seeking time to consult the government leadership on the party's demands.

The demands include the immediate release of activist Sonam Wangchuk, the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, and Rs 1 crore compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide.

This comes as thousands tried to march to Parliament as part of the Cockroach Janta Party's protest call to demand the former's resignation over alleged examination irregularities.

Outside Parliament, police used tear gas and mild force after demonstrators allegedly attempted to breach barricades and march towards the Parliament complex. Several protesters were detained.

Security was tightened across central Delhi, with Rapid Action Force personnel deployed at key locations to prevent any breach. As a precautionary measure, several gates at Metro stations in the area were temporarily closed, affecting commuters.

At least seven CJP protesters, including Abhijeet Dipke, were detained near the Reserve Bank of India, close to Parliament, during the party's 'Sansad Chalo' march, PTI reported.

World.title: DS Group launches Pallu Protection PPE to shield women farmers from pesticide exposure
World.content:
DS Group has launched an initiative to reduce occupational health risks faced by women farmers from exposure to agricultural pesticides and chemicals, rolling out awareness activities and a culturally tailored protective solution in seven villages of Baghpat district.

The programme, part of the companyâs FarmHER initiative, is currently being implemented in Pali, Katha, Bandpur, Sunehra, Basi, Mavikala and Sankrodh. It combines community education, preventive health services and distribution of a practical protective product designed for women who commonly use saree pallus or dupattas while working in the fields.

As part of the campaign, DS Group introduced a washable nano-fibre filter â marketed as the Pallu Protection Equipment (PPE) filter â that can be stitched into a saree pallu or dupatta to act as a barrier against pesticide particles, dust, harmful chemicals and PM2.5 pollutants.

The filters will be made available free of charge through selected tailor shops, pesticide outlets and chemist stores across the seven villages.

The company said the intervention was informed by field research which found many women already use pallus or dupattas as informal protection, despite their limited effectiveness. A male version of the product, designed to be integrated into the traditional gamcha, has also been developed.





DS Groupâs outreach in the villages includes mobile awareness vans, traditional puppet shows, nukkad nataks (street plays), door-to-door education and free health camps. The health camps provide blood pressure and blood sugar screening, basic counselling and distribution of PPE masks. Women participating in the programme also receive mirrors and calendars bearing messages about safer farming practices.

âWomen farmers play a vital role in Indiaâs agricultural economy, yet awareness of the occupational health risks they face remains limited,â said Rajeev Jain, Senior Vice President, Corporate Marketing, DS Group. âOur field research revealed that the saree pallu and dupatta are often used as informal protective coverings during pesticide-intensive agricultural work, despite offering inadequate protection.

This highlights the urgent need for simple, practical and culturally appropriate solutions that women farmers can seamlessly adopt.â

DS Group said the initiative aims to bridge the gap between awareness and action by providing accessible, culturally relevant interventions to protect womenâs health and encourage safer, more sustainable farming practices as part of its broader FarmHER programme.

World.title: Trainee IPS officer, accused of sexual harassment by colleague, hospitalised after suspected suicide attempt
World.content:
Representative image

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: A trainee IPS officer, who was booked for allegedly stalking and sexually harassing a fellow trainee at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy (SVPNPA) in Hyderabad, was hospitalised on Monday following a suspected suicide attempt, police said.According to a doctor who treated him, the trainee officer was brought to a private hospital in an unconscious state by his brother and friends, who suspected that he had consumed a harmful substance.The doctor added that a stomach wash was performed, but no "abnormal" substance was found.The trainee officer's blood and urine samples have been sent for tests, while his vital parameters remain stable.Although he was unconscious when brought to the hospital, he is now drowsy. The doctor added that further details would emerge after he regains full consciousness and the test reports are received.An alcohol bottle and a sanitizer bottle were found near his bed, according to the doctor, who cited the trainee officer's brother.The case stems from a complaint filed by a 30-year-old woman trainee IPS officer, who accused her fellow trainee of stalking and sexually harassing her. She alleged that he had been sending sexually abusive messages through an instant messaging app since June 23 and making derogatory remarks about her in front of her colleagues.The complainant claimed that the officer falsely accused her of having a relationship with another trainee and pressured her to admit to it, while using abusive language.She further alleged that on July 9, he restrained her, took her to his room by force, pulled her hair, attempted to strangle her, and held a knife to her neck, preventing her from leaving. She also accused him of assaulting her the following day.The woman alleged that the officer recorded a private video of her without consent and sent it to her husband in an attempt to blackmail her.Based on the complaint, a case was registered at Attapur police station on July 18 under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including charges related to assault or criminal force against a woman, sexual harassment, stalking, and insulting the modesty of a woman, along with provisions of the Information Technology Act, police said.The trainee IPS officer denied the allegations in a social media post, calling the complaint and rumours against him "baseless and untrue.""I fully trust the legal process and believe justice will prevail," he wrote.A police official said investigators would issue a notice asking him to appear in connection with the case.Following the registration of the case, the trainee officer left the academy, according to sources. He had earlier served as a constable in Andhra Pradesh.

World.title: 30,000 students, 1,100 seats: Delhi University’s one-year PG rollout hits a roadblock
World.content:
With more than 30,000 students graduating from Delhi University’s (DU) inaugural four-year undergraduate cohort and only a little over 1,100 seats on offer across 46 one-year postgraduate programmes, several students contend that the promised progression from the undergraduate degree to a one-year master’s has not been matched by adequate postgraduate capacity, despite having invested an additional year in pursuit of the pathway.

Introduced for the 2026-27 academic session under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the pathway allows students who have completed DU’s Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUP) under the Undergraduate Curriculum Framework (UGCF) 2022 to pursue a master’s degree in one year instead of the conventional two-year programme.

The FYUP is intended to provide greater research exposure, including the option of a bachelor’s degree with honours with research, align Indian degree structures with global higher education frameworks and create a route for eligible students to pursue a one-year master’s degree.

Several central, State and private universities have since adopted similar four-year undergraduate programmes, although implementation timelines vary.

The pathway has been introduced in addition to DU’s existing two-year postgraduate programmes, which offer around 13,500 seats across 74 disciplines.

According to the university’s information bulletin, the one-year postgraduate programmes together offer just over 1,100 seats across 46 disciplines, taking the total postgraduate intake to around 14,600 seats. Students, however, argue that the intake for the one-year pathway remains disproportionately small compared with the size of the first FYUP graduating cohort.

Protests erupt

The issue prompted student organisations to stage protests on campus, demanding an increase in the number of seats.

The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) on Friday staged a protest at the university campus (please check), demanding an increase in the intake of one-year postgraduate programmes.

ABVP Delhi secretary Sarthak Sharma said, “The university administration must immediately enhance the number of seats to ensure that no deserving student is denied access to higher education because of seat constraints.”

Aanchal Nainawat, a fourth-year student at Hansraj College, said the possibility of pursuing a one-year master’s programme was among the primary reasons she opted for the additional year.

“We spent an additional year, along with our time, money and trust, expecting the one-year master’s programme to be a genuine opportunity. Instead, we found ourselves competing for a handful of seats, and the promise we relied on simply was not matched in its implementation,” she said.

According to the information bulletin released on July 5, the one-year M.A. in English programme offers 45 seats across all reservation categories.

Aastha Upadhyay, a fourth-year B.A. English (Hons.) student at Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, said, “When the information bulletin was released, the scale of the mismatch became clear. Hundreds of students had opted for the fourth year, but the M.A. in English had only 45 seats. It fundamentally altered how we viewed the one-year master’s programme.”

Navigating uncertainty

Faculty members said that while the policy itself had merit, its implementation was marked by inadequate planning, frequent procedural changes and unclear communication, leaving both teachers and students navigating uncertainty.

Priyanka Kulhari, Assistant Professor at Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, said, “On paper, the idea is excellent. The problem began with its implementation. We were receiving new guidelines every week, and faculty members themselves were often unsure of the procedures.”

Sanchita Das, a fourth-year B.A. English (Hons.) student at Miranda House, questioned whether the university had adequately planned the transition.

“If Delhi University encouraged thousands of students to opt for the fourth year, it should have simultaneously expanded the one-year master’s programmes. The restricted intake raises serious questions about whether the rollout was planned to accommodate the students it encouraged,” she said.

Prateek Arsh, a fourth-year student at Hansraj College, questioned the transparency of the admission process.

“The issue is not just the limited number of seats, but also the lack of transparency. We were informed about important admission criteria only in the eighth semester. If the university had communicated these guidelines before students opted for the fourth year, many would have made a more informed decision,” he said.

In response to the issue, the university has constituted a six-member committee to examine requests for expanding the intake in its one-year postgraduate programmes.

A notification issued by the DU’s Registrar’s Office on Friday stated: “The university has received requests for an increase in the number of seats in the one-year postgraduate programmes being offered in various departments of the university for the academic session. The competent authority has constituted the following committee to consider the request and suggest measures for its implementation. The committee may submit its recommendations within ten days.”

World.title: IndiGo to place order for over 1,000 aircraft engines with CFM International
World.content:
The country's largest airline, IndiGo, on Monday (July 20, 2026) announced it will place an order with CFM International for more than 1,000 engines to power its 510 A320 neo family planes.

IndiGo and CFM International, an equal joint venture between GE Aerospace and Safran Aircraft Engines, have inked a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the order at the Farnborough International Airshow in the U.K.

The order for more than 1,000 LEAP-1A engines to power 510 Airbus A320 neo family aircraft will also be the "largest single order ever placed for LEAP engines and a record for CFM International," a release said on Monday (July 20).

Financial details were not disclosed.

A320 neo family planes include A320 neos, A321 neos and A321 XLRs. All are narrow-body aircraft.

CFM International would also provide extensive support to the airline in establishing its engine MRO (Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul) facility in Bengaluru.

Besides, it will provide support to the IndiGo fleet through long-term material services agreement, including supply of spare parts.

Currently, IndiGo has an operational fleet of over 400 planes and over 900 Airbus aircraft are on order.

"CFM has been a trusted partner in our growth journey since 2016, supporting a fleet that now exceeds 375 A320/321Family aircraft. The LEAP engine's industry-leading proven reliability makes it the ideal choice to support our scale, operational resilience and sustainability ambitions," IndiGo CEO Designate Willie Walsh said.

IndiGo has been a customer of CFM International for 10 years.

In 2016, the airline operated a sub-fleet of Airbus A320 ceo family aircraft powered by CFM56-5B engines and in 2019, the airline ordered LEAP-1A engines for their newest fleet of Airbus A320/321 neo family aircraft.

India is the third largest market for CFM International, with 5 Indian carriers operating more than 400 LEAP-powered aircraft and 2,000 engines on order.

GE Aerospace Chairman and CEO H Lawrence Culp, Jr said that with a strong installed base, manufacturing in Pune, a broad local supplier network, and advanced engineering in Bengaluru, we remain committed to supporting IndiGo's growth and expanding our presence in India.

"As one of the world's fastest-growing aviation markets, India is of strategic importance to Safran. Through our continued investments in the country, particularly in LEAP engine production and MRO capabilities, we are strengthening our long-term commitment to supporting IndiGo's remarkable growth and to contributing to the development of Indian aerospace industry," Safran CEO Olivier Andries said.

Meanwhile, many planes are grounded due to issues with Pratt & Whitney (P&W) engines.

Earlier in the day, Honeywell Aerospace announced that IndiGo has selected its avionics and power systems for 810 new Airbus A320 neo family aircraft that are to be delivered in the coming years.

World.title: Calcutta High Court refuses Trinamool Congress’ plea to operate bank accounts frozen by ED
World.content:
In a setback to the Trinamool Congress, the Calcutta High Court on Monday (July 20, 2026) refused the party’s plea seeking permission to operate three bank accounts containing around ₹440 crore that were frozen by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in a money laundering case involving alleged transfers of party funds for the purchase of an aircraft and a helicopter.

The Bidhannagar police had earlier frozen the same three accounts on June 19, in response to an FIR lodged by MLA Sandipan Saha, who now belongs to the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction of the Trinamool Congress. In the FIR, he alleged illegal fund diversion from those accounts.

However, on July 9, a Bench led by Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya had directed the police to let the Mamata Banerjee-led faction use money from the accounts for daily administrative purposes under the supervision of a special judicial officer.

Monday’s (July 20) order came in response to another plea filed by the Mamata Banerjee-led faction on July 10, challenging the ED’s decision to freeze the same accounts following a fresh FIR registered by the agency on July 8.

“The ED, after analysing the bank accounts of the petitioner, finds that substantial transfers of funds to various entities, most prominent being the Carewell group. The ED has not imposed a debit freeze on the other 36 accounts of the petitioner, in which an amount of ₹164 crore is lying. This Court did not find any prima facie case and balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of the petitioners. In view of the above, the interim order as prayed for by the petitioners is refused,” said the court presided over by Justice Krishna Rao.

The matter has been listed for further hearing on August 26. The court has directed the ED to file an affidavit regarding the investigation within three weeks.

The party’s 12 more bank accounts across several private and nationalised banks, containing over ₹1,000 crore, have also been frozen by the Bidhannagar Police on July 10.

World.title: Philippines accuses Chinese coast guard of injuring Filipino sailor in disputed shoal
World.content:
The Philippine military on Monday (July 20, 2026) accused China's coast guard of allegedly injuring a Filipino sailor during an incident in a disputed shoal in the South China Sea.

The military said Chinese coast guard personnel aboard a motorboat repeatedly struck the sailor on the head with a wooden baton, injuring him and damaging his smaller vessel.

The assault was captured on video by other Filipino sailors in the hotly disputed Second Thomas Shoal and set off angry condemnations by Philippine officials. They praised the Filipino navy personnel, saying they did not do anything that could have caused an escalation.

China’s coast guard responded by claiming that two rubber boats belonging to an “illegally” stationed Filipino vessel had rammed the Chinese patrol boat “in a dangerous manner.”

“During the incident, Philippine personnel maliciously attacked Chinese law enforcement personnel using oars and long sticks,” the Chinese coast guard said in a statement on social media.

The row was just the latest altercation between Chinese and Philippines personnel in disputed waters in the South China Sea, which Beijing claims virtually in its entirety. China has demanded that Manila pull away a long-marooned and now rusting navy ship, the BRP Sierra Madre, which is manned by Filipino navy personnel and serves as a fragile territorial outpost.

The Philippine military said a Chinese coast guard inflatable boat carrying eight personnel was deployed from a ship and approached the BRP Sierra Madre within close range and maneuvered around while its occupants took pictures and video.

Filipino sailors aboard two rubber boats asked the Chinese to back away in a non-confrontational manner. “The Chinese coast guard vessel personnel reacted violently and aggressively by striking a Philippine Navy personnel on the head with a wooden baton, causing injury and damaging the navy rubber boat,” the Philippine military said.

The extent of the Filipino sailor’s injury was being assessed to determine if he needed to be medically evacuated, it said.

“No act of coercion or aggression will deter us from carrying out our constitutional mandate or exercising the Philippines’ lawful rights in the West Philippine Sea,” the military said, using the Philippine name for the South China Sea.

“The latest act of violence and harassment committed by the China coast guard against Philippine navy personnel … adds to a clear pattern of provocative and hostile behavior and further contributes to the People’s Republic of China’s deficit of trust and credibility,” the Department of National Defense said in a statement.

The Chinese coast guard accused the Philippines of distorting facts by falsely accusing China, “which is a complete reversal of right and wrong,” according to its statement.

The Philippines deliberately beached the Sierra Madre in the shallows of the Second Thomas Shoal in 1999 to serve as a territorial outpost. China, which also claims the shoal, later surrounded the atoll with its ships in a tense territorial standoff that has dragged on for years.

The long-simmering territorial disputes, which also involve, Brunei, Malaysia, Vietnam and Taiwan, is high in the agenda of annual talks in Manila this week between foreign ministers of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and their Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi.

Both sides have been negotiating a nonaggression pact that aims to prevent a major armed conflict that could draw in the United States, which has vowed to help deter growing Chinese aggression and defend freedom of navigation in the busy waterway.

World.title: Madurai City Traffic Police seize 10 motorbikes as minors ride them
World.content:
Madurai City Traffic Police have seized 10 motorbikes on charges of minor children riding them without driving licence on Sunday night.

The police have booked their parents/guardians and the vehicle owners under the provisions of Motor Vehicle Act for letting children without license to ride bikes.

A statement said that based on the instruction of Commissioner of Police, S. Rajenthiran, the traffic police conducted a vehicle check on Sunday night at Tallakulam, Thilagar Thidal, Tideer Nagar, Chinthamani, South Gate, Vilakkuthoon, Anna Nagar, S.S. Colony and Teppakulam police station limits.

The statement said that parents/guardians and vehicle owners would be booked as accused under Section 199-A of Motor Vehicle Act for allowing children without driving licence to use the vehicles.

The accused could get up to three years of jail, ₹25,000 fine and suspension of vehicle registration for one year. Besides, the rider would be imposed a fine of ₹5,000.

The Commissioner has issued a stern warning against those who violate the Motor Vehicle Act.

World.title: Israelis march to Gaza border demanding re-establishment of settlements
World.content:
Thousands of Israelis, including settlers and right-wing activists, marched towards the border with Gaza on Sunday (July 19, 2026), calling on the government to re-establish Israeli settlements in the war-shattered Palestinian territory, an AFP journalist reported.

The demonstrators gathered near the border before walking in large numbers towards the fence overlooking northern Gaza, where Israeli security forces deployed to prevent participants from advancing further.

AFP footage showed marchers waving Israeli flags as soldiers and police blocked their access to the restricted area.

"We are walking today to tell the government of Israel and show all the world that this land belongs to us and that Gaza really belongs to us and that we want to go back there," said participant Daniel Sellem.

"We lived there before they got us out in 2005."

Sellem said the march was intended to push the government to authorise a return to Gaza, more than two decades after Israel evacuated all settlements from the territory under a 2005 disengagement plan.

"We are trying to put pressure on them, and I have a big hope that it will work and that we will go back and live there as soon as possible," Sellem said.

Another participant, Yechiel Greenblum, said the event marked what he viewed as "just the beginning" of a campaign to restore Israeli communities in the coastal territory.

"We are having a big march back to the Gaza Strip, back to where Jews lived for hundreds, thousands of years," he said, adding that the 2005 withdrawal had been temporary. "We are going back."

Greenblum argued that there was "no reason" Jews could not return to settle northern Gaza.

Previous marches have likewise sought to pressure the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, one of the most right-wing in the country's history, to re-establish settlements in the territory -- much of which has been rendered uninhabitable by more than two years of war.

Israeli forces currently control more than 60 percent of the Gaza Strip, where daily violence continues despite a ceasefire between Israel and Palestinian group Hamas.

World.title: SC gives Centre 4-weeks to confer gallantry award on former Madhya Pradesh cop
World.content:
The Supreme Court expressed displeasure with the Union Government on Monday (July 20, 2026) over the repeated delay in conferring the President’s Gallantry Award on a former Madhya Pradesh police officer Vivek Singh Chouhan, who gunned down two dreaded dacoits in an encounter more than two decades ago.

A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and R. Mahadevan, hearing an application filed by Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, granted the Centre time till July 29 to comply with the Madhya Pradesh High Court’s direction to confer the award on Mr. Chouhan.

“This concerns a police officer who risked his life in service. The High Court has directed the award to be conferred. What is the justification for seeking further time now?” the Bench asked.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, informed the Bench that the government had filed a review petition against the Supreme Court’s March 25 order affirming the High Court’s direction.

“We have filed a review. It is an objection in principle. If Your Lordships can consider the review, we can work it out. He may eventually get it, but not under a mandamus,” Mr. Mehta submitted.

Justice Nath questioned why the government could not comply with the direction while simultaneously pursuing its review petition.

“Why don’t you comply and then argue your review?” the Bench asked.

When the Solicitor General argued that the award could be withdrawn if the review petition succeeded, the Bench remarked, “If it is allowed, then the award will go. Why can’t you comply? Why are you making it an issue?”

Final opportunity

Accordingly, the Bench granted the Centre four weeks as the “last and final opportunity” to comply with the direction and warned that any further non-compliance would invite serious consequences.

“We are granting four weeks as the last and final opportunity. If the award is not conferred within this period, the Home Secretary will have to appear in person to explain,” the Bench said, while directing the Union Government to file a compliance affidavit within two weeks. The matter was posted for further hearing after four weeks.

The proceedings arose from a contempt petition alleging that the Union Government had failed to implement the Madhya Pradesh High Court’s December 9, 2024 order directing that the award be conferred on Mr. Chouhan within one month. The direction was subsequently affirmed by a Division Bench and later upheld by the Supreme Court.

The High Court had observed that the Union Government had “overreached” its order by approving the Gallantry Medal, a lower decoration, instead of conferring the President’s Gallantry Award.

Justice Pranay Verma had nevertheless granted the Union one final opportunity to comply with the earlier direction, warning that if it failed to do so before the next hearing, the Home Secretary “shall automatically be deemed to be held in contempt”, following which further proceedings would be initiated.

Mr. Chouhan, who was serving as the Station House Officer of Ghatigaon police station in Gwalior district in 2003, had led an operation against a gang of dacoits after receiving intelligence about their presence in a village. Two dacoits were killed in the encounter, during which Mr. Chouhan himself sustained injuries. Following a magisterial inquiry that gave him a clean chit, recommendations were made for his out-of-turn promotion and for the conferment of the President’s Police Medal for Gallantry.

World.title: Five arrested in Guntur for murders linked to missing person cases
World.content:
Tadikonda police arrested five persons for murder allegedly committed in connection with a robbery linked to a missing person case. During interrogation, the accused also allegedly confessed to their involvement in another murder linked to a separate missing person case, police said on Monday.

According to Guntur Superintendent of Police (SP) Vakul Jindal, the investigation was conducted using scientific and technical evidence. Police said that the prime accused, Devarakonda Nageswara Rao alias Omkar, along with Gujjarlapudi Samuel alias Simon, Kanaparthi Manikanta, Gattamaneni Pushpa and Devalla Padmala, allegedly conspired to rob real estate businessman Madugula Sankara Rao of Phanidharam village after learning about his financial status.

The accused allegedly lured the victim under the pretext of purchasing land at Yadlapadu, procured SIM cards from other States, hired a car and purchased ropes and binding wire in advance. On July 7, they allegedly strangled Sankara Rao near Vankayalapadu village, robbed him of four gold rings, a gold chain and ₹72,000 in cash, and dumped his body in a quarry pit near Pothuru after tying it to a cement fencing pole. They later used the victim's mobile phone to mislead his family before destroying the SIM card.

During interrogation, the accused also allegedly confessed to another murder involving Nagaraju of Vengalayapalem. Police said Omkar, Bannu and Manikanta reportedly admitted to taking Nagaraju in a car, killing him en route and disposing of his body in the Sagar Right Canal near Macherla.

Following a complaint from Nagaraju's parents, police had earlier registered a missing person case at the Nallapadu police station. Police said that further investigation into both the cases was in progress after the seizure of the car, mobile phones, cash and other incriminating material.

World.title: Russia-Ukraine war: 4 Indian sailors among 10 killed as missile hits ship
World.content:
In the first deaths of Indian seafarers in the Russia-Ukraine war, four Indians were among 10 killed in a Russian missile strike on a merchant vessel departing Ukraine’s southern port of Odesa on Sunday.

India was quick to condemn the attack, without directly blaming Russia.

According to the Ukrainian Air Force, Russian forces launched three Kh-59/Kh-69 cruise missiles during the attack. One missile struck the starboard side of the Golden Leo, a Turkish-owned merchant vessel sailing under the flag of Guinea-Bissau, igniting a fire.



“On the evening of 19 July 2026, the vessel MV Golden Leo was attacked while departing the port of Odesa. At the time of the incident, there were 17 crew members on board, including five Indian nationals,” the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement.

World.title: Sohail Khan says he feels ‘lovely’ meeting ex-wife Seema Sajdeh; expert on healthy healing
World.content:
Sohail Khan, who met ex-wife Seema Sajdeh on the reality show Alliance recently, shared that it is always “lovely” to see her. “Lovely. I have lived with this beautiful lady for 25 years, and let me admit on national television if there has been any mistake between us, I take the ownership….that responsibility,” he said in a promo of the reality show in response to host Kunal Kemmu’s question.

In a world where separations often become public blame games and social media encourages people to choose sides, his response offered something far more powerful: dignity, reflected psychotherapist and life coach Delnna Rrajesh.

“One of the biggest misconceptions surrounding divorce is that if a marriage ends, the entire relationship was a failure. Human relationships are rarely that black and white. Two people can genuinely love each other, build a beautiful life together, raise children, create memories, support each other’s dreams, and still reach a point where continuing together is no longer the healthiest path. The end of a marriage does not erase the value of the years that came before it. A relationship can end while still having been meaningful,” described Delnna.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

Relationships, even painful ones, often become our greatest teachers. “They reveal our attachment patterns, communication styles, emotional wounds, childhood conditioning, unmet needs and the areas where we still need to grow,” shared Delnna.

Every relationship has two individual stories, one shared story, countless circumstances, and many variables that cannot always be reduced to one person being right and the other being wrong. “Unfortunately, after divorce, many people remain psychologically married long after they are legally separated. They continue replaying old arguments, seeking validation, proving their innocence, waiting for apologies or carrying resentment that quietly shapes every future relationship. The marriage may have ended, but emotionally, they are still living inside it,” reflected Delnna.

Healing post divorce is essential (Photo: Freepik) Healing post divorce is essential (Photo: Freepik)

This is why dignity after separation is not simply kindness. “It is emotional leadership. Every conversation, every social media post, every interaction with an ex-partner is quietly teaching children how adults handle disappointment, heartbreak and conflict,” said Delnna.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by prime video IN (@primevideoin)

What does healthy post-divorce healing actually look like?

*Allow yourself to grieve without judging the pace of your healing.

*Separate your identity from your marital status. You are more than someone’s former spouse.

*Avoid making your ex-partner the centre of every conversation. The more attention you give the past, the less energy remains for your future.

*sIf children are involved, remember that they deserve to love both parents without feeling guilty.

*Build a life that is not merely free from pain but full of purpose. Reconnect with hobbies, friendships, health, learning, spirituality and personal growth.

*Seek professional support if anger, guilt, shame or resentment continues to dominate your emotional world. Therapy is not only for crisis. It is also a space to rebuild confidence, self-worth and emotional resilience.

*Before entering another relationship, spend time understanding the patterns you wish to leave behind and the qualities you want to carry forward.

World.title: Residents throng PCMC, demand Moshi garbage depot’s shift
World.content:
Days after a waste-to-energy plant building collapsed inside the Moshi garbage depot, aggrieved residents from the area on Monday thronged the civic headquarters in Pimpri seeking redressal to their litany of grievances.

Residents demanded that the compensation amount for families of victims increased substantially and the garbage depot shifted out of the locality. Nine contract employees were killed when the building collapsed on July 8.

A delegation of Moshi residents led by former corporator Dhananjay Alhat met Municipal Commissioner Vijay Suryavanshi and Mayor Ravi Landge went to PCMC headquarters in Pimpri and held discussions over their grievances.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Alhat said, “We have demanded the Moshi garbage should be shifted away from the suburb. If they can’t shift the depot in the immediate future, they should drastically reduce the amount of waste which has been lying in the spot for years.”

Alhat said, “Moshi is growing rapidly, tall residential buildings and commercial complex have come up in the suburb. It is one of the most sought after places to live in Pimpri-Chinchwad. The way it is being treated by PCMC is condemnable. Residents are shocked by the sight of a towering mountain of garbage which breeds nothing but diseases and is causing harming to environment.”



Alhat said they also demanded compensation to victims and their kin should be increased to Rs 50 lakh and the private company, Antony Renewable Energy, should pay Rs one crore. “This is because the deaths did not occur because of a natural calamity. It happened because of negligence of PCMC and the company,” he said.

Also Read | Project head arrested, safety officer booked in Pune building collapse case

Nitin Borate, a local activist who was part of the delegation said, “We demanded the garbage being brought to Moshi depot from all over Pune be stopped. The legacy waste piling up should be immediately reduced. And the capacity of the private firm to convert waste to energy should be stepped up.”



“If the PCMC is not in a position to shift the garbage depot for now, they should at least ensure only garbage from Bhosari assembly area is dumped in Moshi garbage depot,” Borate said.

Alhat and Borate said the PCMC administration has sought three months’ time to redress their grievances. “If the PCMC does not live up to its promise, the residents of Moshi will be forced to launch an agitation against the Moshi garbage depot,” the said.

The delegation demanded strict legal action be taken against officers concerned, machinery, and company responsible for the accident.

The delegation said the entire cost of treatment for injured citizens should be borne by the PCMC and the government as well as necessary action be taken to provide a job in government/municipal service to one eligible member of the affected family.



“Long-term measures should be implemented to address issues related to health, environment, and safety in the area. All pending civic amenity-related issues raised by the villagers should be resolved on a priority basis,” the delegation said in its memorandum submitted to the PCMC.

On its part, the PCMC administration said, “During (Monday)’s meeting, the residents of Moshi presented a detailed review of the situation post the accident. They clearly expressed their sentiments and demands regarding justice for the families of the deceased, strict action against the culprits, assurance of citizen safety in the area, health and environmental adverse effects caused by the garbage depot, and long-pending local issues.”

The administration said residents elaborately presented each demand, noting that the incident was not limited to one concern, but was a matter of utmost gravity concerning citizens’ safety, the environment, and trust in the administration. “They clarified that there will be no compromise on the rightful demands of the people of Moshi, and the administration needs to treat this with top priority,” officials said.



The PCMC chief said issues raised by the Moshi residents will be resolved phase-wise and on priority. He also stated that the administration will not delay the case related to the accident and all necessary administrative actions will be carried out expeditiously.

Mayor Ravi Landge said, “Ensuring justice for the families who lost their lives in the accident, taking strict action against the culprits, and resolving every rightful issue of the Moshi residents is my moral and public responsibility. My follow-up will continue persistently until the promises made to the people of Moshi are fulfilled. Nothing is greater than the trust and safety of citizens.”

World.title: PCMC extends SIR drive; BLO house visits until August 8
World.content:
After the Election Commission of India announced a revised schedule for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) programme of electoral rolls in the state, the PCMC too extended the SIR deadline to August 8.

Considering the recent heavy rainfall situation in the state, the Commission took this decision by accepting the request for a deadline extension made by the Chief Electoral Officer, Maharashtra State, civic officials said.



According to the revised schedule, the drive to collect enumeration forms through house visits by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will now be conducted from June 30 to August 8, 2026. The process to rationalise and restructure polling stations will also be completed by August 8.

World.title: ‘He was set to get married, change jobs’: 4 Indians killed in Russian attack on cargo ship off Ukraine coast
World.content:
A 26-year-old seafarer from Kerala is among four Indians killed in a Russian attack on a cargo ship, M V Golden Leo, off the coast of the Ukrainian city of Odesa on July 19.

The deceased has been identified as Akhil Joyan from Vellarikundu village in Kasaragod district. He has been working as a mariner on the ship for the last six years.



According to family sources, Akhil was the only son of Joyan, a merchant, and Saly, a collection agent at the postal department. He joined the shipping industry as a mariner after completing a course in nautical science from Chennai.

World.title: Mumbai Police detain 200 amid student protest over NEET row
World.content:
Written by Purvi Thevar

Heavy police deployment and barricading at Chaityabhoomi in Dadar on Monday failed to stop hundreds of students and activists from gathering to protest against the Centre over the alleged NEET irregularities, with organisers claiming around 200 people were detained by the Mumbai Police.

The protest, organised under the banner of Mumbai Against Suppression of Students (MASS), was held in solidarity with demonstrations in Delhi led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and activist Sonam Wangchuk. Protesters have been demanding accountability over the alleged irregularities in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.



Police blocked access to the protest site by erecting barricades on roads leading to Chaityabhoomi. Those attempting to reach the venue were detained and taken away in police vehicles, forcing demonstrators to stage multiple small protests in nearby areas.

Several protesters gathered at Chaityabhoomi in Dadar in support of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest were detained by Mumbai Police on Monday. (Express Photo By Ganesh Shirsekar) Several protesters gathered at Chaityabhoomi in Dadar in support of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest were detained by Mumbai Police on Monday. (Express Photo By Ganesh Shirsekar)

Members of several student organisations, including the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), All India Students’ Federation (AISF), Aamchi Padhai Aamchi Ladai and other youth groups, participated in the demonstration carrying placards and raising slogans against the Centre.

According to MASS, more than 500 people turned up for the protest, but police action prevented them from assembling at a single location.



“There was an overwhelming response, but participants were stopped from reaching the venue. They held demonstrations wherever they found space before being detained. Protesters were taken to Sion, Dadar, Mahim and Worli police stations,” an organiser said.

(Express Photo By Ganesh Shirsekar) (Express Photo By Ganesh Shirsekar)

Among those protesting was Nupur Haridas, a 23-year-old fourth year medical student who has appeared for the NEET examination twice.

“The education minister should have a spine and resign,” she said, adding that one of her friends was detained during the protest.

Jenisha Solanki, a 23-year-old accountancy and finance student, said the controversy had discouraged her younger sister, who is preparing for Class 12, from considering medicine as a career. “It is frustrating for students. We are demanding justice, but no one seems to care,” she said.



Heavy police deployment at protest in Mumbai’s Chaityabhoomi in Dadar. (Express Photo By Ganesh Shirsekar) Heavy police deployment at protest in Mumbai’s Chaityabhoomi in Dadar. (Express Photo By Ganesh Shirsekar)

Anju Kothari, 55, who attended the protest with her daughter, said another daughter was participating in the demonstration in Delhi.

“We could not travel to Delhi, so we joined the protest in Mumbai. The government cannot escape accountability,” she said.

School students also joined the demonstration with their parents. Fifteen-year-old CBSE student Navya Shamanthul said, “It is our right to protest, and we are fighting for it.”

The organisers also alleged that several activists and youth leaders were detained even before the protest began.



Shailendra Kamble, Mumbai district secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), alleged that police teams visited the residences of several Opposition leaders and activists, including CPI Mumbai secretary Milind Ranade and Progressive Students’ Organisation president advocate Samya Korde, in an attempt to prevent them from participating.

“Police teams have been visiting the homes of leading activists and attempting to detain them in an effort to suppress a democratic protest,” Kamble alleged.

No permission was granted for holding any protest at Chaityabhoomi. Accordingly, permission for today’s protest by supporters of the Shetkari Kamgar Paksha, CPI(M), and CJP supporters at Chaityabhoomi was denied by Shivaji Park Police Station.

“Process of FIR registration against the protesters who participated in the protest today is currently underway at Shivaji Park Police Station,” said Mahendra Pandit,

DCP Central Zone 3.

The reporter is an intern with The Indian Express.

World.title: High Court orders arrest of Delhi Capitals cricketer Abishek Porel in ‘rape’ case
World.content:
The Calcutta High Court recently ordered the Mogra police to arrest Delhi Capitals cricketer Abishek Porel and seize his electronic devices to prevent dissemination of photographs of the woman who has accused him of rape. The cricketer has also been charged with criminal intimidation and other offences.

Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya, in an order passed on July 14, directed the police to continue their efforts to trace and arrest him.



“It is disclosed in the communication dated 6th July, 2026 that one pen drive/storage device is seized from the petitioner…and it is believed that certain materials are stored therein… It appears that accused persons…are required to be apprehended for seizure of electronic devices lying with them so that data stored therein cannot be shared with others… Communication dated 6th July, 2026 discloses steps taken by the concerned police authorities for apprehending…[the accused] but fact remains…[they] are yet to be apprehended. Concerned police authorities are directed to continue with their endeavour to apprehend respondent nos.6 & 7 [accused] and to make seizure of devices so obnoxious data stored therein shall not be further disseminated,” the order said.

World.title: Magisterial probe ordered into killing of youth in J&K’s Doda
World.content:
The Jammu & Kashmir administration on Monday ordered a magisterial inquiry into the death of a local youth in alleged police firing in Bhaderwah’s Jai area last week.

The order, issued by Doda District Magistrate Krishan Lal, comes two days after police set up a Special Investigation Team (SIT). Police have registered an “open” FIR against unknown persons for attempted murder, voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to a public servant to deter them from discharging duty, assault on a public servant, theft and other offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.



According to police, 30-year-old auto driver Arif Hussain from Cheeka village in Doda was fatally shot during a scuffle between police personnel and alleged cattle smugglers in the picturesque Jai Valley near Bhaderwah in Doda district last Thursday night.

World.title: Iran’s Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni arrives in Pakistan
World.content:
Iran’s Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni on Monday night arrived in Islamabad on an official visit.

Upon his arrival in Pakistan, the senior Iranian official was received by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi.

The visiting dignitary is accompanied by a high-level delegation.

During his visit, Momeni will meet Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, reported state-run Pakistan TV.

Earlier reports had suggested that Momeni was likely to engage with Pakistani officials who previously mediated a now-collapsed interim ceasefire between the US and Iran.

Momeni’s visit comes as mediator Pakistan continues its diplomatic efforts to rescue the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed last month between the US and Iran.

In the ninth consecutive night of attacks on Monday, Washington expanded its strikes across Iran, including a city hosting a nuclear power plant.

Iran kept up its own attacks across the region in response, with its Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) announcing they had hit targets in Bahrain, Jordan and Syria, while Bahrain said Tehran had targeted its air navigation systems.

After US President Donald Trump’s remarks earlier this month that the ceasefire was “over”, his Iranian counterpart Masoud Pezeshkian also said on Monday that they were fighting a “full-scale war”. Tehran has blamed Washington for breaching the MoU.

Despite the latest attacks, Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said diplomatic exchanges with the US via mediators were ongoing.

The Middle East war resumed after a weeks-long lull prompted by an agreement signed in June, and oil prices surged to a one-month high as the foes battled to control the vital Strait of Hormuz.

As its truce with the US collapsed, Tehran reimposed its blockade of the waterway, while Washington hit back by again blockading Iran’s ports.

Pakistan has been leading the peace efforts since the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran on February 28, setting off a war and global fuel crisis as Tehran took measures to disrupt traffic in the Strait of Hormuz — a vital maritime corridor for the supply of oil and gas.

World.title: Andy Burnham becomes UK PM, says Britain needs to 'regain stability'
World.content:
Britain’s King Charles III on Monday appointed Andy Burnham as prime minister after outgoing Keir Starmer officially tendered his resignation, the palace said.

“Andrew Burnham MP accepted The King’s offer and kissed hands upon his appointment as Prime Minister,” Buckingham Palace said in a statement, adding the king had asked him to form the next government.

Burnham became Britain’s sixth prime minister to move into Downing Street in 10 years, with an in-tray overflowing with challenges and little time to make his mark.

BBC reported that a large crowd of supporters erupted into applause as Burnham stepped onto Downing Street for his first speech.

Delivering his address, Burnham promised to set out new measures to help with the cost of living this week before setting out a new 10-year plan for the country later this year.

“Britain needs to show the world that we can regain our stability once again,” Burnham said.

“We have not been good enough, and we need to be better.”

Promising Britons “some breathing space now”, he said the government would set out some measures to tackle the high cost-of-living, and how it plans to fund them.

Further out, he said: “We will help more young people into work by changing the education system and giving them more support, more mental health support, and we will build more council homes.

“That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules, and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

The new leader takes over from the unpopular Keir Starmer just two years after the outgoing prime minister led the Labour Party to power in a landslide election victory after 14 years of Conservative rule.

Burnham said his first calls would include US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, adding that Britain’s support for Ukraine would remain unchanged under his leadership.

In a clip recorded before he was officially appointed as British leader but released after his speech in Downing Street, Burnham was asked who he would contact first and whether that would be Trump, Zelenskiy or another world leader.

He replied by saying those two would be among his first calls.

He said he would make clear to Zelensky that there would be “no change” in Britain’s backing for Ukraine and that he would support the Ukrainian leader “100 per cent” as his predecessor had done.

“President Zelensky will be left in no doubt whatsoever that Britain’s support is steadfast, it is resolute. It will be there for him, and I will be there for him personally too,” Burnham told reporters.

Finance minister Rachel Reeves quits

Britain’s finance minister Rachel Reeves left the government after Andy Burnham became prime minister.

“I wish the very best of luck to my successor, Andy and his cabinet. You have my full support, and I will continue to play my part in helping this Labour government deliver the change the country needs,” she said on X.

An announcement on Burnham’s senior cabinet appointments was also expected on Monday, with all eyes on who will replace Rachel Reeves as finance minister.

The former mayor of Greater Manchester, nicknamed the “King of the North”, has been parachuted in by the Labour Party after Starmer resigned last month, with MPs viewing him as the party’s best chance of reining in Nigel Farage’s anti-immigration Reform UK party.

Starmer departed Downing Street on Monday morning, insisting in a farewell speech that his two years in office had made Britain a better place.

“I am confident that Britain is now stronger and fairer than it was two years ago,” Starmer told reporters outside his central London office.

“I go with good grace, I go with a smile, and I go proud of everything that we have achieved,” he added.

Congratulations pour in

As soon as Buckingham Palace’s statement came in, leaders from across the world began extending their best wishes for the new UK PM.

In a statement, President Asif Ali Zardari expressed the hope that under Burnham’s leadership, Pakistan and the UK would further strengthen their longstanding bilateral partnership and expand cooperation across areas of mutual interest.

President Zardari reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to dialogue, diplomacy and the peaceful resolution of disputes.

He noted that, as the world, particularly the Gulf region, has been passing through a turbulent period since late February, Pakistan has “played its part in promoting peace with the support of many brotherly countries”.

He expressed the hope that the UK, under Burnham’s leadership, would also play its part in securing a cessation of the current hostilities between the United States and Iran and a return to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.

The president wished Burnham success in his new responsibilities and said that he looked forward to working together to further deepen the enduring ties between Pakistan and the UK.

In a post on X, PM Shehbaz Sharif conveyed his “heartiest congratulations” and wished him “every success in his tenure”.

He said he looked forward to working closely with Burnham to “further strengthen the historic and deep-rooted bonds of friendship and cooperation between Pakistan and the UK”.

“These special ties are anchored by millions of proud and vibrant British Pakistanis who serve as a living bridge between our two countries,” the prime minister noted.

“Together, we will strive to elevate Pakistan–UK relations, in particular, our bilateral trade and investment partnership, to new heights,” PM Shehbaz affirmed.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she looked forward to working with Burnham to strengthen the partnership between the European Union (EU) and the UK.

“For the security of our shared continent. And the prosperity of people on both sides of the Channel,” she wrote on X.

EU chief Antonio Costa said he hopes to press on with efforts to improve ties between Brussels and London.

“In the last two years EU-UK relations gained a new, positive momentum,” European Council president Costa posted online.

“I look forward to continuing to further deepen our cooperation for the benefit of our citizens and businesses. The United Kingdom and the European Union are stronger together,” he added.

Ukraine’s Zelensky also felicitated Burnham, wishing him and the British people “every success in addressing the challenges of today”.

“Britain has always been one of the global leaders. We are ready to work together in all possible formats. We highly appreciate the UK’s political, defence, and values-based support,” he wrote on X.

“The foundation of our bilateral relationship is stronger than ever, and we will continue to make each other stronger. I’m looking forward to our conversation later today. Thank you!”
